129.s:
brahmovāca
indratīrtham iti khyātaṃ tatraiva ca vṛṣākapam
phenāyāḥ saṃgamo yatra hanūmataṃ tathaiva ca //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इन्द्रतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं तत्रैव च वृषाकपम्
फेनायाः संगमो यत्र हनूमतं तथैव च ॥
129.m: Brahmā said: / Known as Indratīrtha, and right there Vṛṣākapa, / where there is the confluence of the Phenā, and likewise Hanūmata,

129.s:
abjakaṃ cāpi yat proktaṃ yatra devas trivikramaḥ
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca punarāvṛttidurlabham //
129.d:
अब्जकं चापि यत् प्रोक्तं यत्र देवस् त्रिविक्रमः
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥
129.m: and that which is called Abjaka, where the god Trivikrama resides; / bathing and giving gifts there makes return [to rebirth] rare.

129.s:
tatra vṛttāny athākhyāsye gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe
indreśvaraṃ cottare ca śṛṇu bhaktyā yatavrataḥ //
129.d:
तत्र वृत्तान्य् अथाख्यास्ये गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तटे
इन्द्रेश्वरं चोत्तरे च शृणु भक्त्या यतव्रतः ॥
129.m: Now I shall relate the events there on the south bank of the Gaṅgā, / and Indreśvara on the north; listen with devotion, restrained in vows.

129.s:
namucir balavān āsīd indraśatrur madotkaṭaḥ
tasyendreṇābhavad yuddhaṃ phenenendro 'harac chiraḥ //
129.d:
नमुचिर् बलवान् आसीद् इन्द्रशत्रुर् मदोत्कटः
तस्येन्द्रेणाभवद् युद्धं फेनेनेन्द्रो ऽहरच् छिरः ॥
129.m: Namuci was powerful, an enemy of Indra, arrogant with pride; / a battle took place between him and Indra; with foam Indra took off his head.

129.s:
apāṃ ca namuceḥ śatros tatphenavajrarūpadhṛk
śiraś chittvā tac ca phenaṃ gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe //
129.d:
अपां च नमुचेः शत्रोस् तत्फेनवज्ररूपधृक्
शिरश् छित्त्वा तच् च फेनं गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तटे ॥
129.m: And taking the form of a thunderbolt of foam, the enemy of Namuci [struck] with waters; / having severed his head, that foam, on the south bank of the Gaṅgā,

129.s:
nyapatad bhūmiṃ bhittvā tu rasātalam athāviśat
rasātalabhavaṃ gāṅgaṃ vāri yad viśvapāvanam //
129.d:
न्यपतद् भूमिं भित्त्वा तु रसातलम् अथाविशत्
रसातलभवं गाङ्गं वारि यद् विश्वपावनम् ॥
129.m: fell, and having pierced the earth, it entered the netherworld. / The water of the Gaṅgā arising from the netherworld, which purifies the universe,

129.s:
vajrādiṣṭena mārgeṇa vyagamad bhūmimaṇḍalam
taj jalaṃ phenanāmnā tu nadī pheneti gadyate //
129.d:
वज्रादिष्टेन मार्गेण व्यगमद् भूमिमण्डलम्
तज् जलं फेननाम्ना तु नदी फेनेति गद्यते ॥
129.m: went out to the earthly sphere by the path indicated by the thunderbolt. / That water, by the name of Phenā, is spoken of as the river Phenā.

129.s:
tasyās tu saṃgamaḥ puṇyo gaṅgayā lokaviśrutaḥ
sarvapāpakṣayakaro gaṅgāyamunayor iva //
129.d:
तस्यास् तु संगमः पुण्यो गङ्गया लोकविश्रुतः
सर्वपापक्षयकरो गङ्गायमुनयोर् इव ॥
129.m: Its confluence with the Gaṅgā is holy, renowned in the world, / destroying all sins, like that of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

129.s:
hanūmadupamātā vai yatrāplavanamātrataḥ
mārjāratvād abhūn muktā viṣṇugaṅgāprasādataḥ //
129.d:
हनूमदुपमाता वै यत्राप्लवनमात्रतः
मार्जारत्वाद् अभून् मुक्ता विष्णुगङ्गाप्रसादतः ॥
129.m: Where, merely by bathing, the foster-mother of Hanūmat / was freed from cat-nature by the grace of the Viṣṇugaṅgā.

129.s:
mārjāraṃ ceti tat tīrthaṃ purā proktaṃ mayā tava
hanūmataṃ ca tat proktaṃ tatrākhyānaṃ puroditam //
129.d:
मार्जारं चेति तत् तीर्थं पुरा प्रोक्तं मया तव
हनूमतं च तत् प्रोक्तं तत्राख्यानं पुरोदितम् ॥
129.m: That tīrtha named Mārjāra was told to you by me formerly, / and it is called Hanūmata; the narrative there has been told before.

129.s:
vṛṣākapaṃ cābjakaṃ ca tatredaṃ prayataḥ śṛṇu
hiraṇya iti vikhyāto daityānāṃ pūrvajo balī //
129.d:
वृषाकपं चाब्जकं च तत्रेदं प्रयतः शृणु
हिरण्य इति विख्यातो दैत्यानां पूर्वजो बली ॥
129.m: And Vṛṣākapa and Abjaka are there; listen to this with concentration: / Renowned as Hiraṇya, a mighty ancestor of the Daityas,

129.s:
tapas taptvā suraiḥ sarvair ajeyo 'bhūt sudāruṇaḥ
tasyāpi balavān putro devānāṃ durjayaḥ sadā //
129.d:
तपस् तप्त्वा सुरैः सर्वैर् अजेयो ऽभूत् सुदारुणः
तस्यापि बलवान् पुत्रो देवानां दुर्जयः सदा ॥
129.m: having performed austerities, became invincible to all the gods, extremely terrible. / He also had a powerful son, ever unconquerable by the gods,

129.s:
mahāśanir iti khyātas tasya bhāryā parājitā
tenendrasyābhavad yuddhaṃ bahukālaṃ nirantaram //
129.d:
महाशनिर् इति ख्यातस् तस्य भार्या पराजिता
तेनेन्द्रस्याभवद् युद्धं बहुकालं निरन्तरम् ॥
129.m: famed as Mahāśani; his wife was Parājitā. / Between him and Indra there was a battle for a long time, continuously.

129.s:
mahāśanir mahāvīryaḥ satataṃ raṇamūrdhani
jitvā nāgena sahitaṃ śakraṃ pitre nyavedayat //
129.d:
महाशनिर् महावीर्यः सततं रणमूर्धनि
जित्वा नागेन सहितं शक्रं पित्रे न्यवेदयत् ॥
129.m: Mahāśani, endowed with great valour, constantly at the vanguard of battle, / having conquered Śakra along with his elephant, presented him to his father.

129.s:
baddhvā hastisamāyuktaṃ svasāraṃ vīkṣya tāṃ tadā
vihāya krūratāṃ daityo hiraṇyāya nyavedayat //
129.d:
बद्ध्वा हस्तिसमायुक्तं स्वसारं वीक्ष्य तां तदा
विहाय क्रूरतां दैत्यो हिरण्याय न्यवेदयत् ॥
129.m: Having bound [him] along with his elephant, seeing his sister at that time, / abandoning cruelty, the Daitya presented [him] to Hiraṇya.

129.s:
mahāśanipitā daityaḥ pūrveṣāṃ pūrvavattaraḥ
śacīkāntaṃ tale sthāpya tasya rakṣām athākarot //
129.d:
महाशनिपिता दैत्यः पूर्वेषां पूर्ववत्तरः
शचीकान्तं तले स्थाप्य तस्य रक्षाम् अथाकरोत् ॥
129.m: The father of Mahāśani, the Daitya, foremost among ancestors, / having placed Śacī's beloved in the netherworld, then guarded him.

129.s:
mahāśanir hariṃ jitvā jetuṃ varuṇam abhyagāt
varuṇo 'pi mahābuddhiḥ prādāt kanyāṃ mahāśaneḥ //
129.d:
महाशनिर् हरिं जित्वा जेतुं वरुणम् अभ्यगात्
वरुणो ऽपि महाबुद्धिः प्रादात् कन्यां महाशनेः ॥
129.m: Having conquered Hari [Indra], Mahāśani went to conquer Varuṇa. / Varuṇa too, of great intellect, gave his daughter to Mahāśani.

129.s:
udadhiṃ svālayaṃ prādād varuṇas tu mahāśaneḥ
tayoś ca sakhyam abhavad varuṇasya mahāśaneḥ //
129.d:
उदधिं स्वालयं प्रादाद् वरुणस् तु महाशनेः
तयोश् च सख्यम् अभवद् वरुणस्य महाशनेः ॥
129.m: Varuṇa gave the ocean, his own abode, to Mahāśani, / and friendship was established between the two, Varuṇa and Mahāśani.

129.s:
vāruṇī cāpi yā kanyā sā priyābhūn mahāśaneḥ
vīryeṇa yaśasā cāpi śauryeṇa ca balena ca //
129.d:
वारुणी चापि या कन्या सा प्रियाभून् महाशनेः
वीर्येण यशसा चापि शौर्येण च बलेन च ॥
129.m: And that daughter, Vāruṇī, became dear to Mahāśani. / In valour, in fame, in bravery, and in strength,

129.s:
mahāśanir mahādaityas trailokye nopamīyate
nirindratvaṃ gate loke devāḥ sarve nyamantrayan //
129.d:
महाशनिर् महादैत्यस् त्रैलोक्ये नोपमीयते
निरिन्द्रत्वं गते लोके देवाः सर्वे न्यमन्त्रयन् ॥
129.m: Mahāśani, the great Daitya, was unequalled in the three worlds. / When the world became devoid of Indra, all the gods deliberated:

129.s:
devā ūcuḥ
viṣṇur evendradātā syād daityahantā sa eva ca
mantradṛg vā sa eva syād indraṃ cānyaṃ kariṣyati //
129.d:
देवा ऊचुः
विष्णुर् एवेन्द्रदाता स्याद् दैत्यहन्ता स एव च
मन्त्रदृग् वा स एव स्याद् इन्द्रं चान्यं करिष्यति ॥
129.m: The gods said: / Viṣṇu alone must be the bestower of Indra; he alone is the slayer of Daityas, / or he alone sees the plan and will make another Indra.

129.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ saṃmantrya te devā viṣṇor mantraṃ nyavedayan
mamāvadhyo mahādaityo mahāśanir iti bruvan //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं संमन्त्र्य ते देवा विष्णोर् मन्त्रं न्यवेदयन्
ममावध्यो महादैत्यो महाशनिर् इति ब्रुवन् ॥
129.m: Brahmā said: / Having thus conferred, those gods revealed their counsel to Viṣṇu. / Saying, "The great Daitya Mahāśani cannot be killed by me,"

129.s:
prāyād vārīśvaraṃ viṣṇuḥ śvaśuraṃ varuṇaṃ tadā
keśavo varuṇaṃ gatvā prāhendrasya parābhavam //
129.d:
प्रायाद् वारीश्वरं विष्णुः श्वशुरं वरुणं तदा
केशवो वरुणं गत्वा प्राहेन्द्रस्य पराभवम् ॥
129.m: Viṣṇu went then to Varuṇa, the lord of waters, his father-in-law. / Keśava, having gone to Varuṇa, spoke of Indra's defeat:

129.s:
tathā tvayaitat kartavyaṃ yathāyāti puraṃdaraḥ
tadviṣṇuvacanāc chīghraṃ yayau jalapatir mune //
129.d:
तथा त्वयैतत् कर्तव्यं यथायाति पुरंदरः
तद्विष्णुवचनाच् छीघ्रं ययौ जलपतिर् मुने ॥
129.m: "This must be done by you in such a way that Puraṃdara returns." / At that word of Viṣṇu, O sage, the lord of waters quickly went

129.s:
sutāpatiṃ hiraṇyasutaṃ vikrāntaṃ taṃ mahāśanim
atisaṃmānitas tena jāmātrā varuṇaḥ prabhuḥ //
129.d:
सुतापतिं हिरण्यसुतं विक्रान्तं तं महाशनिम्
अतिसंमानितस् तेन जामात्रा वरुणः प्रभुः ॥
129.m: to his daughter's husband, the son of Hiraṇya, that valiant Mahāśani. / Highly honoured by that son-in-law, Lord Varuṇa

129.s:
papracchāgamanaṃ daityo vinayāc chvaśuraṃ tadā
varuṇaḥ prāha taṃ daityaṃ yad āgamanakāraṇam //
129.d:
पप्रच्छागमनं दैत्यो विनयाच् छ्वशुरं तदा
वरुणः प्राह तं दैत्यं यद् आगमनकारणम् ॥
129.m: was asked by the Daitya with humility then about the purpose of his arrival. / Varuṇa told that Daitya the reason for his arrival.

129.s:
varuṇa uvāca
indraṃ dehi mahābāho yas tvayā nirjitaḥ purā
baddhaṃ rasātalasthaṃ taṃ devānām adhipaṃ sakhe //
129.d:
वरुण उवाच
इन्द्रं देहि महाबाहो यस् त्वया निर्जितः पुरा
बद्धं रसातलस्थं तं देवानाम् अधिपं सखे ॥
129.m: Varuṇa said: / "Give up Indra, O mighty-armed one, who was formerly conquered by you, / bound and staying in the netherworld, that ruler of gods, O friend.

129.s:
asmākaṃ sarvadā mānyaṃ dehi tvaṃ mama śatruhan
baddhvā vimokṣaṇaṃ śatror mahate yaśase satām //
129.d:
अस्माकं सर्वदा मान्यं देहि त्वं मम शत्रुहन्
बद्ध्वा विमोक्षणं शत्रोर् महते यशसे सताम् ॥
129.m: Give him to me, O slayer of enemies, who is always venerable to us; / releasing an enemy after binding him leads to great fame for the virtuous."

129.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā kathaṃcit sa daityeśo varuṇāya tam
prādād indraṃ śacīkāntaṃ vāraṇena samanvitam //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा कथंचित् स दैत्येशो वरुणाय तम्
प्रादाद् इन्द्रं शचीकान्तं वारणेन समन्वितम् ॥
129.m: Brahmā said: / Having said "So be it," that lord of Daityas somehow gave up to Varuṇa / that Indra, beloved of Śacī, together with his elephant.

129.s:
sa daityamadhye 'tivirājamāno
hariṃ tadovāca jaleśasaṃnidhau
saṃpūjya caivātha mahopacārair
mahāśanir maghavantaṃ babhāṣe
129.d:
स दैत्यमध्ये ऽतिविराजमानो
हरिं तदोवाच जलेशसंनिधौ
संपूज्य चैवाथ महोपचारैर्
महाशनिर् मघवन्तं बभाषे
129.m: Shining brilliantly in the midst of the Daityas, / he then spoke to Hari in the presence of the lord of waters; / and having worshipped him with great honours, / Mahāśani addressed Maghavan:

129.s:
mahāśanir uvāca
kena tvam indro 'dya kṛto 'si kena
vīryaṃ tavedṛg bahu bhāṣase ca
tvaṃ saṃgare śatrubhir bādhyase ca
tathāpi cendro bhavasīti citram
129.d:
महाशनिर् उवाच
केन त्वम् इन्द्रो ऽद्य कृतो ऽसि केन
वीर्यं तवेदृग् बहु भाषसे च
त्वं संगरे शत्रुभिर् बाध्यसे च
तथापि चेन्द्रो भवसीति चित्रम्
129.m: Mahāśani said: / "By whom were you made Indra today? By whom? / Such is your valour, yet you boast much! / You are overcome in battle by enemies, / and yet you remain Indra: how wondrous!

129.s:
athāpi baddhā puruṣeṇa kācit
tasyāḥ patis tāṃ mocayatīti yuktam
striyo 'svatantrāḥ puruṣapradhānās
tvaṃ vai pumān bhavitā śakra sādho
129.d:
अथापि बद्धा पुरुषेण काचित्
तस्याः पतिस् तां मोचयतीति युक्तम्
स्त्रियो ऽस्वतन्त्राः पुरुषप्रधानास्
त्वं वै पुमान् भविता शक्र साधो
129.m: Even so, when some female is bound by a man, / it is fitting that her husband releases her; / women are dependent, with men as their head. / Will you truly be a man, O virtuous Śakra?"

129.s:
baddho mayā saṃgare vāhanena
kvāpy astraṃ te vajram uddāmaśakti
cintāratnaṃ nandanaṃ yoṣitas tā
yaśo balaṃ devarājopabhogyam
129.d:
बद्धो मया संगरे वाहनेन
क्वाप्य् अस्त्रं ते वज्रम् उद्दामशक्ति
चिन्तारत्नं नन्दनं योषितस् ता
यशो बलं देवराजोपभोग्यम्
129.m:
You were bound by me in battle together with your mount;
where now is your weapon, the thunderbolt of unbridled power?
The wish-fulfilling gem, the Nandana grove, those women,
fame, strength—all to be enjoyed by the king of the gods—
all indeed is yours. But freed from the lord of waters,
you crave life! Fie upon this [life] of yours!

129.s:
taj jīvanaṃ yat tu yaśonidhānaṃ
sa eva mṛtyur yaśaso yad virodhi
evaṃ jānañ śakra kathaṃ jaleśān
muktiṃ prāpto naiva lajjāṃ bhajethāḥ
129.d:
तज् जीवनं यत् तु यशोनिधानं
स एव मृत्युर् यशसो यद् विरोधि
एवं जानञ् शक्र कथं जलेशान्
मुक्तिं प्राप्तो नैव लज्जां भजेथाः
129.m: That [alone] is life which is a storehouse of fame; / that indeed is death which is opposed to fame. / Knowing this, O Śakra, having obtained release from the lord of waters, / how is it that you feel no shame at all?

129.s:
triviṣṭapasthaḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ san
sarvaiḥ suraiḥ kāntayā vījyamānaḥ
saṃstūyamānaś ca tathāpsarobhir
nūnaṃ lajjā te bibhetīti manye
129.d:
त्रिविष्टपस्थः परिवेष्टितः सन्
सर्वैः सुरैः कान्तया वीज्यमानः
संस्तूयमानश् च तथाप्सरोभिर्
नूनं लज्जा ते बिभेतीति मन्ये
129.m: Dwelling in heaven, surrounded / by all the gods, fanned by your beloved, / and extolled likewise by the apsarases, / surely, I think, shame is afraid of you!

129.s:
tvaṃ vṛtrahā namuceś cāpi hantā
purāṃ bhettā gotrabhid vajrabāhuḥ
evaṃ surās tvāṃ paripūjayantīty
ato jiṣṇo sarvam etat tyajasva
129.d:
त्वं वृत्रहा नमुचेश् चापि हन्ता
पुरां भेत्ता गोत्रभिद् वज्रबाहुः
एवं सुरास् त्वां परिपूजयन्तीत्य्
अतो जिष्णो सर्वम् एतत् त्यजस्व
129.m: “You are the slayer of Vṛtra, the killer of Namuci, / the destroyer of fortresses, the splitter of mountains, having the thunderbolt in your arm”— / thus the gods worship you; / therefore, O Jiṣṇu, abandon all of this!

129.s:
vikāram āpyāpy ahitodbhavaṃ ye
jīvanti lokān anusaṃviśanti
bhavādṛśāṃ duścyavanābjajanmā
kathaṃ na hṛdbhedam avāpa kartā
129.d:
विकारम् आप्याप्य् अहितोद्भवं ये
जीवन्ति लोकान् अनुसंविशन्ति
भवादृशां दुश्च्यवनाब्जजन्मा
कथं न हृद्भेदम् अवाप कर्ता
129.m: Those who, having contracted humiliation born of misfortune, / go on living and enter among people— / for such as you, O Duścyavana, how is it that the lotus-born [Brahmā], / your creator, did not suffer heartbreak?

129.s:
brahmovāca
evam uktvā tu daityeśo varuṇāya mahātmane
prādād indraṃ punaś cedaṃ vacanaṃ tad abhāṣata //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् उक्त्वा तु दैत्येशो वरुणाय महात्मने
प्रादाद् इन्द्रं पुनश् चेदं वचनं तद् अभाषत ॥
129.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, the lord of the daityas handed over Indra / to the noble-minded Varuṇa, and again spoke these words:

129.s:
mahāśanir uvāca
adya prabhṛty asau śiṣya indraḥ syād varuṇo guruḥ
śvaśuro mama yena tvaṃ muktim āpto 'si vāsava //
129.d:
महाशनिर् उवाच
अद्य प्रभृत्य् असौ शिष्य इन्द्रः स्याद् वरुणो गुरुः
श्वशुरो मम येन त्वं मुक्तिम् आप्तो ऽसि वासव ॥
129.m: Mahāśani said: / “From this day forth let this Indra be a pupil and Varuṇa his teacher, / my father-in-law, through whom you have obtained release, O Vāsava!

129.s:
tathā tvaṃ bhṛtyabhāvena vartethā varuṇaṃ prati
no ced baddhvā punas tvāṃ vai kṣepsye caiva rasātalam //
129.d:
तथा त्वं भृत्यभावेन वर्तेथा वरुणं प्रति
नो चेद् बद्ध्वा पुनस् त्वां वै क्षेप्स्ये चैव रसातलम् ॥
129.m: Thus you should behave with the attitude of a servant toward Varuṇa; / otherwise, having bound you once again, I shall indeed cast you down into the netherworld!”

129.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ nirbhartsya taṃ śakraṃ hasaṃś cāpi punaḥ punaḥ
abravīd gaccha gaccheti varuṇaṃ cānumanya tu //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं निर्भर्त्स्य तं शक्रं हसंश् चापि पुनः पुनः
अब्रवीद् गच्छ गच्छेति वरुणं चानुमन्य तु ॥
129.m: Brahmā said: / Having thus rebuked Śakra, laughing again and again, / he permitted Varuṇa [to go] and said, “Go, go!”

129.s:
sa tu prāptaḥ svanilayaṃ lajjayā kaluṣīkṛtaḥ
paulomyāṃ prāha tat sarvaṃ yat tac chatruparābhavam //
129.d:
स तु प्राप्तः स्वनिलयं लज्जया कलुषीकृतः
पौलोम्यां प्राह तत् सर्वं यत् तच् छत्रुपराभवम् ॥
129.m: He, however, reached his own abode, defiled by shame, / and told Paulomī all of that—that defeat by his enemy.

129.s:
indra uvāca
evam uktaḥ kṛtaś caiva śatruṇāhaṃ varānane
nirvāpayāmi yena svam ātmānaṃ subhage vada //
129.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
एवम् उक्तः कृतश् चैव शत्रुणाहं वरानने
निर्वापयामि येन स्वम् आत्मानं सुभगे वद ॥
129.m: Indra said: / “Thus was I addressed and treated by the enemy, O fair-faced one! / Tell me, O fortunate lady, how I may extinguish [this torment of] my soul.”

129.s:
indrāṇy uvāca
dānavānām athodbhūtiṃ śakra māyāṃ parābhavam
varadānaṃ tathā mṛtyuṃ jāne 'haṃ balasūdana //
129.d:
इन्द्राण्य् उवाच
दानवानाम् अथोद्भूतिं शक्र मायां पराभवम्
वरदानं तथा मृत्युं जाने ऽहं बलसूदन ॥
129.m: Indrāṇī said: / “I know the origin of the dānavas, O Śakra, their illusory power, their defeat, / the granting of their boons, and likewise their death, O crusher of Bala.

129.s:
tasmād yasmāt tasya mṛtyur athavāpi parābhavaḥ
jāyeta śṛṇu tat sarvaṃ vakṣye 'haṃ prītaye tava //
129.d:
तस्माद् यस्मात् तस्य मृत्युर् अथवापि पराभवः
जायेत शृणु तत् सर्वं वक्ष्ये ऽहं प्रीतये तव ॥
129.m: Therefore, hear all that from which his death / or defeat may arise; I shall speak it for your satisfaction.

129.s:
hiraṇyasya suto vīraḥ pitṛvyasya suto balī
tasmān mama syāt sa bhrātā varadānāc ca darpitaḥ //
129.d:
हिरण्यस्य सुतो वीरः पितृव्यस्य सुतो बली
तस्मान् मम स्यात् स भ्राता वरदानाच् च दर्पितः ॥
129.m: He is the valiant son of Hiraṇya, the mighty son of my paternal uncle; / therefore he is my brother, and he is arrogant on account of the boon granted to him.

129.s:
brahmāṇaṃ toṣayām āsa tapasā niyamena ca
īdṛśaṃ balam āpannaṃ tapasā kiṃ na sidhyati //
129.d:
ब्रह्माणं तोषयाम् आस तपसा नियमेन च
ईदृशं बलम् आपन्नं तपसा किं न सिध्यति ॥
129.m: He propitiated Brahmā with austerity and restraint, / and attained such strength; what is not achieved through austerity?

129.s:
tasmāt tvayā cittarāgo vismayo vā kathaṃcana
na kāryaḥ śṛṇu tatredaṃ kāryaṃ yat tu kramāgatam //
129.d:
तस्मात् त्वया चित्तरागो विस्मयो वा कथंचन
न कार्यः शृणु तत्रेदं कार्यं यत् तु क्रमागतम् ॥
129.m: Therefore you should not entertain any agitation of the mind / or astonishment at all. Listen to what must be done here, which has come down in due order.”

129.s:
brahmovāca
evam uktvā tu paulomī prāhendraṃ vinayānvitā //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् उक्त्वा तु पौलोमी प्राहेन्द्रं विनयान्विता ॥
129.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, Paulomī, endowed with modesty, spoke to Indra:

129.s:
indrāṇy uvāca
nāsādhyam asti tapaso nāsādhyaṃ yajñakarmaṇaḥ
nāsādhyaṃ lokanāthasya viṣṇor bhaktyā harasya ca //
129.d:
इन्द्राण्य् उवाच
नासाध्यम् अस्ति तपसो नासाध्यं यज्ञकर्मणः
नासाध्यं लोकनाथस्य विष्णोर् भक्त्या हरस्य च ॥
129.m: Indrāṇī said: / “There is nothing unattainable through austerity; there is nothing unattainable through the rites of sacrifice; / there is nothing unattainable through devotion to the lord of the world, Viṣṇu, and to Hara.

129.s:
punaś cedaṃ mayā kānta śrutam asty atiśobhanam
strīṇāṃ svabhāvaṃ jānanti striya eva surādhipa //
129.d:
पुनश् चेदं मया कान्त श्रुतम् अस्त्य् अतिशोभनम्
स्त्रीणां स्वभावं जानन्ति स्त्रिय एव सुराधिप ॥
129.m: Moreover, O beloved, this very auspicious [truth] has been heard by me: / only women understand the nature of women, O ruler of the gods.

129.s:
tasmād bhūmes tathā cāpāṃ nāsādhyaṃ vidyate prabho
tapo vā yajñakarmādi tābhyām eva yato bhavet //
129.d:
तस्माद् भूमेस् तथा चापां नासाध्यं विद्यते प्रभो
तपो वा यज्ञकर्मादि ताभ्याम् एव यतो भवेत् ॥
129.m: Therefore, O lord, nothing is unattainable from the earth and the waters, / since austerity, sacrificial rites, and the like can arise only from those two.

129.s:
tatrāpi tīrthabhūtā tu yā bhūmis tāṃ vrajed bhavān
tatra viṣṇuṃ śivaṃ pūjya sarvān kāmān avāpsyasi //
129.d:
तत्रापि तीर्थभूता तु या भूमिस् तां व्रजेद् भवान्
तत्र विष्णुं शिवं पूज्य सर्वान् कामान् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
129.m: Even there, you should go to that land which has become a sacred ford; / having worshipped Viṣṇu and Śiva there, you will obtain all desires.

129.s:
śrutam asti punaś cedaṃ striyo yāś ca pativratāḥ
tā eva sarvaṃ jānanti dhṛtaṃ tābhiś carācaram //
129.d:
श्रुतम् अस्ति पुनश् चेदं स्त्रियो याश् च पतिव्रताः
ता एव सर्वं जानन्ति धृतं ताभिश् चराचरम् ॥
129.m: Furthermore, this has been heard: those women who are devoted to their husbands, / they alone know everything, and by them the moving and unmoving world is sustained.

129.s:
pṛthivyāṃ sārabhūtaṃ syāt tanmadhye daṇḍakaṃ vanam
tatra gaṅgā jagaddhātrī tatreśaṃ pūjaya prabho //
129.d:
पृथिव्यां सारभूतं स्यात् तन्मध्ये दण्डकं वनम्
तत्र गङ्गा जगद्धात्री तत्रेशं पूजय प्रभो ॥
129.m: That which is the essence on earth is the Daṇḍaka forest in its midst; / there is the Gaṅgā, the fosterer of the world. Worship the Lord there, O master,

129.s:
viṣṇuṃ vā jagatām īśaṃ dīnārtārtiharaṃ vibhum
anāthānām iha nṛṇāṃ majjatāṃ duḥkhasāgare //
129.d:
विष्णुं वा जगताम् ईशं दीनार्तार्तिहरं विभुम्
अनाथानाम् इह नृणां मज्जतां दुःखसागरे ॥
129.m: or Viṣṇu, the lord of the worlds, the all-pervading one who removes the distress of the poor and afflicted, / for men who are destitute here, sinking in the ocean of sorrow.

129.s:
haro harir vā gaṅgā vā kvāpy anyac charaṇaṃ nahi
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena toṣayaitān samāhitaḥ //
129.d:
हरो हरिर् वा गङ्गा वा क्वाप्य् अन्यच् छरणं नहि
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन तोषयैतान् समाहितः ॥
129.m: Hara, Hari, or Gaṅgā—nowhere else is there any refuge. / Therefore, with all effort and with a concentrated mind, propitiate these

129.s:
bhaktyā stotraiś ca tapasā kuru caiva mayā saha
tataḥ prāpsyasi kalyāṇam īśaviṣṇuprasādajam //
129.d:
भक्त्या स्तोत्रैश् च तपसा कुरु चैव मया सह
ततः प्राप्स्यसि कल्याणम् ईशविष्णुप्रसादजम् ॥
129.m: with devotion, hymns of praise, and austerity, and do so together with me; / then you will obtain good fortune born from the grace of the Lord and Viṣṇu.

129.s:
ajñātvaikaguṇaṃ karma phalaṃ dāsyati karmiṇaḥ
jñātvā śataguṇaṃ tat syād bhāryayā ca tad akṣayam //
129.d:
अज्ञात्वैकगुणं कर्म फलं दास्यति कर्मिणः
ज्ञात्वा शतगुणं तत् स्याद् भार्यया च तद् अक्षयम् ॥
129.m: A deed performed without knowledge will grant a single fold of fruit to the doer; / performed with knowledge, it becomes a hundredfold, and with a wife, it becomes imperishable.

129.s:
puṃsaḥ sarveṣu kāryeṣu bhāryaiveha sahāyinī
svalpānām api kāryāṇāṃ nahi siddhis tayā vinā //
129.d:
पुंसः सर्वेषु कार्येषु भार्यैवेह सहायिनी
स्वल्पानाम् अपि कार्याणां नहि सिद्धिस् तया विना ॥
129.m: In all undertakings of a man, his wife alone is his partner here; / without her, there is no success even in small undertakings.

129.s:
ekena yat kṛtaṃ karma tasmād ardhaphalaṃ bhavet
jāyayā tu kṛtaṃ nātha puṣkalaṃ puruṣo labhet //
129.d:
एकेन यत् कृतं कर्म तस्माद् अर्धफलं भवेत्
जायया तु कृतं नाथ पुष्कलं पुरुषो लभेत् ॥
129.m: From an action performed alone, half the fruit arises; / but when done with his wife, O lord, a man obtains the full [fruit].

129.s:
tasmād etat suviditam ardho jāyā iti śruteḥ
śrūyate daṇḍakāraṇye saricchreṣṭhāsti gautamī //
129.d:
तस्माद् एतत् सुविदितम् अर्धो जाया इति श्रुतेः
श्रूयते दण्डकारण्ये सरिच्छ्रेष्ठास्ति गौतमी ॥
129.m: Therefore this is well known from the Vedic scripture: ‘The wife is half.’ / It is heard that in the Daṇḍaka Forest there is the Gautamī, the best of rivers,

129.s:
aśeṣāghapraśamanī sarvābhīṣṭapradāyinī
tasmād gaccha mayā tatra kuru puṇyaṃ mahāphalam //
129.d:
अशेषाघप्रशमनी सर्वाभीष्टप्रदायिनी
तस्माद् गच्छ मया तत्र कुरु पुण्यं महाफलम् ॥
129.m: allayer of all sins, bestower of all desired things. / Therefore go there with me and perform merit yielding great fruit;

129.s: tataḥ śatrūn nihatyājau mahat sukham avāpsyasi //
129.d: ततः शत्रून् निहत्याजौ महत् सुखम् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
129.m: then, having slain your enemies in battle, you will attain great happiness.”

129.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā sa guruṇā bhāryayā ca śatakratuḥ
yayau gaṅgāṃ jagaddhātrīṃ gautamīṃ ceti viśrutām //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा स गुरुणा भार्यया च शतक्रतुः
ययौ गङ्गां जगद्धात्रीं गौतमीं चेति विश्रुताम् ॥
129.m: Brahmā said: / Having said, “So be it,” together with his preceptor and his wife, Śatakratu / went to the Gaṅgā, the fosterer of the world, renowned as the Gautamī.

129.s:
daṇḍakāraṇyamadhyasthāṃ yayau sa prītimān hariḥ
tapaḥ kartuṃ manaś cakre devadevāya śaṃbhave //
129.d:
दण्डकारण्यमध्यस्थां ययौ स प्रीतिमान् हरिः
तपः कर्तुं मनश् चक्रे देवदेवाय शंभवे ॥
129.m: Situated in the midst of the Daṇḍaka Forest, Hari [Indra] went filled with joy, / and set his mind on performing austerity for Śambhu, the god of gods.

129.s:
gaṅgāṃ natvā tu prathamaṃ snātvā ca sa kṛtāñjaliḥ
śivaikaśaraṇo bhūtvā stotraṃ cedaṃ tato 'bravīt //
129.d:
गङ्गां नत्वा तु प्रथमं स्नात्वा च स कृताञ्जलिः
शिवैकशरणो भूत्वा स्तोत्रं चेदं ततो ऽब्रवीत् ॥
129.m: Having first bowed to the Gaṅgā and bathed, with folded hands, / taking sole refuge in Śiva, he then spoke this hymn of praise:

129.s:
indra uvāca
svamāyayā yo hy akhilaṃ carācaraṃ
sṛjaty avaty atti na sajjate 'smin
ekaḥ svatantro 'dvayacit sukhātmakaḥ
sa naḥ prasanno 'stu pinākapāṇiḥ
129.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
स्वमायया यो ह्य् अखिलं चराचरं
सृजत्य् अवत्य् अत्ति न सज्जते ऽस्मिन्
एकः स्वतन्त्रो ऽद्वयचित् सुखात्मकः
स नः प्रसन्नो ऽस्तु पिनाकपाणिः
129.m: Indra said: / “He who by his own illusory power indeed creates, / protects, and devours the entire moving and unmoving world, yet is not attached to it, / who is one, autonomous, non-dual consciousness, whose nature is bliss— / may that Pināka-wielder be pleased with us!

129.s:
na yasya tattvaṃ sanakādayo 'pi
jānanti vedāntarahasyavijñāḥ
sa pārvatīśaḥ sakalābhilāṣa
dātā prasanno 'stu mamāndhakāriḥ
129.d:
न यस्य तत्त्वं सनकादयो ऽपि
जानन्ति वेदान्तरहस्यविज्ञाः
स पार्वतीशः सकलाभिलाष
दाता प्रसन्नो ऽस्तु ममान्धकारिः
129.m: He whose true nature not even Sanaka and the others, / knowers of the secret of Vedānta, know— / may he, the lord of Pārvatī, the granter of all desires, / the enemy of Andhaka, be pleased with me!

129.s:
sṛṣṭvā svayaṃbhūr bhagavān viriñciṃ
bhayaṃkaraṃ cāsya śiro 'nvapaśyat
chittvā nakhāgrair nakhasaktam etac
cikṣepa tasmād abhavat trivargaḥ
129.d:
सृष्ट्वा स्वयंभूर् भगवान् विरिञ्चिं
भयंकरं चास्य शिरो ऽन्वपश्यत्
छित्त्वा नखाग्रैर् नखसक्तम् एतच्
चिक्षेप तस्माद् अभवत् त्रिवर्गः
129.m: Having created Viriñci, the lord Svayambhū / saw his terrifying head; / having cut it with his fingernails, he threw this [head] clinging to his nail, / and from that the three aims of life arose.

129.s:
pāpaṃ daridraṃ tv atha lobhayācñe
moho vipac ceti tato 'py anantam
jātaprabhāvaṃ bhavaduḥkharūpaṃ
babhūva tair vyāptam idaṃ samastam
129.d:
पापं दरिद्रं त्व् अथ लोभयाच्ञे
मोहो विपच् चेति ततो ऽप्य् अनन्तम्
जातप्रभावं भवदुःखरूपं
बभूव तैर् व्याप्तम् इदं समस्तम्
129.m: Then sin, poverty, greed and begging, / delusion, and misfortune—and from that, endless / misery of worldly existence of great power arose, / and by these all this [world] was pervaded.

129.s:
avekṣya sarvaṃ cakitaḥ sureśo
devīm avocaj jagad astam eti
tvaṃ pāhi lokeśvari lokamātar
ume śaraṇye subhage subhadre
129.d:
अवेक्ष्य सर्वं चकितः सुरेशो
देवीम् अवोचज् जगद् अस्तम् एति
त्वं पाहि लोकेश्वरि लोकमातर्
उमे शरण्ये सुभगे सुभद्रे
129.m: Having perceived all this, the frightened lord of gods / said to the Goddess: ‘The world is sinking into ruin! / Protect it, O ruler of the world, mother of the world, / O Umā, refuge, auspicious, gracious one!

129.s:
jagatpratiṣṭhe varade jaya tvaṃ
bhuktiḥ samādhiḥ paramā ca muktiḥ
svāhā svadhā svastir anādisiddhir
gīr buddhir āsīr ajarāmare tvam
129.d:
जगत्प्रतिष्ठे वरदे जय त्वं
भुक्तिः समाधिः परमा च मुक्तिः
स्वाहा स्वधा स्वस्तिर् अनादिसिद्धिर्
गीर् बुद्धिर् आसीर् अजरामरे त्वम्
129.m: O support of the world, granter of boons, be victorious! / You are enjoyment, absorption, and ultimate liberation; / you are svāhā, svadhā, well-being, beginningless perfection, / speech, intellect, blessing, unaging and immortal!

129.s:
vidyādirūpeṇa jagattraye tvaṃ
rakṣāṃ karoṣy eva madājñayā ca
tvayaiva sṛṣṭaṃ bhuvanatrayaṃ syād
yataḥ prakṛtyaiva tathaiva citram
129.d:
विद्यादिरूपेण जगत्त्रये त्वं
रक्षां करोष्य् एव मदाज्ञया च
त्वयैव सृष्टं भुवनत्रयं स्याद्
यतः प्रकृत्यैव तथैव चित्रम्
129.m: In the form of knowledge and the rest, in the three worlds you / indeed provide protection by my command; / by you alone the three worlds must have been created, / since it is wondrous precisely by nature!’”

129.s:
ity evam uktā dayitā hareṇa
saṃśleṣasaṃlāpaparā babhūva
śrāntā bhavasyārdhatanau sulagnā
cikṣepa ca svedajalaṃ karāgraiḥ
129.d:
इत्य् एवम् उक्ता दयिता हरेण
संश्लेषसंलापपरा बभूव
श्रान्ता भवस्यार्धतनौ सुलग्ना
चिक्षेप च स्वेदजलं कराग्रैः
129.m:
Addressed in this way by Hara, his beloved
devoted herself to embracing and conversing [with him].
Wearied, clinging fast to Bhava's half-body,
she cast off her sweat with the tips of her fingers.

129.s:
tasmād babhūva prathamaṃ sa dharmo
lakṣmīr atho dānam atho suvṛṣṭiḥ
sattvaṃ susaṃpannadharaṃ sarāṃsi
dhānyāni puṣpāṇi phalāni caiva
129.d:
तस्माद् बभूव प्रथमं स धर्मो
लक्ष्मीर् अथो दानम् अथो सुवृष्टिः
सत्त्वं सुसंपन्नधरं सरांसि
धान्यानि पुष्पाणि फलानि चैव
129.m:
From that arose first dharma,
then prosperity, then charitable giving, then abundant rain,
vitality, the earth bearing wealth, lakes,
grains, flowers, and fruits;

129.s:
saubhāgyavastūni vapuḥ suveṣaḥ
śṛṅgārabhājīni mahauṣadhāni
nṛtyāni gītāny amṛtaṃ purāṇaṃ
śrutismṛtī nītir athānnapāne
129.d:
सौभाग्यवस्तूनि वपुः सुवेषः
शृङ्गारभाजीनि महौषधानि
नृत्यानि गीतान्य् अमृतं पुराणं
श्रुतिस्मृती नीतिर् अथान्नपाने
129.m:
auspicious articles, physical beauty, elegant garments,
erotic adornments, great medicinal herbs,
dances, songs, nectar, the Purāṇa,
the Śruti and Smṛti, statecraft, and food and drink;

129.s:
śastrāṇi śāstrāṇi gṛhopayogyāny
astrāṇi tīrthāni ca kānanāni
iṣṭāni pūrtāni ca maṅgalāni
yānāni śubhrābharaṇāsanāni
129.d:
शस्त्राणि शास्त्राणि गृहोपयोग्यान्य्
अस्त्राणि तीर्थानि च काननानि
इष्टानि पूर्तानि च मङ्गलानि
यानानि शुभ्राभरणासनानि
129.m:
weapons, treatises, household utilities,
missiles, holy bathing sites, and forests,
sacrificial rites and charitable works, auspicious things,
vehicles, bright ornaments, and seats.

129.s:
bhavāṅgasaṃsargasusaṃprahāsa
susvedasaṃlāparahaḥprakāraiḥ
tathaiva jātaṃ sacarācaraṃ ca
apāpakaṃ devi tataś ca jātam
129.d:
भवाङ्गसंसर्गसुसंप्रहास
सुस्वेदसंलापरहःप्रकारैः
तथैव जातं सचराचरं च
अपापकं देवि ततश् च जातम्
129.m:
Through the ways of intimate congress, joyful laughter,
copious sweat, and secret talks upon Bhava’s body,
everything moving and unmoving was likewise born,
and sinlessness arose from that, O goddess.

129.s:
sukhaṃ prabhūtaṃ ca śubhaṃ ca nityaṃ
virāji caitat tava devi bhāvāt
tasmāt tu māṃ rakṣa jagajjanitri
bhītaṃ bhayebhyo jagatāṃ pradhāne
129.d:
सुखं प्रभूतं च शुभं च नित्यं
विराजि चैतत् तव देवि भावात्
तस्मात् तु मां रक्ष जगज्जनित्रि
भीतं भयेभ्यो जगतां प्रधाने
129.m:
Abundant and eternal happiness and good fortune
shine forth through your presence, O goddess.
Therefore protect me, O Mother of the World,
who am frightened by perils, O pradhāna among the worlds!

129.s:
eke tarkair vimuhyanti līyante tatra cāpare
śivaśaktyos tadādvaitaṃ sundaraṃ naumi vigraham //
129.d:
एके तर्कैर् विमुह्यन्ति लीयन्ते तत्र चापरे
शिवशक्त्योस् तदाद्वैतं सुन्दरं नौमि विग्रहम् ॥
129.m:
Some are bewildered by dry arguments, while others merge into it;
I bow to that beautiful form, the non-duality of Śiva and Śakti.

129.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ tu stuvatas tasya purastād abhavac chivaḥ //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं तु स्तुवतस् तस्य पुरस्ताद् अभवच् छिवः ॥
129.m:
Brahmā said:
While he was thus praising him, Śiva appeared before him.

129.s:
śiva uvāca
kim abhīṣṭaṃ varayase hare vada parāyaṇam //
129.d:
शिव उवाच
किम् अभीष्टं वरयसे हरे वद परायणम् ॥
129.m:
Śiva said:
What wish do you choose as a boon, O Hari? Speak of your foremost desire.

129.s:
indra uvāca
balavān me ripuś cāsīd darśanaiś ca śanir yathā
tena baddhas talaṃ nītaḥ paribhūtas tv anekadhā //
129.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
बलवान् मे रिपुश् चासीद् दर्शनैश् च शनिर् यथा
तेन बद्धस् तलं नीतः परिभूतस् त्व् अनेकधा ॥

129.s:
vāksāyakais tathā viddhas tadvadhāya tv iyaṃ kṛtiḥ
tadarthaṃ jagatām īśa yena jeṣye ripuṃ prabho //
129.d:
वाक्सायकैस् तथा विद्धस् तद्वधाय त्व् इयं कृतिः
तदर्थं जगताम् ईश येन जेष्ये रिपुं प्रभो ॥
129.m:
I was pierced by arrows of words, and this effort is for his slaying;
for that purpose, O Lord of the Worlds, grant that by which I may conquer the enemy, O Lord.

129.s:
tad eva dehi vīryaṃ me yac cānyad ripunāśanam
jātaḥ parābhavo yasmāt tadvināśe kṛte sati
punarjātam ahaṃ manye varaṃ kīrtir jayaśriyoḥ //
129.d:
तद् एव देहि वीर्यं मे यच् चान्यद् रिपुनाशनम्
जातः पराभवो यस्मात् तद्विनाशे कृते सति
पुनर्जातम् अहं मन्ये वरं कीर्तिर् जयश्रियोः ॥
129.m:
Grant me that very strength, and whatever else destroys an enemy.
Since humiliation was born [of him], once his destruction is accomplished,
I consider that the boon of fame and the glory of victory are born anew.

129.s:
brahmovāca
sa śivaḥ śakram āhedaṃ na mayaikena te ripuḥ
vadham āpnoti tasmāt tvaṃ viṣṇum apy avyayaṃ harim //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स शिवः शक्रम् आहेदं न मयैकेन ते रिपुः
वधम् आप्नोति तस्मात् त्वं विष्णुम् अप्य् अव्ययं हरिम् ॥
129.m:
Brahmā said:
That Śiva said this to Śakra: "Your enemy shall not be slain
by me alone; therefore you, also [relying upon] Viṣṇu, imperishable Hari,

129.s:
ārādhayasva paulomyā saha devaṃ janārdanam
lokatrayaikaśaraṇaṃ nārāyaṇam ananyadhīḥ //
129.d:
आराधयस्व पौलोम्या सह देवं जनार्दनम्
लोकत्रयैकशरणं नारायणम् अनन्यधीः ॥
129.m:
propitiate god Janārdana together with Paulomī,
Nārāyaṇa, the sole refuge of the three worlds, with undivided mind.

129.s:
tataḥ prāpsyasi tasmāc ca mattaś cāpi priyaṃ hare
punaś covāca bhagavān ādikartā maheśvaraḥ //
129.d:
ततः प्राप्स्यसि तस्माच् च मत्तश् चापि प्रियं हरे
पुनश् चोवाच भगवान् आदिकर्ता महेश्वरः ॥
129.m:
Then you will attain your desired wish from him and also from me, O Hari!"
And the blessed Lord Maheśvara, the first maker, spoke again:

129.s:
mantrābhyāsas tapo vāpi yogābhyasanam eva ca
saṃgame yatra kutrāpi siddhidaṃ munayo viduḥ //
129.d:
मन्त्राभ्यासस् तपो वापि योगाभ्यसनम् एव च
संगमे यत्र कुत्रापि सिद्धिदं मुनयो विदुः ॥
129.m:
"The recitation of mantras, austerity, or the practice of yoga—
wherever at a confluence, sages know it to bestow accomplishment.

129.s:
kiṃ punaḥ saṃgame vipra gautamīsindhuphenayoḥ
girīṇāṃ gahvare yad vā saritām atha saṃgame //
129.d:
किं पुनः संगमे विप्र गौतमीसिन्धुफेनयोः
गिरीणां गह्वरे यद् वा सरिताम् अथ संगमे ॥
129.m:
How much more at the confluence of the Gautamī and Sindhu-Phenā, O twice-born,
or in a cave of the mountains, or at the confluence of rivers!

129.s:
vipro dhiyaiva bhavati mukundāṅghriniviṣṭayā
gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe tīra āpastambo munīśvaraḥ //
129.d:
विप्रो धियैव भवति मुकुन्दाङ्घ्रिनिविष्टया
गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तीर आपस्तम्बो मुनीश्वरः ॥
129.m:
One becomes a twice-born only through an intellect fixed on Mukunda’s feet.
On the southern bank of the Gaṅgā dwells the lord of sages Āpastamba;

129.s:
āste tasyāpy ahaṃ toṣam agamaṃ balasūdana
tena tvaṃ bhāryayā caiva toṣayasva gadādharam //
129.d:
आस्ते तस्याप्य् अहं तोषम् अगमं बलसूदन
तेन त्वं भार्यया चैव तोषयस्व गदाधरम् ॥
129.m:
I, too, found satisfaction in him, O slayer of Bala.
Along with your wife, propitiate Gadādhara through him."

129.s:
brahmovāca
āpastambena sahito gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe
tuṣṭāva devaṃ prayataḥ snātvā puṇye 'tha saṃgame //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
आपस्तम्बेन सहितो गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तटे
तुष्टाव देवं प्रयतः स्नात्वा पुण्ये ऽथ संगमे ॥
129.m:
Brahmā said:
Accompanied by Āpastamba, on the southern bank of the Gaṅgā,
restrained, having bathed at the holy confluence,

129.s:
phenāyāś caiva gaṅgāyās tatra devaṃ janārdanam
vaidikair vividhair mantrais tapasātoṣayat tadā //
129.d:
फेनायाश् चैव गङ्गायास् तत्र देवं जनार्दनम्
वैदिकैर् विविधैर् मन्त्रैस् तपसातोषयत् तदा ॥
129.m:
of the Phenā and the Gaṅgā, he then propitiated
god Janārdana there with various Vedic mantras and austerity.

129.s:
tatas tuṣṭo 'bhavad viṣṇuḥ kiṃ deyaṃ cety abhāṣata
dehi me śatruhantāram ity āha bhagavān hariḥ //
129.d:
ततस् तुष्टो ऽभवद् विष्णुः किं देयं चेत्य् अभाषत
देहि मे शत्रुहन्तारम् इत्य् आह भगवान् हरिः ॥
129.m:
Then Viṣṇu was pleased and spoke: "What should be given?"
"Give me a slayer of my enemy," said the blessed Hari.

129.s:
dattam ity eva jānīhi tam uvāca janārdanaḥ
tatrābhavac chivasyaiva gaṅgāviṣṇvoḥ prasādataḥ //
129.d:
दत्तम् इत्य् एव जानीहि तम् उवाच जनार्दनः
तत्राभवच् छिवस्यैव गङ्गाविष्ण्वोः प्रसादतः ॥
129.m:
"Know it as given!" Janārdana said to him.
There, by the grace of Śiva, Gaṅgā, and Viṣṇu,

129.s:
ambhasā puruṣo jātaḥ śivaviṣṇusvarūpadhṛk
cakrapāṇiḥ śūladharaḥ sa gatvā tu rasātalam //
129.d:
अम्भसा पुरुषो जातः शिवविष्णुस्वरूपधृक्
चक्रपाणिः शूलधरः स गत्वा तु रसातलम् ॥
129.m:
a man was born from the water, bearing the forms of Śiva and Viṣṇu,
disc-handed and spear-bearing. Going to Rasātala,

129.s:
nijaghāna tadā daityam indraśatruṃ mahāśanim
sakhābhavat sa cendrasya abjakaḥ sa vṛṣākapiḥ //
129.d:
निजघान तदा दैत्यम् इन्द्रशत्रुं महाशनिम्
सखाभवत् स चेन्द्रस्य अब्जकः स वृषाकपिः ॥
129.m:
he then slew the Daitya Mahāśani, the enemy of Indra.
And he became Indra's friend, the water-born Vṛṣākapi.

129.s:
divistho 'pi sadā cendras tam anveti vṛṣākapim
kupitā praṇayenābhūd anyāsaktaṃ vilokya tam
śacīṃ tāṃ sāntvayann āha śatamanyur hasann idam //
129.d:
दिविस्थो ऽपि सदा चेन्द्रस् तम् अन्वेति वृषाकपिम्
कुपिता प्रणयेनाभूद् अन्यासक्तं विलोक्य तम्
शचीं तां सान्त्वयन्न् आह शतमन्युर् हसन्न् इदम् ॥

129.s:
indra uvāca
nāham indrāṇi śaraṇam ṛte sakhyur vṛṣākapeḥ
vāri vāpi havir yasya agneḥ priyakaraṃ sadā //
129.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
नाहम् इन्द्राणि शरणम् ऋते सख्युर् वृषाकपेः
वारि वापि हविर् यस्य अग्नेः प्रियकरं सदा ॥
129.m:
Indra said:
"O Indrāṇī, I have no refuge except my friend Vṛṣākapi,
whose water or oblation is ever pleasing to Agni.

129.s:
nāham anyatra gantāsmi priye cāṅgena te śape
tasmān nārhasi māṃ vaktuṃ śaṅkayānyatra bhāmini //
129.d:
नाहम् अन्यत्र गन्तास्मि प्रिये चाङ्गेन ते शपे
तस्मान् नार्हसि मां वक्तुं शङ्कयान्यत्र भामिनि ॥
129.m:
I will not go elsewhere, my dear; I swear by your body!
Therefore you should not speak to me with suspicion of another, O radiant lady.

129.s:
pativratā priyā me tvaṃ dharme mantre sahāyinī
sāpatyā ca kulīnā ca tvatto 'nyā kā priyā mama //
129.d:
पतिव्रता प्रिया मे त्वं धर्मे मन्त्रे सहायिनी
सापत्या च कुलीना च त्वत्तो ऽन्या का प्रिया मम ॥
129.m:
You are devoted to your husband, dear to me, my helper in dharma and counsel,
blessed with children, and of noble birth; what other woman is dear to me besides you?

129.s:
tasmāt tavopadeśena gaṅgāṃ prāpya mahānadīm
prasādād devadevasya viṣṇor vai cakrapāṇinaḥ //
129.d:
तस्मात् तवोपदेशेन गङ्गां प्राप्य महानदीम्
प्रसादाद् देवदेवस्य विष्णोर् वै चक्रपाणिनः ॥
129.m:
Therefore, through your counsel, having reached the great river Gaṅgā,
by the grace of Viṣṇu, the god of gods, who bears the disc in hand,

129.s:
tathā śivasya devasya prasādāc ca vṛṣākapeḥ
jalodbhavāc ca me mitrād abjakāl lokaviśrutāt //
129.d:
तथा शिवस्य देवस्य प्रसादाच् च वृषाकपेः
जलोद्भवाच् च मे मित्राद् अब्जकाल् लोकविश्रुतात् ॥
129.m:
and by the grace of the god Śiva, and of Vṛṣākapi,
my friend born from the water, the water-born one world-renowned,

129.s:
uttīrṇaduḥkhaḥ subhage ita indro 'ham acyutaḥ
kiṃ na sādhyaṃ yatra bhāryā bhartṛcittānugāminī //
129.d:
उत्तीर्णदुःखः सुभगे इत इन्द्रो ऽहम् अच्युतः
किं न साध्यं यत्र भार्या भर्तृचित्तानुगामिनी ॥
129.m:
I have crossed beyond sorrow, O fortunate lady; from now on I am Indra, unfallen.
What cannot be accomplished where a wife follows her husband’s mind?

129.s:
duṣkarā tatra no muktiḥ kiṃtv arthāditrayaṃ śubhe
jāyaiva paramaṃ mitraṃ lokadvayahitaiṣiṇī //
129.d:
दुष्करा तत्र नो मुक्तिः किंत्व् अर्थादित्रयं शुभे
जायैव परमं मित्रं लोकद्वयहितैषिणी ॥
129.m:
Liberation is not hard to attain there, let alone the triad of wealth and the rest, O auspicious lady.
A wife alone is the supreme friend, wishing the welfare of both worlds.

129.s:
sā cet kulīnā priyabhāṣiṇī ca
pativratā rūpavatī guṇāḍhyā
saṃpatsu cāpatsu samānarūpā
tayā hy asādhyaṃ kim iha trilokyām
129.d:
सा चेत् कुलीना प्रियभाषिणी च
पतिव्रता रूपवती गुणाढ्या
संपत्सु चापत्सु समानरूपा
तया ह्य् असाध्यं किम् इह त्रिलोक्याम्
129.m:
If she is noble, sweet-speaking,
devoted to her husband, beautiful, rich in virtues,
and remains the same in prosperity and adversity,
what indeed in the three worlds is impossible through her?

129.s:
tasmāt tava dhiyā kānte mamedaṃ śubham āgatam
itas tavoditaṃ caiva kartavyaṃ nānyad asti me //
129.d:
तस्मात् तव धिया कान्ते ममेदं शुभम् आगतम्
इतस् तवोदितं चैव कर्तव्यं नान्यद् अस्ति मे ॥
129.m:
Therefore, O beloved, this good fortune has come to me through your wisdom;
from now on, only what is spoken by you is my duty, none other.

129.s:
paraloke ca dharme ca satputrasadṛśaṃ na ca
ārtasya puruṣasyeha bhāryāvad bheṣajaṃ nahi //
129.d:
परलोके च धर्मे च सत्पुत्रसदृशं न च
आर्तस्य पुरुषस्येह भार्यावद् भेषजं नहि ॥
129.m:
In the other world and in dharma there is nothing equal to a virtuous son;
for an afflicted man here, there is truly no medicine like a wife.

129.s:
niḥśreyasapadaprāptyai tathā pāpasya muktaye
gaṅgayā sadṛśaṃ nāsti śṛṇu cānyad varānane //
129.d:
निःश्रेयसपदप्राप्त्यै तथा पापस्य मुक्तये
गङ्गया सदृशं नास्ति शृणु चान्यद् वरानने ॥
129.m:
For attaining the state of highest bliss and for liberation from sin,
there is nothing equal to the Gaṅgā; and hear another thing, O fair-faced one:

129.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ prāptaye pāpamuktaye
śivaviṣṇvor ananyatvajñānān nāsty atra muktaye //
129.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां प्राप्तये पापमुक्तये
शिवविष्ण्वोर् अनन्यत्वज्ञानान् नास्त्य् अत्र मुक्तये ॥
129.m:
For attaining dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation, and for freedom from sin,
there is nothing here for liberation like the knowledge of the non-difference of Śiva and Viṣṇu.

129.s:
tasmāt tava dhiyā sādhvi sarvam etan manogatam
avāptaṃ ca śivād viṣṇor gaṅgāyāś ca prasādataḥ //
129.d:
तस्मात् तव धिया साध्वि सर्वम् एतन् मनोगतम्
अवाप्तं च शिवाद् विष्णोर् गङ्गायाश् च प्रसादतः ॥
129.m:
Therefore, O virtuous lady, through your wisdom, all this desire of my mind
has been obtained by the grace of Śiva, Viṣṇu, and the Gaṅgā.

129.s:
indratvaṃ me sthiraṃ ceto manye mitrabalāt punaḥ
vṛṣākapir mama sakhā yo jātas tv apsu bhāmini //
129.d:
इन्द्रत्वं मे स्थिरं चेतो मन्ये मित्रबलात् पुनः
वृषाकपिर् मम सखा यो जातस् त्व् अप्सु भामिनि ॥
129.m:
I consider my sovereignty as Indra to be steady again through the power of my friend—
Vṛṣākapi, my friend who was born in the waters, O radiant lady.

129.s:
tvaṃ ca priyasakhī nityaṃ nānyat priyataraṃ mama
tīrthānāṃ gautamī gaṅgā devānāṃ hariśaṃkarau //
129.d:
त्वं च प्रियसखी नित्यं नान्यत् प्रियतरं मम
तीर्थानां गौतमी गङ्गा देवानां हरिशंकरौ ॥
129.m:
And you are my constant dear friend; nothing is dearer to me.
Among holy bathing places is Gautamī Gaṅgā; among gods, Hari and Śaṅkara.

129.s:
tasmād ebhyaḥ prasādena sarvaṃ cepsitam āptavān
mama prītikaraṃ cedaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam //
129.d:
तस्माद् एभ्यः प्रसादेन सर्वं चेप्सितम् आप्तवान्
मम प्रीतिकरं चेदं तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ॥
129.m:
Therefore, by their grace, I have attained everything I desired;
and this world-renowned holy bathing place is dear to me.

129.s:
tasmād etad dhi yāciṣye devān sarvān anukramāt
anumanyantu ṛṣayo gaṅgā ca hariśaṃkarau //
129.d:
तस्माद् एतद् धि याचिष्ये देवान् सर्वान् अनुक्रमात्
अनुमन्यन्तु ऋषयो गङ्गा च हरिशंकरौ ॥
129.m:
Therefore, I shall surely ask this of all the gods in sequence:
let the ṛṣis, the Gaṅgā, and Hari and Śaṅkara grant their consent!

129.s:
indreśvare cābjake ca ubhayos tīrayoḥ surāḥ
ekatra śaṃkaro devo hy aparatra janārdanaḥ //
129.d:
इन्द्रेश्वरे चाब्जके च उभयोस् तीरयोः सुराः
एकत्र शंकरो देवो ह्य् अपरत्र जनार्दनः ॥
129.m:
At Indreśvara and at Abjaka, on both banks, O gods,
on one side is the god Śaṅkara, and on the other, Janārdana,

129.s:
pāvayan daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ sākṣād viṣṇus trivikramaḥ
antare yāni tīrthāni sarvapuṇyapradāni ca //
129.d:
पावयन् दण्डकारण्यं साक्षाद् विष्णुस् त्रिविक्रमः
अन्तरे यानि तीर्थानि सर्वपुण्यप्रदानि च ॥
129.m:
sanctifying the Daṇḍaka Forest, manifest Viṣṇu Trivikrama;
and whichever holy bathing sites are in between, they bestow all merit.

129.s:
atra tu snānamātreṇa sarve te muktim āpnuyuḥ
pāpiṣṭhāḥ pāpato muktim āpnuyur ye ca dharmiṇaḥ //
129.d:
अत्र तु स्नानमात्रेण सर्वे ते मुक्तिम् आप्नुयुः
पापिष्ठाः पापतो मुक्तिम् आप्नुयुर् ये च धर्मिणः ॥
129.m: Here, by bathing alone, all of them would attain liberation; / the most sinful would attain liberation from sin, and those who are righteous

129.s:
teṣāṃ tu paramā muktiḥ pitṛbhiḥ pañcapañcabhiḥ
atra kiṃcic ca ye dadyur arthibhyas tilamātrakam //
129.d:
तेषां तु परमा मुक्तिः पितृभिः पञ्चपञ्चभिः
अत्र किंचिच् च ये दद्युर् अर्थिभ्यस् तिलमात्रकम् ॥
129.m: would attain supreme liberation along with twenty-five generations of ancestors. / And whatever someone gives here to petitioners, even if only a single sesame seed,

129.s:
dātṛbhyo hy akṣayaṃ tat syāt kāmadaṃ mokṣadaṃ tathā
dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyam ārogyaṃ puṇyavardhanam //
129.d:
दातृभ्यो ह्य् अक्षयं तत् स्यात् कामदं मोक्षदं तथा
धन्यं यशस्यम् आयुष्यम् आरोग्यं पुण्यवर्धनम् ॥
129.m: shall become inexhaustible for the givers, granting desires and granting liberation, / bringing fortune, fame, longevity, health, and increase of merit.

129.s:
ākhyānaṃ viṣṇuśaṃbhvoś ca jñātvā snānāc ca muktidam
asya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ ye śṛṇvanti paṭhanti ca //
129.d:
आख्यानं विष्णुशंभ्वोश् च ज्ञात्वा स्नानाच् च मुक्तिदम्
अस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं ये शृण्वन्ति पठन्ति च ॥
129.m: Those who hear and recite the narrative of Viṣṇu and Śaṃbhu, / knowing that it grants liberation through bathing, and the greatness of this tīrtha,

129.s:
puṇyabhājo bhaveyus te tebhyo 'traiva smṛtir bhavet
śivaviṣṇvor aśeṣāghasaṃghavicchedakāriṇī
yāṃ prārthayanti munayo vijitendriyamānasāḥ //
129.d:
पुण्यभाजो भवेयुस् ते तेभ्यो ऽत्रैव स्मृतिर् भवेत्
शिवविष्ण्वोर् अशेषाघसंघविच्छेदकारिणी
यां प्रार्थयन्ति मुनयो विजितेन्द्रियमानसाः ॥
129.m: shall become possessors of merit; to them right here shall come the remembrance / of Śiva and Viṣṇu, which destroys the entire mass of sins, / which the sages, with minds and senses conquered, pray for.

129.s:
brahmovāca
bhaviṣyaty evam eveti taṃ devā ṛṣayo 'bruvan
gautamyā uttare pāre tīrthānāṃ mokṣadāyinām //
129.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
भविष्यत्य् एवम् एवेति तं देवा ऋषयो ऽब्रुवन्
गौतम्या उत्तरे पारे तीर्थानां मोक्षदायिनाम् ॥
129.m:
Brahmā said:
“It will be just so,” the gods and sages said to him. / On the northern bank of the Gautamī, among the liberation-bestowing tīrthas,

129.s:
devarṣisiddhasevyānāṃ sahasrāṇy atha sapta vai
tathaiva dakṣiṇe tīre tīrthāny ekādaśaiva tu //
129.d:
देवर्षिसिद्धसेव्यानां सहस्राण्य् अथ सप्त वै
तथैव दक्षिणे तीरे तीर्थान्य् एकादशैव तु ॥
129.m: frequented by divine sages and Siddhas, there are indeed seven thousand; / likewise, on the southern bank there are eleven [thousand] tīrthas.

129.s:
abjakaṃ hṛdayaṃ proktaṃ godāvaryā munīśvaraiḥ
viśrāmasthānam īśasya viṣṇor brahmaṇa eva ca //
129.d:
अब्जकं हृदयं प्रोक्तं गोदावर्या मुनीश्वरैः
विश्रामस्थानम् ईशस्य विष्णोर् ब्रह्मण एव च ॥
129.m: Abjaka is called the heart of the Godāvarī by the lordly sages, / the resting place of the Lord, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā.

130.s:
brahmovāca
āpastambam iti khyātaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam
smaraṇād apy aśeṣāghasaṃghavidhvaṃsanakṣamam //
130.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
आपस्तम्बम् इति ख्यातं तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्
स्मरणाद् अप्य् अशेषाघसंघविध्वंसनक्षमम् ॥
130.m:
Brahmā said:
Famous across the three worlds is the tīrtha known as Āpastamba, / capable of destroying the entire mass of sins even by remembrance.

130.s:
āpastambo mahāprājño munir āsīn mahāyaśāḥ
tasya bhāryākṣasūtreti patidharmaparāyaṇā //
130.d:
आपस्तम्बो महाप्राज्ञो मुनिर् आसीन् महायशाः
तस्य भार्याक्षसूत्रेति पतिधर्मपरायणा ॥
130.m: There was a very wise sage of great renown named Āpastamba; / his wife, named Akṣasūtrā, was devoted to her husband's dharma.

130.s:
tasya putro mahāprājñaḥ karkināmātha tattvavit
tasyāśramam anuprāpto hy agastyo munisattamaḥ //
130.d:
तस्य पुत्रो महाप्राज्ञः कर्किनामाथ तत्त्ववित्
तस्याश्रमम् अनुप्राप्तो ह्य् अगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः ॥
130.m: His son was very wise, named Karki, a knower of reality. / To his hermitage came Agastya, the best of sages.

130.s:
tam agastyaṃ pūjayitvā āpastambo munīśvaraḥ
śiṣyair anugato dhīmāṃs taṃ praṣṭum upacakrame //
130.d:
तम् अगस्त्यं पूजयित्वा आपस्तम्बो मुनीश्वरः
शिष्यैर् अनुगतो धीमांस् तं प्रष्टुम् उपचक्रमे ॥
130.m: Having honoured Agastya, the wise sage Āpastamba, / accompanied by his disciples, proceeded to ask him:

130.s:
āpastamba uvāca
trayāṇāṃ ko nu pūjyaḥ syād devānāṃ munisattama
bhuktir muktiś ca kasmād vā syād anādiś ca ko bhavet //
130.d:
आपस्तम्ब उवाच
त्रयाणां को नु पूज्यः स्याद् देवानां मुनिसत्तम
भुक्तिर् मुक्तिश् च कस्माद् वा स्याद् अनादिश् च को भवेत् ॥
130.m:
Āpastamba said:
Among the three gods, who is to be worshipped, O best of sages? / From whom comes enjoyment and liberation? And who is without beginning?

130.s:
anantaś cāpi ko vipra devānām api daivatam
yajñaiḥ ka ijyate devaḥ ko vedeṣv anugīyate
etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ chettuṃ vadāgastya mahāmune //
130.d:
अनन्तश् चापि को विप्र देवानाम् अपि दैवतम्
यज्ञैः क इज्यते देवः को वेदेष्व् अनुगीयते
एतं मे संशयं छेत्तुं वदागस्त्य महामुने ॥
130.m: And who is endless, O twice-born? Who is the deity even of the gods? / Which god is worshipped with sacrifices? Who is celebrated in the Vedas? / Speak, O great sage Agastya, to cut away this doubt of mine!

130.s:
agastya uvāca
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ pramāṇaṃ śabda ucyate
tatrāpi vaidikaḥ śabdaḥ pramāṇaṃ paramaṃ mataḥ //
130.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां प्रमाणं शब्द उच्यते
तत्रापि वैदिकः शब्दः प्रमाणं परमं मतः ॥
130.m:
Agastya said:
Verbal testimony is called the means of valid knowledge for dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation; / even there, Vedic testimony is held to be the supreme means of valid knowledge.

130.s:
vedena gīyate yas tu puruṣaḥ sa parāt paraḥ
mṛto 'paraḥ sa vijñeyo hy amṛtaḥ para ucyate //
130.d:
वेदेन गीयते यस् तु पुरुषः स परात् परः
मृतो ऽपरः स विज्ञेयो ह्य् अमृतः पर उच्यते ॥
130.m: The puruṣa who is sung by the Veda is higher than the high; / he who is mortal should be known as the lower, while the immortal is called the higher.

130.s:
yo 'mūrtaḥ sa paro jñeyo hy aparo mūrta ucyate
guṇābhivyāptibhedena mūrto 'sau trividho bhavet //
130.d:
यो ऽमूर्तः स परो ज्ञेयो ह्य् अपरो मूर्त उच्यते
गुणाभिव्याप्तिभेदेन मूर्तो ऽसौ त्रिविधो भवेत् ॥
130.m: He who is formless should be known as higher, while he who possesses form is called lower; / by the distinction of the pervasion of the guṇas, this one with form becomes threefold.

130.s:
brahmā viṣṇuḥ śivaś ceti eka eva tridhocyate
trayāṇām api devānāṃ vedyam ekaṃ paraṃ hi tat //
130.d:
ब्रह्मा विष्णुः शिवश् चेति एक एव त्रिधोच्यते
त्रयाणाम् अपि देवानां वेद्यम् एकं परं हि तत् ॥
130.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva: thus the one alone is spoken of as threefold. / For of all three gods, the supreme object of knowledge is that one.

130.s:
ekasya bahudhā vyāptir guṇakarmavibhedataḥ
lokānām upakārārtham ākṛtitritayaṃ bhavet //
130.d:
एकस्य बहुधा व्याप्तिर् गुणकर्मविभेदतः
लोकानाम् उपकारार्थम् आकृतित्रितयं भवेत् ॥
130.m: The pervasion of the one becomes manifold through the distinction of qualities and actions; / for the benefit of the worlds there is a triad of forms.

130.s:
yas tattvaṃ vetti paramaṃ sa ca vidvān na cetaraḥ
tatra yo bhedam ācaṣṭe liṅgabhedī sa ucyate //
130.d:
यस् तत्त्वं वेत्ति परमं स च विद्वान् न चेतरः
तत्र यो भेदम् आचष्टे लिङ्गभेदी स उच्यते ॥
130.m: He who knows the supreme reality is the learned man, and none other. / Whoever proclaims a difference among them is called a divider of the mark;

130.s:
prāyaścittaṃ na tasyāsti yaś caiṣāṃ vyāhared bhidam
trayāṇām api devānāṃ mūrtibhedaḥ pṛthak pṛthak //
130.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं न तस्यास्ति यश् चैषां व्याहरेद् भिदम्
त्रयाणाम् अपि देवानां मूर्तिभेदः पृथक् पृथक् ॥
130.m: there is no expiation for him who would speak of a difference among them. / The difference of form for each of the three gods is distinct;

130.s:
vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvatra sākāreṣu pṛthak pṛthak
nirākāraṃ ca yat tv ekaṃ tat tebhyaḥ paramaṃ matam //
130.d:
वेदाः प्रमाणं सर्वत्र साकारेषु पृथक् पृथक्
निराकारं च यत् त्व् एकं तत् तेभ्यः परमं मतम् ॥
130.m: the Vedas are the means of valid knowledge everywhere regarding their distinct individual forms, / but that which is one and formless is held to be higher than them.

130.s:
āpastamba uvāca
nānena nirṇayaḥ kaścin mayātra vidito bhavet
tatrāpy atra rahasyaṃ yat tad vimṛśyāśu kīrtyatām
niḥsaṃśayaṃ nirvikalpaṃ bhājanaṃ sarvasaṃpadām //
130.d:
आपस्तम्ब उवाच
नानेन निर्णयः कश्चिन् मयात्र विदितो भवेत्
तत्राप्य् अत्र रहस्यं यत् तद् विमृश्याशु कीर्त्यताम्
निःसंशयं निर्विकल्पं भाजनं सर्वसंपदाम् ॥
130.m:
Āpastamba said:
By this no definite conclusion has been understood by me here. / Therefore, whatever is secret in this matter, having reflected upon it, let it be declared at once— / free of doubt, without hesitation, a vessel of all fortunes!

130.s:
brahmovāca
etad ākarṇya bhagavān agastyo vākyam abravīt //
130.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतद् आकर्ण्य भगवान् अगस्त्यो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
130.m:
Brahmā said:
Having heard this, the venerable Agastya spoke these words:

130.s:
agastya uvāca
yadyapy eṣāṃ na bhedo 'sti devānāṃ tu parasparam
tathāpi sarvasiddhiḥ syāc chivād eva sukhātmanaḥ //
130.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
यद्यप्य् एषां न भेदो ऽस्ति देवानां तु परस्परम्
तथापि सर्वसिद्धिः स्याच् छिवाद् एव सुखात्मनः ॥
130.m:
Agastya said:
Although there is no mutual difference among these gods, / nevertheless, all accomplishment comes from Śiva alone, whose nature is bliss.

130.s:
prapañcasya nimittaṃ yat taj jyotiś ca paraṃ śivaḥ
tam eva sādhaya haraṃ bhaktyā paramayā mune
gautamyāṃ sakalāghaughasaṃhartā daṇḍake vane //
130.d:
प्रपञ्चस्य निमित्तं यत् तज् ज्योतिश् च परं शिवः
तम् एव साधय हरं भक्त्या परमया मुने
गौतम्यां सकलाघौघसंहर्ता दण्डके वने ॥
130.m: Śiva is the supreme light that is the cause of the phenomenal expanse; / propitiate him alone, Hara, with supreme devotion, O sage, / the destroyer of the flood of all sins on the Gautamī in the Daṇḍaka forest.

130.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā muner vākyaṃ parāṃ prītim upāgataḥ
bhuktido muktidaḥ puṃsāṃ sākāro 'tha nirākṛtiḥ //
130.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा मुनेर् वाक्यं परां प्रीतिम् उपागतः
भुक्तिदो मुक्तिदः पुंसां साकारो ऽथ निराकृतिः ॥
130.m:
Brahmā said:
Having heard this word of the sage, he attained supreme delight. / He grants enjoyment and grants liberation to men, having form and yet being formless;

130.s:
sṛṣṭyākāras tataḥ śaktaḥ pālanākāra eva ca
dātā ca hanti sarvaṃ yo yasmād etat samāpyate //
130.d:
सृष्ट्याकारस् ततः शक्तः पालनाकार एव च
दाता च हन्ति सर्वं यो यस्माद् एतत् समाप्यते ॥
130.m: then [he takes] the form of creation, being capable, and also the form of maintenance; / he is the giver, and he destroys everything, because this ends from him.

130.s:
agastya uvāca
brahmākṛtiḥ kartṛrūpā vaiṣṇavī pālanī tathā
rudrākṛtir nihantrī sā sarvavedeṣu paṭhyate //
130.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
ब्रह्माकृतिः कर्तृरूपा वैष्णवी पालनी तथा
रुद्राकृतिर् निहन्त्री सा सर्ववेदेषु पठ्यते ॥
130.m:
Agastya said:
The form of Brahmā has the nature of the creator; likewise, the form of Viṣṇu maintains; / the form of Rudra is the destroyer: thus it is recited in all the Vedas.

130.s:
brahmovāca
āpastambas tadā gaṅgāṃ gatvā snātvā yatavrataḥ
tuṣṭāva śaṃkaraṃ devaṃ stotreṇānena nārada //
130.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
आपस्तम्बस् तदा गङ्गां गत्वा स्नात्वा यतव्रतः
तुष्टाव शंकरं देवं स्तोत्रेणानेन नारद ॥
130.m:
Brahmā said:
Then Āpastamba went to the river, bathed, restrained his vows, / and praised the god Śaṅkara with this hymn of praise, O Nārada:

130.s:
āpastamba uvāca
kāṣṭheṣu vahniḥ kusumeṣu gandho
bījeṣu vṛkṣādi dṛṣatsu hema
bhūteṣu sarveṣu tathāsti yo vai
taṃ somanāthaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
आपस्तम्ब उवाच
काष्ठेषु वह्निः कुसुमेषु गन्धो
बीजेषु वृक्षादि दृषत्सु हेम
भूतेषु सर्वेषु तथास्ति यो वै
तं सोमनाथं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m:
Āpastamba said:
Just as there is fire in pieces of wood, fragrance in flowers, / trees and such in seeds, and gold in stones, / so he who is present in all beings— / to that Somanātha I go for refuge.

130.s:
yo līlayā viśvam idaṃ cakāra
dhātā vidhātā bhuvanatrayasya
yo viśvarūpaḥ sadasatparo yaḥ
someśvaraṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
यो लीलया विश्वम् इदं चकार
धाता विधाता भुवनत्रयस्य
यो विश्वरूपः सदसत्परो यः
सोमेश्वरं तं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m: He who made this universe in play, / the creator and ordainer of the three worlds, / who is of universal form, who is beyond being and non-being— / to that Someśvara I go for refuge.

130.s:
yaṃ smṛtya dāridryamahābhiśāpa
rogādibhir na spṛśyate śarīrī
yam āśritāś cepsitam āpnuvanti
someśvaraṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
यं स्मृत्य दारिद्र्यमहाभिशाप
रोगादिभिर् न स्पृश्यते शरीरी
यम् आश्रिताश् चेप्सितम् आप्नुवन्ति
सोमेश्वरं तं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m: Remembering whom an embodied being is not touched / by poverty, great curses, disease, and the like, / and relying upon whom they attain what is desired— / to that Someśvara I go for refuge.

130.s:
yena trayīdharmam avekṣya pūrvaṃ
brahmādayas tatra samīhitāś ca
evaṃ dvidhā yena kṛtaṃ śarīraṃ
someśvaraṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
येन त्रयीधर्मम् अवेक्ष्य पूर्वं
ब्रह्मादयस् तत्र समीहिताश् च
एवं द्विधा येन कृतं शरीरं
सोमेश्वरं तं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m: By whom, having first regarded the dharma of the triple Veda, / Brahmā and the others were set to action in it, / by whom the body was thus made twofold— / to that Someśvara I go for refuge.

130.s:
yasmai namo gacchati mantrapūtaṃ
hutaṃ havir yā ca kṛtā ca pūjā
dattaṃ havir yena surā bhajante
someśvaraṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
यस्मै नमो गच्छति मन्त्रपूतं
हुतं हविर् या च कृता च पूजा
दत्तं हविर् येन सुरा भजन्ते
सोमेश्वरं तं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m: To whom goes the salutation purified by mantra, / the oblation offered, and the worship performed, / by whom given the gods enjoy the oblation— / to that Someśvara I go for refuge.

130.s:
yasmāt paraṃ nānyad asti praśastaṃ
yasmāt paraṃ naiva susūkṣmam anyat
yasmāt paraṃ no mahatāṃ mahac ca
someśvaraṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
यस्मात् परं नान्यद् अस्ति प्रशस्तं
यस्मात् परं नैव सुसूक्ष्मम् अन्यत्
यस्मात् परं नो महतां महच् च
सोमेश्वरं तं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m: Beyond whom there is nothing else praised, / beyond whom there is nothing exceedingly subtle, / beyond whom there is nothing greater than the great— / to that Someśvara I go for refuge.

130.s:
yasyājñayā viśvam idaṃ vicitram
acintyarūpaṃ vividhaṃ mahac ca
ekakriyaṃ yadvad anuprayāti
someśvaraṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
यस्याज्ञया विश्वम् इदं विचित्रम्
अचिन्त्यरूपं विविधं महच् च
एकक्रियं यद्वद् अनुप्रयाति
सोमेश्वरं तं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m: By whose command this wonderful universe, / inconceivable in form, diverse and vast, / proceeds as though with a single action— / to that Someśvara I go for refuge.

130.s:
yasmin vibhūtiḥ sakalādhipatyaṃ
kartṛtvadātṛtvamahattvam eva
prītir yaśaḥ saukhyam anādidharmaḥ
someśvaraṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
यस्मिन् विभूतिः सकलाधिपत्यं
कर्तृत्वदातृत्वमहत्त्वम् एव
प्रीतिर् यशः सौख्यम् अनादिधर्मः
सोमेश्वरं तं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m: In whom are sovereign power, lordship over all, / agency, the quality of giving, and greatness itself, / love, fame, happiness, and beginningless dharma— / to that Someśvara I go for refuge.

130.s:
nityaṃ śaraṇyaḥ sakalasya pūjyo
nityaṃ priyo yaḥ śaraṇāgatasya
nityaṃ śivo yaḥ sakalasya rūpaṃ
someśvaraṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi
130.d:
नित्यं शरण्यः सकलस्य पूज्यो
नित्यं प्रियो यः शरणागतस्य
नित्यं शिवो यः सकलस्य रूपं
सोमेश्वरं तं शरणं व्रजामि
130.m: "The eternal refuge, worthy of worship by all, / Who is ever dear to him who has sought refuge, / Who is ever auspicious, the form of everything— / To that Someśvara I go for refuge."

130.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prasanno bhagavān āha nārada taṃ munim
ātmārthaṃ ca parārthaṃ ca āpastambo 'bravīc chivam //
130.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान् आह नारद तं मुनिम्
आत्मार्थं च परार्थं च आपस्तम्बो ऽब्रवीच् छिवम् ॥
130.m:
Brahmā said:
Then the Lord, being pleased, spoke to that sage, O Nārada; / and Āpastamba spoke to Śiva for his own sake and for the sake of others:

130.s:
sarvān kāmān āpnuyus te ye snātvā devam īśvaram
paśyeyur jagatām īśam astv ity āha śivo munim //
130.d:
सर्वान् कामान् आप्नुयुस् ते ये स्नात्वा देवम् ईश्वरम्
पश्येयुर् जगताम् ईशम् अस्त्व् इत्य् आह शिवो मुनिम् ॥
130.m: “May those who bathe and behold the Lord, the god, / the Lord of the worlds, obtain all desires!” Śiva said to the sage: “So be it!”

130.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham āpastambam udāhṛtam
anādy avidyātimiravrātanirmūlanakṣamam //
130.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् आपस्तम्बम् उदाहृतम्
अनाद्य् अविद्यातिमिरव्रातनिर्मूलनक्षमम् ॥
130.m: From then on, that tīrtha has been called Āpastamba, / capable of uprooting the beginningless mass of the darkness of ignorance.

131.s:
brahmovāca
yamatīrtham iti khyātaṃ pitṝṇāṃ prītivardhanam
aśeṣapāpaśamanaṃ tatra vṛttam idaṃ śṛṇu //
131.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यमतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं पितॄणां प्रीतिवर्धनम्
अशेषपापशमनं तत्र वृत्तम् इदं शृणु ॥
131.m: Brahmā said: / Known as Yamatīrtha, it enhances the delight of the ancestors / and pacifies all sins. Listen to what happened there.

131.s:
tatrākhyānam idaṃ tv āsīd itihāsaṃ purātanam
sarameti prasiddhāsti nāmnā devaśunī mune //
131.d:
तत्राख्यानम् इदं त्व् आसीद् इतिहासं पुरातनम्
सरमेति प्रसिद्धास्ति नाम्ना देवशुनी मुने ॥
131.m: Concerning it there was this narrative, an ancient epic history. / There is the famous divine bitch named Saramā, O sage.

131.s:
tasyāḥ putrau mahāśreṣṭhau śvānau nityaṃ janān anu
gāminau pavanāhārau caturakṣau yamapriyau //
131.d:
तस्याः पुत्रौ महाश्रेष्ठौ श्वानौ नित्यं जनान् अनु
गामिनौ पवनाहारौ चतुरक्षौ यमप्रियौ ॥
131.m: Her two very noble sons were dogs, constantly following / people, subsisting on wind, four-eyed, and dear to Yama.

131.s:
gā rakṣati sma devānāṃ yajñārthaṃ kalpitān paśūn
rakṣantīm anujagmus te rākṣasā daityadānavāḥ //
131.d:
गा रक्षति स्म देवानां यज्ञार्थं कल्पितान् पशून्
रक्षन्तीम् अनुजग्मुस् ते राक्षसा दैत्यदानवाः ॥
131.m: She was guarding the cows of the gods, beasts designated for the sacrifice. / As she guarded them, rākṣasas, daityas, and dānavas came after them.

131.s:
rakṣantīṃ tāṃ mahāprājñāḥ śvānayor mātaraṃ śunīm
pralobhayitvā vividhair vākyair dānaiś ca yatnataḥ //
131.d:
रक्षन्तीं तां महाप्राज्ञाः श्वानयोर् मातरं शुनीम्
प्रलोभयित्वा विविधैर् वाक्यैर् दानैश् च यत्नतः ॥
131.m: As she guarded them, O highly wise one, that bitch, the mother of the two dogs, / was enticed by them diligently with various words and gifts.

131.s:
hṛtā gā rākṣasaiḥ pāpaiḥ paśvarthe kalpitāḥ śubhāḥ
tata āgatya sā devān idam āha kramāc chunī //
131.d:
हृता गा राक्षसैः पापैः पश्वर्थे कल्पिताः शुभाः
तत आगत्य सा देवान् इदम् आह क्रमाच् छुनी ॥
131.m: The auspicious cows designated for sacrifice were stolen by the sinful rākṣasas. / Then that bitch came and gradually addressed the gods as follows.

131.s:
saramovāca
māṃ baddhvā rākṣasaiḥ pāśais tāḍayitvā prahārakaiḥ
nītā gā yajñasiddhyarthaṃ kalpitāḥ paśavaḥ surāḥ //
131.d:
सरमोवाच
मां बद्ध्वा राक्षसैः पाशैस् ताडयित्वा प्रहारकैः
नीता गा यज्ञसिद्ध्यर्थं कल्पिताः पशवः सुराः ॥
131.m: Saramā said: / Having bound me with cords and beaten me with blows, / the rākṣasas carried off the cows that were appointed as sacrificial beasts, O gods!

131.s:
brahmovāca
tasyā vācaṃ niśamyāśu surān prāha bṛhaspatiḥ //
131.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तस्या वाचं निशम्याशु सुरान् प्राह बृहस्पतिः ॥
131.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing her words, Bṛhaspati quickly spoke to the gods:

131.s:
bṛhaspatir uvāca
iyaṃ vikṛtarūpāste asyāḥ pāpaṃ ca lakṣaye
asyā matena tā gāvo nītā nānyena hetunā
pāpeyaṃ sukṛtīveti lakṣyate dehaceṣṭitaiḥ //
131.d:
बृहस्पतिर् उवाच
इयं विकृतरूपास्ते अस्याः पापं च लक्षये
अस्या मतेन ता गावो नीता नान्येन हेतुना
पापेयं सुकृतीवेति लक्ष्यते देहचेष्टितैः ॥
131.m: Bṛhaspati said: / She stands here deformed in appearance, and I perceive sin in her. / It was with her consent that those cows were taken, not for any other reason. / She is sinful, though she appears virtuous by her bodily actions.

131.s:
brahmovāca
tad guror vacanāc chakraḥ padā tāṃ prāharac chunīm
padāghātāt tadā tasyā mukhāt kṣīraṃ prasusruve //
131.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् गुरोर् वचनाच् छक्रः पदा तां प्राहरच् छुनीम्
पदाघातात् तदा तस्या मुखात् क्षीरं प्रसुस्रुवे ॥
131.m: Brahmā said: / Then, at the word of his preceptor, Śakra struck the bitch with his foot. / From the kick of his foot, milk then flowed from her mouth.

131.s:
punaḥ prāha śacībhartā kṣīraṃ pītaṃ tvayā śuni
rākṣasaiś ca tadā dattaṃ tasmān nītās tu gā mama //
131.d:
पुनः प्राह शचीभर्ता क्षीरं पीतं त्वया शुनि
राक्षसैश् च तदा दत्तं तस्मान् नीतास् तु गा मम ॥
131.m: Again the husband of Śacī spoke: Milk was drunk by you, O bitch, / and it was given then by the rākṣasas; therefore my cows were taken away!

131.s:
saramovāca
nāparādho 'sti me nātha na cānyasyāpi kasyacit
nāparādho na copekṣā mamāsti tridaśeśvara
tasmād ruṣṭo 'si kiṃ nātha ripavo balinas tu te //
131.d:
सरमोवाच
नापराधो ऽस्ति मे नाथ न चान्यस्यापि कस्यचित्
नापराधो न चोपेक्षा ममास्ति त्रिदशेश्वर
तस्माद् रुष्टो ऽसि किं नाथ रिपवो बलिनस् तु ते ॥
131.m: Saramā said: / There is no fault of mine, O lord, nor of anyone else. / There is neither fault nor neglect on my part, O lord of the thirty [gods]. / Why, then, are you angry, O lord? Your enemies, however, are strong!

131.s:
brahmovāca
tato dhyātvā devagurur jñātvā tasyā viceṣṭitam
satyaṃ śakra tv iyaṃ duṣṭā ripūṇāṃ pakṣakāriṇī //
131.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो ध्यात्वा देवगुरुर् ज्ञात्वा तस्या विचेष्टितम्
सत्यं शक्र त्व् इयं दुष्टा रिपूणां पक्षकारिणी ॥
131.m: Brahmā said: / Then, having meditated and known her conduct, the preceptor of the gods [said]: / Truly, O Śakra, she is wicked, taking the side of the enemies.

131.s:
tataḥ śaśāpa tāṃ śakraḥ pāpiṣṭhe tvaṃ śunī bhava
martyaloke pāpabhūtā ajñānāt pāpakāriṇī //
131.d:
ततः शशाप तां शक्रः पापिष्ठे त्वं शुनी भव
मर्त्यलोके पापभूता अज्ञानात् पापकारिणी ॥
131.m: Then Śakra cursed her: O most sinful one, become a bitch / in the mortal world, having become a sinful creature, doing evil through ignorance!

131.s:
tadendrasya tu śāpena mānuṣe sā vyajāyata
yathā śaptā maghavatā pāpāt sā hy atibhīṣaṇā //
131.d:
तदेन्द्रस्य तु शापेन मानुषे सा व्यजायत
यथा शप्ता मघवता पापात् सा ह्य् अतिभीषणा ॥
131.m: Then, by Indra's curse, she was born among human beings; / as cursed by Maghavat, she became exceedingly frightful due to her sin.

131.s:
gāvo yā rākṣasair nītās tāsām ānayanāya ca
yatnaṃ kurvan surapatir viṣṇave tan nyavedayat //
131.d:
गावो या राक्षसैर् नीतास् तासाम् आनयनाय च
यत्नं कुर्वन् सुरपतिर् विष्णवे तन् न्यवेदयत् ॥
131.m: And making an effort to bring back those cows / which had been taken by the rākṣasas, the lord of the gods reported that to Viṣṇu.

131.s:
viṣṇur daityāṃś ca danujān gohartṝṃś caiva rākṣasān
hantuṃ prayatnam akaroj jagṛhe ca mahad dhanuḥ //
131.d:
विष्णुर् दैत्यांश् च दनुजान् गोहर्तॄंश् चैव राक्षसान्
हन्तुं प्रयत्नम् अकरोज् जगृहे च महद् धनुः ॥
131.m: Viṣṇu made an effort to kill the daityas, danujas, / and cow-stealing rākṣasas, and took up his great bow:

131.s:
śārṅgaṃ yal lokavikhyātaṃ daityanāśanam eva ca
jitāriḥ pūjito devaiḥ svayaṃ sthitvā janārdanaḥ //
131.d:
शार्ङ्गं यल् लोकविख्यातं दैत्यनाशनम् एव च
जितारिः पूजितो देवैः स्वयं स्थित्वा जनार्दनः ॥
131.m: Śārṅga, which is world-renowned and the destroyer of daityas. / Having conquered his foes and worshipped by the gods, Janārdana stood there in person.

131.s:
yatra vai daṇḍakāraṇye śārṅgapāṇir jagatprabhuḥ
tatrasthān daityadanujān rākṣasāṃś ca balīyasaḥ //
131.d:
यत्र वै दण्डकारण्ये शार्ङ्गपाणिर् जगत्प्रभुः
तत्रस्थान् दैत्यदनुजान् राक्षसांश् च बलीयसः ॥
131.m: Where, in the Daṇḍaka Forest, the lord of the world, holding Śārṅga in hand, [stood], / the mighty daityas, danujas, and rākṣasas stationed there—

131.s:
punar jaghne sa vai viṣṇur gā yair nītāś ca rākṣasaiḥ
tatra vai daṇḍakāraṇye śārṅgapāṇir iti śrutaḥ //
131.d:
पुनर् जघ्ने स वै विष्णुर् गा यैर् नीताश् च राक्षसैः
तत्र वै दण्डकारण्ये शार्ङ्गपाणिर् इति श्रुतः ॥
131.m: Viṣṇu once again slew those rākṣasas by whom the cows had been taken. / There indeed in the Daṇḍaka Forest he is famous as Śārṅgapāṇi.

131.s:
yudhyamānas tato viṣṇur ditijai rākṣasaiḥ saha
te jagmur dakṣiṇām āśāṃ viṣṇos trāsān mahāmune //
131.d:
युध्यमानस् ततो विष्णुर् दितिजै राक्षसैः सह
ते जग्मुर् दक्षिणाम् आशां विष्णोस् त्रासान् महामुने ॥
131.m: As Viṣṇu was fighting with the sons of Diti and the rākṣasas, / they fled to the southern direction out of fear of Viṣṇu, O great sage.

131.s:
anvagacchat tato viṣṇus tān eva parameśvaraḥ
garutmatā tān avāpya śārṅgamuktair manojavaiḥ //
131.d:
अन्वगच्छत् ततो विष्णुस् तान् एव परमेश्वरः
गरुत्मता तान् अवाप्य शार्ङ्गमुक्तैर् मनोजवैः ॥
131.m: The supreme lord Viṣṇu then pursued them. / Reaching them by means of Garuḍa, with [arrows] shot from Śārṅga, swift as thought,

131.s:
bāṇais tān vyāhanad viṣṇur gaṅgāyā uttare taṭe
devārayaḥ kṣayaṃ nītā viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā //
131.d:
बाणैस् तान् व्याहनद् विष्णुर् गङ्गाया उत्तरे तटे
देवारयः क्षयं नीता विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ॥
131.m: with arrows Viṣṇu struck them down on the northern bank of the Gaṅgā. / The enemies of the gods were brought to destruction by the mighty Viṣṇu.

131.s:
śārṅgamuktair mahāvegaiḥ susvanaiś ca sumantritaiḥ
kṣayaṃ prāptā viṣṇubāṇais tatas te devaśatravaḥ //
131.d:
शार्ङ्गमुक्तैर् महावेगैः सुस्वनैश् च सुमन्त्रितैः
क्षयं प्राप्ता विष्णुबाणैस् ततस् ते देवशत्रवः ॥
131.m: Shot from Śārṅga, of great speed, resonant, and empowered by mantras, / by the arrows of Viṣṇu those enemies of the gods then met their destruction.

131.s:
gāvo labdhā yatra devair bāṇatīrthaṃ tad ucyate
vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaviditaṃ gotīrthaṃ ceti viśrutam //
131.d:
गावो लब्धा यत्र देवैर् बाणतीर्थं तद् उच्यते
वैष्णवं लोकविदितं गोतीर्थं चेति विश्रुतम् ॥
131.m: Where the cows were recovered by the gods, that is called Bāṇatīrtha, / sacred to Viṣṇu, known in the world, and celebrated as Gotīrtha.

131.s:
paśvarthe kalpitā gāvo gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe
pradrutās te surāḥ sarve gaṅgāyāṃ saṃnyaveśayan //
131.d:
पश्वर्थे कल्पिता गावो गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तटे
प्रद्रुतास् ते सुराः सर्वे गङ्गायां संन्यवेशयन् ॥
131.m: The cows designated for the sacrifice [gathered] on the southern bank of the Gaṅgā; / having run forward, all those gods settled them in the Gaṅgā.

131.s:
tanmadhye kārayām āsur dvīpaṃ caivāśrayaṃ gavām
tair gobhis tatra gaṅgāyāṃ surayajño vyajāyata //
131.d:
तन्मध्ये कारयाम् आसुर् द्वीपं चैवाश्रयं गवाम्
तैर् गोभिस् तत्र गङ्गायां सुरयज्ञो व्यजायत ॥
131.m: In the midst of it they had an island made as a shelter for the cows. / With those cows, a sacrifice of the gods took place there in the Gaṅgā.

131.s:
yajñatīrthaṃ tu tat proktaṃ godvīpaṃ gāṅgamadhyataḥ
devānāṃ yajanaṃ tac ca sarvakāmapradaṃ śubham //
131.d:
यज्ञतीर्थं तु तत् प्रोक्तं गोद्वीपं गाङ्गमध्यतः
देवानां यजनं तच् च सर्वकामप्रदं शुभम् ॥
131.m: That is proclaimed as Yajñatīrtha, an island of cows in the middle of the Gaṅgā; / and it is a place of sacrifice for the gods, auspicious and granting all desires.

131.s:
svayaṃ mūrtimatī bhūtvā gaṅgāśaktir mahādyute
asārāpārasaṃsārasāgarottaraṇe tariḥ //
131.d:
स्वयं मूर्तिमती भूत्वा गङ्गाशक्तिर् महाद्युते
असारापारसंसारसागरोत्तरणे तरिः ॥
131.m: She herself assumed a physical form, the power of Gaṅgā, O one of great splendor, / a boat for crossing the boundless, worthless ocean of saṃsāra,

131.s:
viśveśvarī yogamāyā sadbhaktābhayadāyinī
gorakṣaṃ tu tatas tīrthaṃ gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe //
131.d:
विश्वेश्वरी योगमाया सद्भक्ताभयदायिनी
गोरक्षं तु ततस् तीर्थं गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तटे ॥
131.m: the ruler of the universe, Yogamāyā, bestowing fearlessness upon true devotees. / Thence there is the Gorakṣa tīrtha on the southern bank of the Gaṅgā.

131.s:
tau śvānau saramāputrau caturakṣau yamapriyau
mātuḥ śāpaṃ cāparādhaṃ sarvaṃ cāpi savistaram //
131.d:
तौ श्वानौ सरमापुत्रौ चतुरक्षौ यमप्रियौ
मातुः शापं चापराधं सर्वं चापि सविस्तरम् ॥
131.m: Those two dogs, the sons of Saramā, four-eyed and dear to Yama, / [reported] their mother's curse and transgression, indeed everything in full detail.

131.s:
nivedya tu yathānyāyaṃ kāryaṃ cāpi sukhapradam
viśāpakaraṇaṃ cāpi papracchatur ubhau yamam //
131.d:
निवेद्य तु यथान्यायं कार्यं चापि सुखप्रदम्
विशापकरणं चापि पप्रच्छतुर् उभौ यमम् ॥
131.m: Having reported it properly, and also the measure that would bring happiness / and the removal of the curse, both questioned Yama.

131.s:
sa tābhyāṃ sahitaḥ sauriḥ pitre sūryāya cābravīt
śrutvā sūryaḥ sutaṃ prāha gaṅgāyāṃ surasattama //
131.d:
स ताभ्यां सहितः सौरिः पित्रे सूर्याय चाब्रवीत्
श्रुत्वा सूर्यः सुतं प्राह गङ्गायां सुरसत्तम ॥
131.m: Accompanied by the two, Yama, the son of Sūrya, spoke to his father, the sun. / Having heard, Sūrya said to his son: At the Gaṅgā, O best of gods,

131.s:
lokatrayaikapāvanyāṃ gautamyāṃ daṇḍake vane
śraddhayā parayā vatsa susnātaḥ susamāhitaḥ //
131.d:
लोकत्रयैकपावन्यां गौतम्यां दण्डके वने
श्रद्धया परया वत्स सुस्नातः सुसमाहितः ॥
131.m: at the Gautamī in the Daṇḍaka forest, the sole purifier of the three worlds, / with supreme faith, my child, well-bathed and well-composed,

131.s:
brahmāṇaṃ caiva viṣṇuṃ ca mām īśaṃ ca yathākramam
stuhi tvaṃ sarvabhāvena bhṛtyau prītim avāpsyataḥ //
131.d:
ब्रह्माणं चैव विष्णुं च माम् ईशं च यथाक्रमम्
स्तुहि त्वं सर्वभावेन भृत्यौ प्रीतिम् अवाप्स्यतः ॥
131.m: praise Brahmā, Viṣṇu, myself, and Śiva in due order / with your whole being; the two servants will attain satisfaction.

131.s:
tat pitur vacanaṃ śrutvā yamaḥ prītamanās tadā
tayoś ca prītaye prāyād devatarpaṇayor yamaḥ //
131.d:
तत् पितुर् वचनं श्रुत्वा यमः प्रीतमनास् तदा
तयोश् च प्रीतये प्रायाद् देवतर्पणयोर् यमः ॥
131.m: Hearing those words of his father, Yama was then delighted in mind; / and for their satisfaction, Yama went to perform the libations to the gods.

131.s:
gautamyām aghahāriṇyāṃ susamāhitamānasaḥ
tathaiva toṣayām āsa gaṅgāyāṃ surasattamān //
131.d:
गौतम्याम् अघहारिण्यां सुसमाहितमानसः
तथैव तोषयाम् आस गङ्गायां सुरसत्तमान् ॥
131.m: At the Gautamī that removes sin, with a well-composed mind, / he pleased the best of gods at the Gaṅgā in that very manner.

131.s:
śvabhyāṃ ca sahitaḥ śrīmān dakṣiṇāśāpatiḥ prabhuḥ
brahmāṇaṃ toṣayām āsa bhānuṃ vai dakṣiṇe taṭe //
131.d:
श्वभ्यां च सहितः श्रीमान् दक्षिणाशापतिः प्रभुः
ब्रह्माणं तोषयाम् आस भानुं वै दक्षिणे तटे ॥
131.m: Accompanied by the two dogs, the glorious lord, the ruler of the southern quarter, / pleased Brahmā and the sun on the southern bank,

131.s:
īśānam uttare viṣṇuṃ svayaṃ dharmaḥ pratāpavān
dattavanto varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ saramāyā viśāpakam
varān ayācata bahūṃl lokānām upakārakān //
131.d:
ईशानम् उत्तरे विष्णुं स्वयं धर्मः प्रतापवान्
दत्तवन्तो वरं श्रेष्ठं सरमाया विशापकम्
वरान् अयाचत बहूंल् लोकानाम् उपकारकान् ॥
131.m: and Śiva and Viṣṇu on the northern [bank], he being the glorious Dharma personified. / They granted an excellent boon removing Saramā's curse; / he asked for many boons beneficial to the worlds.

131.s:
yama uvāca
eṣu snānaṃ tu ye kuryur brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ
ātmārthaṃ ca parārthaṃ ca te kāmān āpnuyuḥ śubhān //
131.d:
यम उवाच
एषु स्नानं तु ये कुर्युर् ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः
आत्मार्थं च परार्थं च ते कामान् आप्नुयुः शुभान् ॥
131.m: Yama said: / O Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, those who bathe in these [tīrthas], / for their own sake or for the sake of another, may they attain auspicious desires!

131.s:
bāṇatīrthe tu ye snātvā śārṅgapāṇiṃ smaranti vai
tebhyo dāridryaduḥkhāni na bhaveyur yuge yuge //
131.d:
बाणतीर्थे तु ये स्नात्वा शार्ङ्गपाणिं स्मरन्ति वै
तेभ्यो दारिद्र्यदुःखानि न भवेयुर् युगे युगे ॥
131.m: Those who bathe at Bāṇatīrtha and remember the one who holds Śārṅga in hand, / to them may there be no miseries of poverty in age after age!

131.s:
gotīrthe brahmatīrthe vā yas tu snātvā yatavrataḥ
brahmāṇaṃ taṃ namasyātha dvīpasyāpi pradakṣiṇam //
131.d:
गोतीर्थे ब्रह्मतीर्थे वा यस् तु स्नात्वा यतव्रतः
ब्रह्माणं तं नमस्याथ द्वीपस्यापि प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
131.m: He who, having bathed at Gotīrtha or Brahmatīrtha, restrained in vows, / having bowed to that Brahmā, then performs circumambulation of the island—

131.s:
yaḥ kuryāt tena pṛthivī saptadvīpā vasuṃdharā
pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tatra kiṃcid dattvā vasu dvijam //
131.d:
यः कुर्यात् तेन पृथिवी सप्तद्वीपा वसुंधरा
प्रदक्षिणीकृता तत्र किंचिद् दत्त्वा वसु द्विजम् ॥
131.m: by him the earth with its seven islands, the bearer of wealth, is circumambulated. / Having given some wealth there to a twice-born,

131.s:
tad devayajanaṃ prāpya kiṃcid dhutvā hutāśane
aśvamedhādiyajñānāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti puṣkalam //
131.d:
तद् देवयजनं प्राप्य किंचिद् धुत्वा हुताशने
अश्वमेधादियज्ञानां फलं प्राप्नोति पुष्कलम् ॥
131.m: and reaching that place of divine sacrifice and offering something into the fire, / he obtains the abundant fruit of sacrifices such as the horse-sacrifice.

131.s:
yaḥ sakṛt tatra paṭhati gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram
adhītās tena vedā vai niṣkāmo muktibhājanam //
131.d:
यः सकृत् तत्र पठति गायत्रीं वेदमातरम्
अधीतास् तेन वेदा वै निष्कामो मुक्तिभाजनम् ॥
131.m: He who recites once there the Gāyatrī, the mother of the Vedas, / by him the Vedas have indeed been studied; free of desire, he becomes a vessel of liberation.

131.s:
snātvā tu dakṣiṇe kūle śaktiṃ devīṃ tu bhaktitaḥ
pūjayitvā yathānyāyaṃ sarvān kāmān avāpnuyāt //
131.d:
स्नात्वा तु दक्षिणे कूले शक्तिं देवीं तु भक्तितः
पूजयित्वा यथान्यायं सर्वान् कामान् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
131.m: Having bathed on the southern bank and worshipped goddess Śakti with devotion / in accordance with the proper rule, one obtains all desires.

131.s:
brahmaviṣṇumaheśānāṃ śaktir mātā trayīmayī
sarvān kāmān avāpnoti putravān dhanavān bhavet //
131.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशानां शक्तिर् माता त्रयीमयी
सर्वान् कामान् अवाप्नोति पुत्रवान् धनवान् भवेत् ॥
131.m: She is the power, the mother of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa, consisting of the three Vedas; / [worshipping her,] one obtains all desires, and becomes rich and endowed with sons.

131.s:
ādityaṃ bhaktito yas tu dakṣiṇe niyato naraḥ
snātvā paśyeta teneṣṭā yajñā vividhadakṣiṇāḥ //
131.d:
आदित्यं भक्तितो यस् तु दक्षिणे नियतो नरः
स्नात्वा पश्येत तेनेष्टा यज्ञा विविधदक्षिणाः ॥
131.m: And whatever disciplined man, having bathed, beholds the sun with devotion / on the southern [bank], by him sacrifices with various sacrificial fees have been performed.

131.s:
kūle yaś cottare caiva gaṅgāyā daityasūdanam
snātvā paśyeta taṃ natvā tasya viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam //
131.d:
कूले यश् चोत्तरे चैव गङ्गाया दैत्यसूदनम्
स्नात्वा पश्येत तं नत्वा तस्य विष्णोः परं पदम् ॥
131.m: And whoever, having bathed on the northern bank of the Gaṅgā, beholds the slayer of the Daityas / and bows to him, his is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

131.s:
yameśvaraṃ tato yas tu yamatīrthe tu pūjitam
snātaḥ paśyati yuktātmā sa karoty acireṇa hi //
131.d:
यमेश्वरं ततो यस् तु यमतीर्थे तु पूजितम्
स्नातः पश्यति युक्तात्मा स करोत्य् अचिरेण हि ॥
131.m: Then, whoever, self-composed and having bathed, beholds Yameśvara / worshipped at Yamatīrtha, he soon produces indeed

131.s:
pitṝṇām akṣayaṃ puṇyaṃ phaladaṃ kīrtivardhanam
tatra snānena dānena japena stavanena ca
api duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ pitaro mokṣam āpnuyuḥ //
131.d:
पितॄणाम् अक्षयं पुण्यं फलदं कीर्तिवर्धनम्
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन जपेन स्तवनेन च
अपि दुष्कृतकर्माणः पितरो मोक्षम् आप्नुयुः ॥
131.m: imperishable merit that yields fruit and increases fame for the ancestors; / by bathing, making gifts, murmuring prayers, and praising there, / even ancestors of wicked deeds would attain liberation.

131.s:
brahmovāca
ityādy aṣṭa sahasrāṇi tīrthāni trīṇi nārada
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca sarvam akṣayapuṇyadam //
131.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्याद्य् अष्ट सहस्राणि तीर्थानि त्रीणि नारद
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च सर्वम् अक्षयपुण्यदम् ॥
131.m: Brahmā said: / In this way there are eight thousand and three tīrthas, O Nārada; / bathing and making gifts in them yields entirely imperishable merit.

131.s:
eteṣāṃ smaraṇaṃ puṇyaṃ nānājanmāghanāśanam
śravaṇāt pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ paṭhanāt svakulaiḥ saha //
131.d:
एतेषां स्मरणं पुण्यं नानाजन्माघनाशनम्
श्रवणात् पितृभिः सार्धं पठनात् स्वकुलैः सह ॥
131.m: The remembrance of these is meritorious, destroying the sins of diverse births; / through hearing [of them] along with one's ancestors, and through reciting [them] together with one's own family,

131.s:
teṣām apy atipāpāni nāśaṃ yānti mamājñayā
tatra snānādi yaḥ kṛtvā kiṃcid dattvā yatātmavān //
131.d:
तेषाम् अप्य् अतिपापानि नाशं यान्ति ममाज्ञया
तत्र स्नानादि यः कृत्वा किंचिद् दत्त्वा यतात्मवान् ॥
131.m: even their extreme sins go to destruction by my command; / having performed bathing and other rites there, and having given something with self-restraint,

131.s:
pitṝṇāṃ piṇḍadānādi kṛtvā natvā surān imān
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ yaśo vīryam āyur ārogyasaṃpadaḥ //
131.d:
पितॄणां पिण्डदानादि कृत्वा नत्वा सुरान् इमान्
धनं धान्यं यशो वीर्यम् आयुर् आरोग्यसंपदः ॥
