131.m: having offered rice balls and other rites for the ancestors, and having bowed to these gods, / [one obtains] wealth, grain, fame, strength, long life, and the treasures of health;

131.s:
putrān pautrān priyāṃ bhāryāṃ labdhvā cānyan manīṣitam
aviyuktaḥ prītamanā bandhubhiś cātimānitaḥ //
131.d:
पुत्रान् पौत्रान् प्रियां भार्यां लब्ध्वा चान्यन् मनीषितम्
अवियुक्तः प्रीतमना बन्धुभिश् चातिमानितः ॥
131.m: having obtained sons, grandsons, a beloved wife, and whatever else is desired, / unseparated [from them], cheerful in mind, and greatly honored by kinsmen,

131.s:
narakasthān api pitṝṃs tārayitvā kulāni ca
pāvayitvā priyair yukto hy ante viṣṇuṃ śivaṃ smaret
tato muktipadaṃ gacched devānāṃ vacanaṃ yathā //
131.d:
नरकस्थान् अपि पितॄंस् तारयित्वा कुलानि च
पावयित्वा प्रियैर् युक्तो ह्य् अन्ते विष्णुं शिवं स्मरेत्
ततो मुक्तिपदं गच्छेद् देवानां वचनं यथा ॥
131.m: having delivered even the ancestors residing in hell and purified his lineages, / united with beloved ones, he should remember Viṣṇu and Śiva at the end; / then he will go to the state of liberation, just as is the word of the gods.

132.s:
brahmovāca
yakṣiṇīsaṃgamaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ sarvaphalapradam
tatra snānena dānena sarvān kāmān avāpnuyāt //
132.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यक्षिणीसंगमं नाम तीर्थं सर्वफलप्रदम्
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन सर्वान् कामान् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
132.m: Brahmā said: / The tīrtha named Yakṣiṇīsaṃgama grants all fruits; / by bathing and making gifts there, one obtains all desires.

132.s:
yatra yakṣeśvaro devo darśanād bhuktimuktidaḥ
tatra ca snānamātreṇa sattrayāgaphalaṃ labhet //
132.d:
यत्र यक्षेश्वरो देवो दर्शनाद् भुक्तिमुक्तिदः
तत्र च स्नानमात्रेण सत्त्रयागफलं लभेत् ॥
132.m: Where Lord Yakṣeśvara, through sight of him, grants worldly enjoyment and liberation, / there, by mere bathing, one obtains the fruit of a sacrificial session.

132.s:
viśvāvasoḥ svasā nāmnā pippalā guruhāsinī
ṛṣīṇāṃ sattram agamad gautamītīravartinām //
132.d:
विश्वावसोः स्वसा नाम्ना पिप्पला गुरुहासिनी
ऋषीणां सत्त्रम् अगमद् गौतमीतीरवर्तिनाम् ॥
132.m: The sister of Viśvāvasu named Pippalā, who laughed loudly, / went to a sacrificial session of sages who dwelled on the banks of the Gautamī.

132.s:
dṛṣṭvā tatra ṛṣīn kṣāmān sā jahāsātigarvitā
yā gatvāśrāvaya vauṣaḍ astu śrauṣaḍ iti sthiram //
132.d:
दृष्ट्वा तत्र ऋषीन् क्षामान् सा जहासातिगर्विता
या गत्वाश्रावय वौषड् अस्तु श्रौषड् इति स्थिरम् ॥
132.m: Seeing the emaciated sages there, she laughed, exceedingly haughty; / going there, she called out loudly, 'Let there be vauṣaṭ, let there be śrauṣaṭ,'

132.s:
visvareṇa bruvatī tāṃ te śepuḥ srāviṇī bhava
tato nady abhavat tatra yakṣiṇīti suviśrutā //
132.d:
विस्वरेण ब्रुवती तां ते शेपुः स्राविणी भव
ततो नद्य् अभवत् तत्र यक्षिणीति सुविश्रुता ॥
132.m: speaking discordantly; they cursed her: 'Become a flowing stream!' / Then she became a river there, well known as the Yakṣiṇī.

132.s:
tato viśvāvasuḥ pūjya ṛṣīn devaṃ trilocanam
saṃgamya caiva gautamyā tāṃ viśāpām athākarot //
132.d:
ततो विश्वावसुः पूज्य ऋषीन् देवं त्रिलोचनम्
संगम्य चैव गौतम्या तां विशापाम् अथाकरोत् ॥
132.m: Then Viśvāvasu, having worshipped the sages and the three-eyed god, / and having joined her with the Gautamī, released her from the curse.

132.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ yakṣiṇīsaṃgamaṃ smṛtam
tatra snānādidānena sarvān kāmān avāpnuyāt //
132.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं यक्षिणीसंगमं स्मृतम्
तत्र स्नानादिदानेन सर्वान् कामान् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
132.m: From that time forward that tīrtha has been known as Yakṣiṇīsaṃgama; / by bathing, making gifts, and other rites there, one obtains all desires.

132.s:
viśvāvasoḥ prasanno 'bhūd yatra śaṃbhuḥ śivānvitaḥ
śaivaṃ tat paramaṃ tīrthaṃ durgātīrthaṃ ca viśrutam //
132.d:
विश्वावसोः प्रसन्नो ऽभूद् यत्र शंभुः शिवान्वितः
शैवं तत् परमं तीर्थं दुर्गातीर्थं च विश्रुतम् ॥
132.m: Where Śambhu, accompanied by Śivā, became pleased with Viśvāvasu, / that supreme tīrtha of Śiva is famous as Durgātīrtha.

132.s:
sarvapāpaughaharaṇaṃ sarvadurgatināśanam
sarveṣāṃ tīrthamukhyānāṃ tad dhi sāraṃ mahāmune
tīrthaṃ munivaraiḥ khyātaṃ sarvasiddhipradaṃ nṛṇām //
132.d:
सर्वपापौघहरणं सर्वदुर्गतिनाशनम्
सर्वेषां तीर्थमुख्यानां तद् धि सारं महामुने
तीर्थं मुनिवरैः ख्यातं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदं नृणाम् ॥
132.m: It takes away the flood of all sins, and destroys all misfortune; / of all chief tīrthas it is indeed the essence, O great sage; / it is a tīrtha celebrated by the best of sages, granting all accomplishments to mortals.

133.s:
brahmovāca
śuklatīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvasiddhikaraṃ nṛṇām
yasya smaraṇamātreṇa sarvakāmān avāpnuyāt //
133.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शुक्लतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं सर्वसिद्धिकरं नृणाम्
यस्य स्मरणमात्रेण सर्वकामान् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
133.m: Brahmā said: / The tīrtha famous as Śuklatīrtha brings all accomplishments to mortals; / by mere remembrance of it, one obtains all desires.

133.s:
bharadvāja iti khyāto muniḥ paramadhārmikaḥ
tasya paiṭhīnasī nāma bhāryā sukalabhūṣaṇā //
133.d:
भरद्वाज इति ख्यातो मुनिः परमधार्मिकः
तस्य पैठीनसी नाम भार्या सुकलभूषणा ॥
133.m: There was a most righteous sage known as Bharadvāja; / he had a wife named Paiṭhīnasī, adorned with lovely arts.

133.s:
gautamītīram adhyāste pativrataparāyaṇā
agnīṣomīyam aindrāgnaṃ puroḍāśam akalpayat //
133.d:
गौतमीतीरम् अध्यास्ते पतिव्रतपरायणा
अग्नीषोमीयम् ऐन्द्राग्नं पुरोडाशम् अकल्पयत् ॥
133.m: Devoted to her husband, she dwelt on the bank of the Gautamī; / she prepared the sacrificial cake dedicated to Agni and Soma, and that dedicated to Indra and Agni.

133.s:
puroḍāśe śrapyamāṇe dhūmāt kaścid ajāyata
puroḍāśaṃ bhakṣayitvā lokatritayabhīṣaṇaḥ //
133.d:
पुरोडाशे श्रप्यमाणे धूमात् कश्चिद् अजायत
पुरोडाशं भक्षयित्वा लोकत्रितयभीषणः ॥
133.m: While the sacrificial cake was being cooked, someone was born from the smoke; / he ate the sacrificial cake, terrifying to the three worlds.

133.s:
yajñaṃ me hy atra ko haṃsi kopāt tvam iti taṃ muniḥ
provāca satvaraṃ kruddho bharadvājo dvijottamaḥ
tad ṛṣer vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasaḥ pratyuvāca tam //
133.d:
यज्ञं मे ह्य् अत्र को हंसि कोपात् त्वम् इति तं मुनिः
प्रोवाच सत्वरं क्रुद्धो भरद्वाजो द्विजोत्तमः
तद् ऋषेर् वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसः प्रत्युवाच तम् ॥
133.m: 'Who are you that destroy my sacrifice here in wrath?' / The enraged sage Bharadvāja, best of the twice-born, swiftly spoke to him; / hearing those words of the sage, the rākṣasa replied to him.

133.s:
rākṣasa uvāca
havyaghna iti vikhyātaṃ bharadvāja nibodha mām
saṃdhyāsuto 'haṃ jyeṣṭhaś ca sutaḥ prācīnabarhiṣaḥ //
133.d:
राक्षस उवाच
हव्यघ्न इति विख्यातं भरद्वाज निबोध माम्
संध्यासुतो ऽहं ज्येष्ठश् च सुतः प्राचीनबर्हिषः ॥
133.m: The rākṣasa said: / Know me, O Bharadvāja, as celebrated by the name Havyaghna; / I am the son of Saṃdhyā, and the eldest son of Prācīnabarhis.

133.s:
brahmaṇā me varo datto yajñān khāda yathāsukham
mamānujaḥ kaliś cāpi balavān atibhīṣaṇaḥ //
133.d:
ब्रह्मणा मे वरो दत्तो यज्ञान् खाद यथासुखम्
ममानुजः कलिश् चापि बलवान् अतिभीषणः ॥
133.m: A boon was given to me by Brahmā: 'Consume sacrifices as you please'; / and my younger brother Kali is also mighty and exceedingly terrifying.

133.s:
ahaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ pitā kṛṣṇo mātā kṛṣṇā tathānujaḥ
ahaṃ makhaṃ haniṣyāmi yūpaṃ chedmi kṛtāntakaḥ //
133.d:
अहं कृष्णः पिता कृष्णो माता कृष्णा तथानुजः
अहं मखं हनिष्यामि यूपं छेद्मि कृतान्तकः ॥
133.m: I am black, my father is black, my mother is black, and so is my younger brother; / I will destroy the sacrifice and cut down the sacrificial post, being Death itself.

133.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
rakṣyatāṃ me tvayā yajñaḥ priyo dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
jāne tvāṃ yajñahantāraṃ saddvijaṃ rakṣa me kratum //
133.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
रक्ष्यतां मे त्वया यज्ञः प्रियो धर्मः सनातनः
जाने त्वां यज्ञहन्तारं सद्द्विजं रक्ष मे क्रतुम् ॥
133.m: Bharadvāja said: / Let my sacrifice be protected by you; the eternal dharma is dear [to me]; / I know you to be a destroyer of sacrifices; protect my rite, [O you who are now] a good twice-born!

133.s:
yajñaghna uvāca
bharadvāja nibodhedaṃ vākyaṃ mama samāsataḥ
brahmaṇāhaṃ purā śapto devadānavasaṃnidhau //
133.d:
यज्ञघ्न उवाच
भरद्वाज निबोधेदं वाक्यं मम समासतः
ब्रह्मणाहं पुरा शप्तो देवदानवसंनिधौ ॥
133.m: The sacrifice-destroyer said: / Understand these words of mine in brief, O Bharadvāja: / formerly I was cursed by Brahmā in the presence of the gods and Dānavas.

133.s:
tataḥ prasādito devo mayā lokapitāmahaḥ
amṛtaiḥ prokṣayiṣyanti yadā tvāṃ munisattamāḥ //
133.d:
ततः प्रसादितो देवो मया लोकपितामहः
अमृतैः प्रोक्षयिष्यन्ति यदा त्वां मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
133.m: Then the god, the grandfather of the worlds, was propitiated by me: / 'When the best of sages sprinkle you with nectars,

133.s:
tadā viśāpo bhavitā havyaghna tvaṃ na cānyathā
evaṃ kariṣyasi yadā tataḥ sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati //
133.d:
तदा विशापो भविता हव्यघ्न त्वं न चान्यथा
एवं करिष्यसि यदा ततः सर्वं भविष्यति ॥
133.m: then, O Havyaghna, you will be freed from the curse, and not otherwise; / when you do this, then all will come to pass.'

133.s:
brahmovāca
bharadvājaḥ punaḥ prāha sakhā me 'si mahāmate
makhasaṃrakṣaṇaṃ yena syān me vada karomi tat //
133.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
भरद्वाजः पुनः प्राह सखा मे ऽसि महामते
मखसंरक्षणं येन स्यान् मे वद करोमि तत् ॥
133.m: Brahmā said: / Bharadvāja said again, 'You are my friend, O noble-minded one; / tell me that by which the protection of my sacrifice may be achieved, and I shall do it.

133.s:
saṃbhūya devā daiteyā mamanthuḥ kṣīrasāgaram
alabhantāmṛtaṃ kaṣṭāt tad asmatsulabhaṃ katham //
133.d:
संभूय देवा दैतेया ममन्थुः क्षीरसागरम्
अलभन्तामृतं कष्टात् तद् अस्मत्सुलभं कथम् ॥
133.m: The gods and sons of Diti, joining together, churned the ocean of milk; / with difficulty they obtained nectar; how can that be easily obtained by us?

133.s:
prītyā yadi prasanno 'si sulabhaṃ yad vadasva tat
tad ṛṣer vacanaṃ śrutvā rakṣaḥ prāha tadā mudā //
133.d:
प्रीत्या यदि प्रसन्नो ऽसि सुलभं यद् वदस्व तत्
तद् ऋषेर् वचनं श्रुत्वा रक्षः प्राह तदा मुदा ॥
133.m: If you are favorably disposed out of affection, tell me what is easily obtainable.' / Hearing the sage's words, the demon then joyfully replied.

133.s:
rakṣa uvāca
amṛtaṃ gautamīvāri amṛtaṃ svarṇam ucyate
amṛtaṃ gobhavaṃ cājyam amṛtaṃ soma eva ca //
133.d:
रक्ष उवाच
अमृतं गौतमीवारि अमृतं स्वर्णम् उच्यते
अमृतं गोभवं चाज्यम् अमृतं सोम एव च ॥
133.m: The demon said: / The water of the Gautamī is nectar, gold is called nectar, / ghee produced from cows is nectar, and soma itself is nectar.

133.s:
etair mām abhiṣiñcasva athavaitais tathā tribhiḥ
gaṅgāyā vāriṇājyena hiraṇyena tathaiva ca
sarvebhyo 'py adhikaṃ divyam amṛtaṃ gautamījalam //
133.d:
एतैर् माम् अभिषिञ्चस्व अथवैतैस् तथा त्रिभिः
गङ्गाया वारिणाज्येन हिरण्येन तथैव च
सर्वेभ्यो ऽप्य् अधिकं दिव्यम् अमृतं गौतमीजलम् ॥
133.m: Sprinkle me with these, or else with these three: / with the water of the Gaṅgā, with ghee, and likewise with gold; / superior even to all of them is the divine nectar, the water of the Gautamī.

133.s:
brahmovāca
etad ākarṇya sa ṛṣiḥ paraṃ saṃtoṣam āgataḥ
pāṇāv ādāya gaṅgāyāḥ salilāmṛtam ādarāt //
133.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतद् आकर्ण्य स ऋषिः परं संतोषम् आगतः
पाणाव् आदाय गङ्गायाः सलिलामृतम् आदरात् ॥
133.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing this, the sage attained supreme satisfaction; / taking in his hand the nectar-water of the Gaṅgā with reverence,

133.s:
tenākarod ṛṣī rakṣo hy abhiṣiktaṃ tadā makhe
punaś ca yūpe ca paśāv ṛtvikṣu makhamaṇḍale //
133.d:
तेनाकरोद् ऋषी रक्षो ह्य् अभिषिक्तं तदा मखे
पुनश् च यूपे च पशाव् ऋत्विक्षु मखमण्डले ॥
133.m: the sage then sprinkled the demon during the sacrifice with it, / and again upon the post, the sacrificial victim, the priests, and the sacrificial arena.

133.s:
sarvam evābhavac chuklam abhiṣekān mahātmanaḥ
tad rakṣo 'pi tadā śuklo bhūtvotpanno mahābalaḥ //
133.d:
सर्वम् एवाभवच् छुक्लम् अभिषेकान् महात्मनः
तद् रक्षो ऽपि तदा शुक्लो भूत्वोत्पन्नो महाबलः ॥
133.m: Everything indeed became white through the consecration by the great-souled [sage]; / that demon too, having become white, then arose possessed of great strength.

133.s:
yaḥ purā kṛṣṇarūpo 'bhūt sa tu śuklo 'bhavat kṣaṇāt
yajñaṃ sarvaṃ samāpyātha bharadvājaḥ pratāpavān //
133.d:
यः पुरा कृष्णरूपो ऽभूत् स तु शुक्लो ऽभवत् क्षणात्
यज्ञं सर्वं समाप्याथ भरद्वाजः प्रतापवान् ॥
133.m: He who formerly was black in form became white in an instant; / then, having concluded the entire sacrifice, the glorious Bharadvāja,

133.s:
ṛtvijo 'pi visṛjyātha yūpaṃ gaṅgodake 'kṣipat
gaṅgāmadhye tad dhi yūpam adyāpy āste mahāmate //
133.d:
ऋत्विजो ऽपि विसृज्याथ यूपं गङ्गोदके ऽक्षिपत्
गङ्गामध्ये तद् धि यूपम् अद्याप्य् आस्ते महामते ॥
133.m: having dismissed the priests, threw the sacrificial post into the water of the Gaṅgā; / and that sacrificial post remains in the middle of the Gaṅgā even today, O noble-minded one.

133.s:
abhiṣiktaṃ cāmṛtena abhijñānaṃ tu tan mahat
tatra tīrthe punā rakṣo bharadvājam uvāca ha //
133.d:
अभिषिक्तं चामृतेन अभिज्ञानं तु तन् महत्
तत्र तीर्थे पुना रक्षो भरद्वाजम् उवाच ह ॥
133.m: Sprinkled with nectar, it is indeed a great token of recognition; / at that tīrtha, the purified demon spoke to Bharadvāja:

133.s:
rakṣa uvāca
ahaṃ yāmi bharadvāja kṛtaḥ śuklas tvayā punaḥ
tasmāt tavātra tīrthe ye snānadānādipūjanam //
133.d:
रक्ष उवाच
अहं यामि भरद्वाज कृतः शुक्लस् त्वया पुनः
तस्मात् तवात्र तीर्थे ये स्नानदानादिपूजनम् ॥
133.m:
The rakṣasa said:
I am departing, O Bharadvāja; I have been made bright again by you.
Therefore, whoever in this tīrtha of yours performs bathing, gifts, worship, and the like,

133.s:
kuryus teṣām abhīṣṭāni bhaveyur yat phalaṃ makhe
smaraṇād api pāpāni nāśaṃ yāntu sadā mune //
133.d:
कुर्युस् तेषाम् अभीष्टानि भवेयुर् यत् फलं मखे
स्मरणाद् अपि पापानि नाशं यान्तु सदा मुने ॥
133.m:
may their desires be fulfilled, with the fruit that is gained in a sacrifice!
Even from remembering it, O sage, may sins always be destroyed!

133.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ śuklatīrtham iti smṛtam
gautamyāṃ daṇḍakāraṇye svargadvāram apāvṛtam //
133.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं शुक्लतीर्थम् इति स्मृतम्
गौतम्यां दण्डकारण्ये स्वर्गद्वारम् अपावृतम् ॥
133.m:
From that time forward, that tīrtha has been renowned as Śuklatīrtha,
an open gate to heaven on the Gautamī in the Daṇḍaka Forest.

133.s:
ubhayos tīrayoḥ sapta sahasrāṇy aparāṇi ca
tīrthānāṃ muniśārdūla sarvasiddhipradāyinām //
133.d:
उभयोस् तीरयोः सप्त सहस्राण्य् अपराणि च
तीर्थानां मुनिशार्दूल सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायिनाम् ॥
133.m:
On both banks there are another seven thousand
tīrthas, O tiger among sages, that grant all attainments.

134.s:
brahmovāca
cakratīrtham iti khyātaṃ smaraṇāt pāpanāśanam
tasya prabhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu yatnena nārada //
134.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
चक्रतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं स्मरणात् पापनाशनम्
तस्य प्रभावं वक्ष्यामि शृणु यत्नेन नारद ॥
134.m:
Brahmā said:
There is a place known as Cakratīrtha, destroying sins by its very remembrance.
I shall tell you its power; listen attentively, O Nārada.

134.s:
ṛṣayaḥ sapta vikhyātā vasiṣṭhapramukhā mune
gautamyās tīram āśritya sattrayajñam upāsate //
134.d:
ऋषयः सप्त विख्याता वसिष्ठप्रमुखा मुने
गौतम्यास् तीरम् आश्रित्य सत्त्रयज्ञम् उपासते ॥
134.m:
Seven celebrated sages, headed by Vasiṣṭha, O sage,
resorted to the bank of the Gautamī and undertook a sacrificial session.

134.s:
tatra vighna upakrānte rakṣobhir atibhīṣaṇe
mām abhyetyātha munayo rakṣaḥkṛtyaṃ nyavedayan //
134.d:
तत्र विघ्न उपक्रान्ते रक्षोभिर् अतिभीषणे
माम् अभ्येत्याथ मुनयो रक्षःकृत्यं न्यवेदयन् ॥
134.m:
When a very terrifying obstruction was initiated there by rakṣasas,
the sages came to me and reported the deed of the rakṣasas.

134.s:
tadāhaṃ pramadārūpaṃ māyayāsṛjya nārada
yasyāś ca darśanād eva nāśaṃ yānty atha rākṣasāḥ //
134.d:
तदाहं प्रमदारूपं माययासृज्य नारद
यस्याश् च दर्शनाद् एव नाशं यान्त्य् अथ राक्षसाः ॥
134.m:
Then, O Nārada, I created by illusory power the form of a beautiful woman,
at the mere sight of whom the rākṣasas would be destroyed.

134.s:
evam uktvā tu tāṃ prādām ṛṣibhyaḥ pramadāṃ mune
madvākyād ṛṣayo māyām ādāya punar āgaman //
134.d:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु तां प्रादाम् ऋषिभ्यः प्रमदां मुने
मद्वाक्याद् ऋषयो मायाम् आदाय पुनर् आगमन् ॥
134.m:
Having spoken thus, I gave that woman to the sages, O sage.
At my word, the sages took the illusory form and returned.

134.s:
ajaikā yā samākhyātā kṛṣṇalohitarūpiṇī
muktakeśīty abhidhayā sāste 'dyāpi svarūpiṇī //
134.d:
अजैका या समाख्याता कृष्णलोहितरूपिणी
मुक्तकेशीत्य् अभिधया सास्ते ऽद्यापि स्वरूपिणी ॥
134.m:
She who is proclaimed the one unborn woman, having the form of black and red,
by the name of Muktakeśī, still abides in her own form today,

134.s:
lokatritayasaṃmohadāyinī kāmarūpiṇī
tadbalāt svasthamanasaḥ sarve ca munipuṃgavaḥ //
134.d:
लोकत्रितयसंमोहदायिनी कामरूपिणी
तद्बलात् स्वस्थमनसः सर्वे च मुनिपुंगवः ॥
134.m:
bestowing delusion upon the three worlds, assuming any form at will.
Through her power, all the foremost sages, with minds at ease,

134.s:
gautamīṃ saritāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ punar yajñāya dīkṣitāḥ
punas tanmakhanāśāya rākṣasāḥ samupāgaman //
134.d:
गौतमीं सरितां श्रेष्ठां पुनर् यज्ञाय दीक्षिताः
पुनस् तन्मखनाशाय राक्षसाः समुपागमन् ॥
134.m:
were consecrated again for the sacrifice on the Gautamī, the best of rivers.
Then the rākṣasas approached once more to destroy that sacrifice.

134.s:
yakṣavāṭāntike māyāṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasapuṃgavāḥ
tato nṛtyanti gāyanti hasanti ca rudanti ca //
134.d:
यक्षवाटान्तिके मायां दृष्ट्वा राक्षसपुंगवाः
ततो नृत्यन्ति गायन्ति हसन्ति च रुदन्ति च ॥
134.m:
Seeing that illusory woman near the sacrificial enclosure, the foremost rākṣasas
then danced, sang, laughed, and wept.

134.s:
māheśvarī mahāmāyā prabhāveṇātidarpitā
teṣāṃ madhye daityapatiḥ śambaro nāma vīryavān //
134.d:
माहेश्वरी महामाया प्रभावेणातिदर्पिता
तेषां मध्ये दैत्यपतिः शम्बरो नाम वीर्यवान् ॥
134.m:
She was Māheśvarī, the great illusory power, exceedingly proud through her majesty.
Among them, a powerful lord of the Daityas named Śambara

134.s:
māyārūpāṃ tu pramadāṃ bhakṣayām āsa nārada
tad adbhutam atīvāsīt tanmāyābaladarśinām //
134.d:
मायारूपां तु प्रमदां भक्षयाम् आस नारद
तद् अद्भुतम् अतीवासीत् तन्मायाबलदर्शिनाम् ॥
134.m:
devoured that woman of illusory form, O Nārada.
That was an extraordinary wonder to those who witnessed the power of that illusory form.

134.s:
makhe vidhvaṃsyamāne tu te viṣṇuṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ
prādād viṣṇuś cakram atho munīnāṃ rakṣaṇāya tu //
134.d:
मखे विध्वंस्यमाने तु ते विष्णुं शरणं ययुः
प्रादाद् विष्णुश् चक्रम् अथो मुनीनां रक्षणाय तु ॥
134.m:
When the sacrifice was being destroyed, however, they went to Viṣṇu for refuge.
Then Viṣṇu gave his discus for the protection of the sages.

134.s:
cakraṃ tad rākṣasān ājau daityāṃś ca danujāṃs tathā
ciccheda tadbhayād eva mṛtā rākṣasapuṃgavāḥ //
134.d:
चक्रं तद् राक्षसान् आजौ दैत्यांश् च दनुजांस् तथा
चिच्छेद तद्भयाद् एव मृता राक्षसपुंगवाः ॥
134.m:
That discus cut down the rākṣasas, Daityas, and Danujas in battle;
out of sheer fear of it, the foremost rākṣasas died.

134.s:
ṛṣibhis tan mahāsattraṃ saṃpūrṇam abhavat tadā
viṣṇoḥ prakṣālitaṃ cakraṃ gaṅgāmbhobhiḥ sudarśanam //
134.d:
ऋषिभिस् तन् महासत्त्रं संपूर्णम् अभवत् तदा
विष्णोः प्रक्षालितं चक्रं गङ्गाम्भोभिः सुदर्शनम् ॥
134.m:
That great sacrificial session was then brought to completion by the sages.
Viṣṇu's discus Sudarśana was washed with the waters of the Gaṅgā.

134.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ cakratīrtham udāhṛtam
tatra snānena dānena sattrayāgaphalaṃ labhet //
134.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं चक्रतीर्थम् उदाहृतम्
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन सत्त्रयागफलं लभेत् ॥
134.m:
From that time forward, that tīrtha has been proclaimed as Cakratīrtha.
Through bathing and giving gifts there, one obtains the fruit of a sacrificial session.

134.s:
tatra pañca śatāny āsaṃs tīrthānāṃ pāpahāriṇām
teṣu snānaṃ tathā dānaṃ pratyekaṃ muktidāyakam //
134.d:
तत्र पञ्च शतान्य् आसंस् तीर्थानां पापहारिणाम्
तेषु स्नानं तथा दानं प्रत्येकं मुक्तिदायकम् ॥
134.m:
There were five hundred sin-destroying tīrthas there;
bathing and giving gifts at each of them bestows liberation.

135.s:
brahmovāca
vāṇīsaṃgamam ākhyātaṃ yatra vāgīśvaro haraḥ
tat tīrthaṃ sarvapāpānāṃ mocanaṃ sarvakāmadam //
135.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वाणीसंगमम् आख्यातं यत्र वागीश्वरो हरः
तत् तीर्थं सर्वपापानां मोचनं सर्वकामदम् ॥

135.s:
tatra snānena dānena brahmahatyādināśanam
brahmaviṣṇvoś ca saṃvāde mahattve ca parasparam //
135.d:
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन ब्रह्महत्यादिनाशनम्
ब्रह्मविष्ण्वोश् च संवादे महत्त्वे च परस्परम् ॥
135.m:
Through bathing and giving gifts there, one destroys sins such as killing a brahmin.
In the dispute between Brahmā and Viṣṇu over their mutual greatness,

135.s:
tayor madhye mahādevo jyotirmūrtir abhūt kila
tatraiva vāg uvācedaṃ daivī putra tayoḥ śubhā //
135.d:
तयोर् मध्ये महादेवो ज्योतिर्मूर्तिर् अभूत् किल
तत्रैव वाग् उवाचेदं दैवी पुत्र तयोः शुभा ॥
135.m:
Mahādeva, it is said, appeared between them in the form of light.
Right there, O son, an auspicious divine voice spoke to both of them.

135.s:
aham asmi mahāṃs tatra aham asmīti vai mithaḥ
daivī vāk tāv ubhau prāha yas tv asyāntaṃ tu paśyati //
135.d:
अहम् अस्मि महांस् तत्र अहम् अस्मीति वै मिथः
दैवी वाक् ताव् उभौ प्राह यस् त्व् अस्यान्तं तु पश्यति ॥
135.m:
'I am great,' 'I am great'—as they argued with one another,
the divine voice said to both: 'Whoever sees the end of this [pillar of light]

135.s:
sa tu jyeṣṭho bhavet tasmān mā vādaṃ kartum arhathaḥ
tadvākyād viṣṇur agamad adho 'haṃ cordhvam eva ca //
135.d:
स तु ज्येष्ठो भवेत् तस्मान् मा वादं कर्तुम् अर्हथः
तद्वाक्याद् विष्णुर् अगमद् अधो ऽहं चोर्ध्वम् एव च ॥
135.m:
shall indeed be the elder; therefore, you two ought not to dispute.'
At that word, Viṣṇu went downward, and I went upward.

135.s:
tato viṣṇuḥ śīghram etya jyotiḥpārśva upāviśat
aprāpyāntam ahaṃ prāyāṃ dūrād dūrataraṃ mune //
135.d:
ततो विष्णुः शीघ्रम् एत्य ज्योतिःपार्श्व उपाविशत्
अप्राप्यान्तम् अहं प्रायां दूराद् दूरतरं मुने ॥
135.m:
Then Viṣṇu quickly returned and sat beside the light.
Unable to reach the end, I traveled farther and farther, O sage.

135.s:
tataḥ śrānto nivṛtto 'haṃ draṣṭum īśaṃ tu taṃ prabhum
tadaivaṃ mama dhīr āsīd dṛṣṭaś cānto mayā bhṛśam //
135.d:
ततः श्रान्तो निवृत्तो ऽहं द्रष्टुम् ईशं तु तं प्रभुम्
तदैवं मम धीर् आसीद् दृष्टश् चान्तो मया भृशम् ॥
135.m:
Then, weary, I turned back to see that Lord, the ruler;
and right then this thought occurred to me: 'The end has indeed been seen by me,

135.s:
asya devasya tad viṣṇor mama jyaiṣṭhyaṃ sphuṭaṃ bhavet
punaś cāpi mama tv evaṃ matir āsīn mahāmate //
135.d:
अस्य देवस्य तद् विष्णोर् मम ज्यैष्ठ्यं स्फुटं भवेत्
पुनश् चापि मम त्व् एवं मतिर् आसीन् महामते ॥
135.m:
of this god; so my seniority over Viṣṇu will be evident.'
Yet again, O noble-minded one, the thought came to me:

135.s:
satyair vaktraiḥ kathaṃ vakṣye pīḍito 'py anṛtaṃ vacaḥ
nānāvidheṣu pāpeṣu nānṛtāt pātakaṃ param //
135.d:
सत्यैर् वक्त्रैः कथं वक्ष्ये पीडितो ऽप्य् अनृतं वचः
नानाविधेषु पापेषु नानृतात् पातकं परम् ॥
135.m:
'How can I, though distressed, utter an untrue word with truthful mouths?
Among various kinds of sins, there is no higher crime than falsehood.

135.s:
satyair vaktrair asatyāṃ vā vācaṃ vakṣye kathaṃ tv iti
tato 'haṃ pañcamaṃ vaktraṃ gardabhākṛtibhīṣaṇam //
135.d:
सत्यैर् वक्त्रैर् असत्यां वा वाचं वक्ष्ये कथं त्व् इति
ततो ऽहं पञ्चमं वक्त्रं गर्दभाकृतिभीषणम् ॥
135.m:
How can I speak an untrue word with truthful mouths?'
Then, making a fifth mouth, terrifying with the form of an ass,

135.s:
kṛtvā tenānṛtaṃ vakṣya iti dhyātvā ciraṃ tadā
abravaṃ taṃ hariṃ tatra āsīnaṃ jagatāṃ prabhum //
135.d:
कृत्वा तेनानृतं वक्ष्य इति ध्यात्वा चिरं तदा
अब्रवं तं हरिं तत्र आसीनं जगतां प्रभुम् ॥
135.m:
having resolved for a long time, 'With this I shall speak the untruth,'
I spoke to Hari, the lord of the worlds, who was seated there:

135.s:
asya cānto mayā dṛṣṭas tena jyaiṣṭhyaṃ janārdana
mameti vadataḥ pārśve ubhau tau hariśaṃkarau //
135.d:
अस्य चान्तो मया दृष्टस् तेन ज्यैष्ठ्यं जनार्दन
ममेति वदतः पार्श्वे उभौ तौ हरिशंकरौ ॥
135.m:
'Its end has been seen by me; therefore, Janārdana, seniority is mine.'
As I spoke, right beside me those two, Hari and Śaṅkara,

135.s:
ekarūpatvam āpannau sūryācandramasāv iva
tau dṛṣṭvā vismito bhītaś cāstavaṃ tāv ubhāv api
tataḥ kruddhau jagannāthau vācaṃ tām idam ūcatuḥ //
135.d:
एकरूपत्वम् आपन्नौ सूर्याचन्द्रमसाव् इव
तौ दृष्ट्वा विस्मितो भीतश् चास्तवं ताव् उभाव् अपि
ततः क्रुद्धौ जगन्नाथौ वाचं ताम् इदम् ऊचतुः ॥
135.m:
became of one form, like the sun and the moon.
Seeing them, astonished and afraid, I praised them both.
Then the two lords of the world, enraged, spoke this word to Speech:

135.s:
hariharāv ūcatuḥ
duṣṭe tvaṃ nimnagā bhūyā nānṛtād asti pātakam //
135.d:
हरिहराव् ऊचतुः
दुष्टे त्वं निम्नगा भूया नानृताद् अस्ति पातकम् ॥
135.m:
Hari and Hara said:
Wicked one, become a river! There is no sin worse than falsehood!

135.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ sā vihvalā bhūtvā nadībhāvam upāgatā
tad dṛṣṭvā vismito bhītas tām abravam ahaṃ tadā //
135.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः सा विह्वला भूत्वा नदीभावम् उपागता
तद् दृष्ट्वा विस्मितो भीतस् ताम् अब्रवम् अहं तदा ॥
135.m:
Brahmā said:
Then, agitated, she turned into the state of a river.
Seeing that, astonished and afraid, I then said to her:

135.s:
yasmād asatyam uktāsi brahmavāci sthitā satī
tasmād adṛśyā tvaṃ bhūyāḥ pāparūpāsy asaṃśayam //
135.d:
यस्माद् असत्यम् उक्तासि ब्रह्मवाचि स्थिता सती
तस्माद् अदृश्या त्वं भूयाः पापरूपास्य् असंशयम् ॥
135.m:
'Since you, remaining in the speech of Brahmā, uttered a falsehood,
therefore become invisible; you are unquestionably of the form of sin.'

135.s:
etac chāpaṃ viditvā tu tau devau praṇatā tadā
viśāpatvaṃ prārthayantī tuṣṭāva ca punaḥ punaḥ //
135.d:
एतच् छापं विदित्वा तु तौ देवौ प्रणता तदा
विशापत्वं प्रार्थयन्ती तुष्टाव च पुनः पुनः ॥
135.m:
Aware of this curse, she bowed to the two gods then,
and begging for release from the curse, she praised them again and again.

135.s:
tatas tuṣṭau devadevau prārthitau tridaśārcitau
prītyā hariharāv evaṃ vācaṃ vācam athocatuḥ //
135.d:
ततस् तुष्टौ देवदेवौ प्रार्थितौ त्रिदशार्चितौ
प्रीत्या हरिहराव् एवं वाचं वाचम् अथोचतुः ॥
135.m:
Then the two gods of gods, worshiped by the thirty gods, being pleased,
Hari and Hara with love thus spoke word upon word to Speech:

135.s:
hariharāv ūcatuḥ
gaṅgayā saṃgatā bhadre yadā tvaṃ lokapāvanī
tadā punar vapus te syāt pavitraṃ hi suśobhane //
135.d:
हरिहराव् ऊचतुः
गङ्गया संगता भद्रे यदा त्वं लोकपावनी
तदा पुनर् वपुस् ते स्यात् पवित्रं हि सुशोभने ॥
135.m:
Hari and Hara said:
When you unite with the Gaṅgā, O auspicious one, purifying the world,
then your body shall again be pure, O very lovely lady!

135.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā sāpi devī gaṅgayā saṃgatābhavat
bhāgīrathī gautamī ca tataś cāpi svakaṃ vapuḥ //
135.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा सापि देवी गङ्गया संगताभवत्
भागीरथी गौतमी च ततश् चापि स्वकं वपुः ॥
135.m:
Brahmā said:
Saying 'So be it,' that goddess too united with the Gaṅgā,
the Bhāgīrathī and the Gautamī; and thereafter that goddess

135.s:
devī sā vyagamad brahman devānām api durlabham
gautamyāṃ saiva vikhyātā nāmnā vāṇīti puṇyadā //
135.d:
देवी सा व्यगमद् ब्रह्मन् देवानाम् अपि दुर्लभम्
गौतम्यां सैव विख्याता नाम्ना वाणीति पुण्यदा ॥
135.m:
attained her own form, O brahmin, difficult even for gods to obtain.
On the Gautamī she is celebrated by the name Vāṇī, the bestower of merit.

135.s:
bhāgīrathyāṃ saiva devī sarasvaty abhidhīyate
ubhayatrāpi vikhyātaḥ saṃgamo lokapūjitaḥ //
135.d:
भागीरथ्यां सैव देवी सरस्वत्य् अभिधीयते
उभयत्रापि विख्यातः संगमो लोकपूजितः ॥
135.m:
On the Bhāgīrathī that same goddess is called Sarasvatī.
In both places the confluence is celebrated and revered by the world.

135.s:
sarasvatīsaṃgamaś ca vāṇīsaṃgama eva ca
gautamyā saṃgatā devī vāṇī vācā sarasvatī //
135.d:
सरस्वतीसंगमश् च वाणीसंगम एव च
गौतम्या संगता देवी वाणी वाचा सरस्वती ॥
135.m: Both the confluence of the Sarasvatī and the confluence of the Vāṇī: / the goddess joined with the Gautamī as speech, as voice, as Sarasvatī.

135.s:
sarvatra pūjitaṃ tīrthaṃ tatra vācā śivaṃ prabhum
deveśvaraṃ pūjayitvā viśāpam agamad yataḥ //
135.d:
सर्वत्र पूजितं तीर्थं तत्र वाचा शिवं प्रभुम्
देवेश्वरं पूजयित्वा विशापम् अगमद् यतः ॥
135.m: That holy place is revered everywhere, where by his speech, having worshipped Lord Śiva, / the ruler of the gods, he became free of the curse.

135.s:
brahmā vidhūya vāgdauṣṭyaṃ svaṃ ca dhāmāgamat punaḥ
tasmāt tatra śucir bhūtvā snātvā tatra ca saṃgame //
135.d:
ब्रह्मा विधूय वाग्दौष्ट्यं स्वं च धामागमत् पुनः
तस्मात् तत्र शुचिर् भूत्वा स्नात्वा तत्र च संगमे ॥
135.m: Having dispelled the wicked speech, Brahmā returned again to his own abode. / Therefore, having become pure there, having bathed at that confluence,

135.s:
vāgīśvaraṃ tato dṛṣṭvā tāvatā muktim āpnuyāt
dānahomādikaṃ kiṃcid upavāsādikāṃ kriyām //
135.d:
वागीश्वरं ततो दृष्ट्वा तावता मुक्तिम् आप्नुयात्
दानहोमादिकं किंचिद् उपवासादिकां क्रियाम् ॥
135.m: and then beholding Vāgīśvara, one will attain liberation by just that much. / Whoever performs gifts, fire oblations, and the like, or observances such as fasting,

135.s:
yaḥ kuryāt saṃgame puṇye saṃsāre na bhavet punaḥ
ekonaviṃśatiśataṃ tīrthānāṃ tīrayor dvayoḥ
nānājanmārjitāśeṣapāpakṣayavidhāyinām //
135.d:
यः कुर्यात् संगमे पुण्ये संसारे न भवेत् पुनः
एकोनविंशतिशतं तीर्थानां तीरयोर् द्वयोः
नानाजन्मार्जिताशेषपापक्षयविधायिनाम् ॥
135.m: at that holy confluence will never return to worldly existence. / There are one hundred and nineteen holy places on its two banks / which destroy all sins acquired across various lifetimes.

136.s:
brahmovāca
viṣṇutīrtham iti khyātaṃ tatra vṛttam idaṃ śṛṇu
maudgalya iti vikhyāto mudgalasya suto ṛṣiḥ //
136.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
विष्णुतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं तत्र वृत्तम् इदं शृणु
मौद्गल्य इति विख्यातो मुद्गलस्य सुतो ऋषिः ॥
136.m: Brahmā said: / It is celebrated as the holy place of Viṣṇu. Hear the event that took place there. / There was a sage known as Maudgalya, the son of Mudgala.

136.s:
tasya bhāryā tu jābālā nāmnā khyātā suputriṇī
pitā ṛṣis tathā vṛddho mudgalo lokaviśrutaḥ //
136.d:
तस्य भार्या तु जाबाला नाम्ना ख्याता सुपुत्रिणी
पिता ऋषिस् तथा वृद्धो मुद्गलो लोकविश्रुतः ॥
136.m: His wife was known by the name Jābālā, endowed with virtuous sons. / His father was the aged sage Mudgala, world-renowned,

136.s:
tasya bhāryā tathā khyātā nāmnā bhāgīrathī śubhā
sa maudgalyaḥ prātar eva gaṅgāṃ snāti yatavrataḥ //
136.d:
तस्य भार्या तथा ख्याता नाम्ना भागीरथी शुभा
स मौद्गल्यः प्रातर् एव गङ्गां स्नाति यतव्रतः ॥
136.m: and his auspicious wife was well-known by the name Bhāgīrathī. / That Maudgalya, strictly observing his vows, bathed in the Gaṅgā early in the morning.

136.s:
nityam eva tv idaṃ karma tasyāsīn munisattama
gaṅgātīre kuśair mṛdbhiḥ śamīpuṣpair aharniśam //
136.d:
नित्यम् एव त्व् इदं कर्म तस्यासीन् मुनिसत्तम
गङ्गातीरे कुशैर् मृद्भिः शमीपुष्पैर् अहर्निशम् ॥
136.m: This was his daily duty, O best of sages: / on the bank of the Gaṅgā, day and night, with kuśa grass, clay, and flowers of the śamī tree,

136.s:
gurūditena mārgeṇa svamānasasaroruhe
āvāhanaṃ nityam eva viṣṇoś cakre sa maudgaliḥ //
136.d:
गुरूदितेन मार्गेण स्वमानससरोरुहे
आवाहनं नित्यम् एव विष्णोश् चक्रे स मौद्गलिः ॥
136.m: in the manner taught by his guru, in the lotus of his own mind, / that Maudgalya always performed the invocation of Viṣṇu.

136.s:
tenāhūtas tvarann eti lakṣmībhartā jagatpatiḥ
vainateyam athāruhya śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ //
136.d:
तेनाहूतस् त्वरन्न् एति लक्ष्मीभर्ता जगत्पतिः
वैनतेयम् अथारुह्य शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ॥
136.m: Invoked by him, the lord of the world, husband of Lakṣmī, bearer of the conch, discus, and mace, / arrived in haste, mounted upon the son of Vinatā.

136.s:
pūjitas tena ṛṣiṇā sa maudgalyena yatnataḥ
prabrūte ca kathāś citrā maudgalyāya jagatprabhuḥ //
136.d:
पूजितस् तेन ऋषिणा स मौद्गल्येन यत्नतः
प्रब्रूते च कथाश् चित्रा मौद्गल्याय जगत्प्रभुः ॥
136.m: Worshipped diligently by that sage Maudgalya, / the lord of the universe related wondrous tales to Maudgalya.

136.s:
tato 'parāhṇasamaye viṣṇuḥ prāha sa maudgalim
yāhi vatsa svabhavanaṃ śrānto 'sīti punaḥ punaḥ //
136.d:
ततो ऽपराह्णसमये विष्णुः प्राह स मौद्गलिम्
याहि वत्स स्वभवनं श्रान्तो ऽसीति पुनः पुनः ॥
136.m: Then, in the afternoon, Viṣṇu repeatedly said to Maudgalya: / “Go home, dear child, you are tired.”

136.s:
evam uktaḥ sa devena viṣṇunā yāti sa dvijaḥ
jagatprabhus tato yāti devair yuktaḥ svamandiram //
136.d:
एवम् उक्तः स देवेन विष्णुना याति स द्विजः
जगत्प्रभुस् ततो याति देवैर् युक्तः स्वमन्दिरम् ॥
136.m: Spoken to in this way by Lord Viṣṇu, that twice-born sage departed; / the lord of the universe then went to his own abode along with the gods.

136.s:
maudgalyo 'pi tathābhyetya kiṃcid ādāya nityaśaḥ
svam eva bhavanaṃ vidvān bhāryāyai svārjitaṃ dhanam //
136.d:
मौद्गल्यो ऽपि तथाभ्येत्य किंचिद् आदाय नित्यशः
स्वम् एव भवनं विद्वान् भार्यायै स्वार्जितं धनम् ॥
136.m: Maudgalya also, returning home, continually brought something, / the wise man bringing his earned wealth to his wife.

136.s:
dadāti sa mahāviṣṇucaraṇābjaparāyaṇaḥ
maudgalyasya priyā sāpi pativrataparāyaṇā //
136.d:
ददाति स महाविष्णुचरणाब्जपरायणः
मौद्गल्यस्य प्रिया सापि पतिव्रतपरायणा ॥
136.m: Devoted to the lotus-feet of Mahāviṣṇu, he gave it to her; / and Maudgalya's beloved wife was devoted to the duties of a faithful wife.

136.s:
śākaṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ vāpi bhartrānītaṃ tu yatnataḥ
susaṃskṛtyāpy atithīnāṃ bālānāṃ bhartur eva ca //
136.d:
शाकं मूलं फलं वापि भर्त्रानीतं तु यत्नतः
सुसंस्कृत्याप्य् अतिथीनां बालानां भर्तुर् एव च ॥
136.m: Vegetables, roots, or fruits diligently brought by her husband / she properly prepared and gave as food to guests, children, and her husband,

136.s:
dattvā tu bhojanaṃ tebhyaḥ paścād bhuṅkte yatavratā
bhuktavatsv atha sarveṣu rātrau nityaṃ sa maudgaliḥ //
136.d:
दत्त्वा तु भोजनं तेभ्यः पश्चाद् भुङ्क्ते यतव्रता
भुक्तवत्स्व् अथ सर्वेषु रात्रौ नित्यं स मौद्गलिः ॥
136.m: and after giving food to them, she ate afterwards, observing her vows. / When all had eaten, every night that Maudgalya,

136.s:
viṣṇoḥ śrutāḥ kathāś citrās tebhyo vakty atha harṣitaḥ
evaṃ bahutithe kāle vyatīte cātivismitā
maudgalyasya raho bhāryā bhartāraṃ vākyam abravīt //
136.d:
विष्णोः श्रुताः कथाश् चित्रास् तेभ्यो वक्त्य् अथ हर्षितः
एवं बहुतिथे काले व्यतीते चातिविस्मिता
मौद्गल्यस्य रहो भार्या भर्तारं वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
136.m: delighted, recited to them the wondrous tales he had heard of Viṣṇu. / Thus after much time had passed, exceedingly astonished, / Maudgalya's wife spoke these words in secret to her husband:

136.s:
jābālovāca
yadi te viṣṇur abhyeti samīpaṃ tridaśārcitaḥ
tathāpi kaṣṭam asmākaṃ kasmād iti jagatprabhum //
136.d:
जाबालोवाच
यदि ते विष्णुर् अभ्येति समीपं त्रिदशार्चितः
तथापि कष्टम् अस्माकं कस्माद् इति जगत्प्रभुम् ॥
136.m: Jābālā said: / “If Viṣṇu, worshipped by the thirty [gods], approaches you, / then why do we still suffer hardship? Ask the lord of the universe that,

136.s:
tat pṛccha tvaṃ mahāprājña yadāsau viṣṇur eti ca
yasmiṃś ca smṛtamātre tu jarājanmarujo mṛtiḥ
nāśaṃ yānti kuto dṛṣṭe tasmāt pṛccha jagatpatim //
136.d:
तत् पृच्छ त्वं महाप्राज्ञ यदासौ विष्णुर् एति च
यस्मिंश् च स्मृतमात्रे तु जराजन्मरुजो मृतिः
नाशं यान्ति कुतो दृष्टे तस्मात् पृच्छ जगत्पतिम् ॥
136.m: O greatly wise one, when that Viṣṇu arrives, / the one who, being merely remembered, dispels old age, birth, disease, and death— / how much more so when he is seen! Therefore, ask the lord of the universe.”

136.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā priyāvākyān maudgalyo nityavad dharim
pūjayitvā vinītaś ca papraccha sa kṛtāñjaliḥ //
136.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा प्रियावाक्यान् मौद्गल्यो नित्यवद् धरिम्
पूजयित्वा विनीतश् च पप्रच्छ स कृताञ्जलिः ॥
136.m: Brahmā said: / Saying “So be it” at the words of his beloved, Maudgalya worshipped Hari as usual, / and humble, with folded hands, he questioned him.

136.s:
maudgalya uvāca
tvayi smṛte jagannātha śokadāridryaduṣkṛtam
nāśaṃ yāti vipattir me tvayi dṛṣṭe kathaṃ sthitā //
136.d:
मौद्गल्य उवाच
त्वयि स्मृते जगन्नाथ शोकदारिद्र्यदुष्कृतम्
नाशं याति विपत्तिर् मे त्वयि दृष्टे कथं स्थिता ॥
136.m: Maudgalya said: / “O Lord of the Universe, when you are remembered, grief, poverty, and misdeeds / meet their destruction; how then does misfortune remain with me when you are seen?”

136.s:
śrīviṣṇur uvāca
svakṛtaṃ bhujyate bhūtaiḥ sarvaiḥ sarvatra sarvadā
na kopi kasyacit kiṃcit karoty atra hitāhite //
136.d:
श्रीविष्णुर् उवाच
स्वकृतं भुज्यते भूतैः सर्वैः सर्वत्र सर्वदा
न कोपि कस्यचित् किंचित् करोत्य् अत्र हिताहिते ॥
136.m: Glorious Viṣṇu said: / “All beings everywhere and always experience their own deeds. / No one here causes anything beneficial or unbeneficial for anyone else.

136.s:
yādṛśaṃ copyate bījaṃ phalaṃ bhavati tādṛśam
rasālaḥ syān na nimbasya bījāj jātv api kutracit //
136.d:
यादृशं चोप्यते बीजं फलं भवति तादृशम्
रसालः स्यान् न निम्बस्य बीजाज् जात्व् अपि कुत्रचित् ॥
136.m: Whatever kind of seed is sown, such is the fruit that arises; / a sweet mango tree can never come from the seed of a neem tree anywhere.

136.s:
na kṛtā gautamīsevā nārcitau hariśaṃkarau
na dattaṃ yaiś ca viprebhyas te kathaṃ bhājanaṃ śriyaḥ //
136.d:
न कृता गौतमीसेवा नार्चितौ हरिशंकरौ
न दत्तं यैश् च विप्रेभ्यस् ते कथं भाजनं श्रियः ॥
136.m: Those who have not served the Gautamī, have not worshipped Hari and Śaṅkara, / and have not given to the Brahmins—how could they be the vessel of prosperity?

136.s:
tvayā na dattaṃ kiṃcic ca brāhmaṇebhyo mamāpi ca
yad dīyate tad eveha parasmiṃś copatiṣṭhati //
136.d:
त्वया न दत्तं किंचिच् च ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ममापि च
यद् दीयते तद् एवेह परस्मिंश् चोपतिष्ठति ॥
136.m: Nothing has been given by you to Brahmins, nor to me; / and only whatever is given here attends one in the other world.

136.s:
mṛdbhir vārbhiḥ kuśair mantraiḥ śucikarma sadaiva yat
karoti tasmāt pūtātmā śarīrasya ca śoṣaṇāt //
136.d:
मृद्भिर् वार्भिः कुशैर् मन्त्रैः शुचिकर्म सदैव यत्
करोति तस्मात् पूतात्मा शरीरस्य च शोषणात् ॥
136.m: Because one constantly performs rites of purification with clay, water, kuśa grass, and mantras, / and through the emaciation of the body, the self becomes purified.

136.s:
vinā dānena na kvāpi bhogāvāptir nṛṇāṃ bhavet
satkarmācaraṇāc chuddho viraktaḥ syāt tato naraḥ //
136.d:
विना दानेन न क्वापि भोगावाप्तिर् नृणां भवेत्
सत्कर्माचरणाच् छुद्धो विरक्तः स्यात् ततो नरः ॥
136.m: Without giving, men never attain enjoyment anywhere. / Purified by the performance of good deeds, a man becomes detached;

136.s:
tato 'pratihatajñāno jīvanmuktas tato bhavet
sarveṣāṃ sulabhā muktir madbhaktyā ceha pūrtataḥ //
136.d:
ततो ऽप्रतिहतज्ञानो जीवन्मुक्तस् ततो भवेत्
सर्वेषां सुलभा मुक्तिर् मद्भक्त्या चेह पूर्ततः ॥
136.m: then, with unobstructed knowledge, he becomes liberated while alive. / Liberation is easy for all to attain through devotion to me and through works of public charity here;

136.s:
bhuktir dānādinā sarvabhūtaduḥkhanibarhaṇāt
athavā lapsyase muktiṃ bhaktyā bhuktiṃ na lapsyase //
136.d:
भुक्तिर् दानादिना सर्वभूतदुःखनिबर्हणात्
अथवा लप्स्यसे मुक्तिं भक्त्या भुक्तिं न लप्स्यसे ॥
136.m: enjoyment comes through gifts and the like, by removing the suffering of all creatures. / Alternatively, you will attain liberation through devotion, but you will not attain enjoyment.”

136.s:
maudgalya uvāca
bhaktyā muktiḥ kathaṃ bhūyād bhukter muktiḥ sudurlabhā
jātā ced dehināṃ muktiḥ kim anyena prayojanam //
136.d:
मौद्गल्य उवाच
भक्त्या मुक्तिः कथं भूयाद् भुक्तेर् मुक्तिः सुदुर्लभा
जाता चेद् देहिनां मुक्तिः किम् अन्येन प्रयोजनम् ॥
136.m: Maudgalya said: / “How can liberation arise through devotion? Liberation from worldly enjoyment is extremely difficult to attain. / If liberation has arisen for embodied beings, what need is there for anything else?

136.s: bhaktyā muktiḥ sarvapūjyā tām iccheyaṃ jaganmaya //
136.d: भक्त्या मुक्तिः सर्वपूज्या ताम् इच्छेयं जगन्मय ॥
136.m: Liberation through devotion is worshipped by all; that is what I desire, O You whose form is the universe!”

136.s:
viṣṇur uvāca
etad evāntaraṃ brahman dīyate mām anusmaran
brāhmaṇāyāthavārthibhyas tad evākṣayatāṃ vrajet //
136.d:
विष्णुर् उवाच
एतद् एवान्तरं ब्रह्मन् दीयते माम् अनुस्मरन्
ब्राह्मणायाथवार्थिभ्यस् तद् एवाक्षयतां व्रजेत् ॥
136.m: Viṣṇu said: / “This is the distinction, O Brahmin: whatever is given while remembering me, / whether to a Brahmin or to supplicants, becomes imperishable.

136.s:
mām adhyātvātha yad dadyāt tat tanmātraphalapradam
tat punar dattam eveha na bhogāyātra kalpate //
136.d:
माम् अध्यात्वाथ यद् दद्यात् तत् तन्मात्रफलप्रदम्
तत् पुनर् दत्तम् एवेह न भोगायात्र कल्पते ॥
136.m: Whatever one gives without meditating on me bestows only limited fruit; / once given here, that does not serve for enjoyment in this world.

136.s:
tasmād dehi mahābuddhe bhojyaṃ kiṃcin mama dhruvam
athavā vipramukhyāya gautamītīram āśritaḥ //
136.d:
तस्माद् देहि महाबुद्धे भोज्यं किंचिन् मम ध्रुवम्
अथवा विप्रमुख्याय गौतमीतीरम् आश्रितः ॥
136.m: Therefore, O greatly wise one, residing on the bank of the Gautamī, / surely give some food to me, or to an eminent Brahmin.”

136.s:
brahmovāca
maudgalyaḥ prāha taṃ viṣṇuṃ deyaṃ mama na vidyate
nānyat kiṃcana dehādi yat tat tvayi samarpitam //
136.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मौद्गल्यः प्राह तं विष्णुं देयं मम न विद्यते
नान्यत् किंचन देहादि यत् तत् त्वयि समर्पितम् ॥
136.m: Brahmā said: / Maudgalya said to that Viṣṇu: “I have nothing that can be given; / I have nothing else whatsoever—this body and all else is offered to you.”

136.s:
tato viṣṇur garutmantaṃ prāha śīghraṃ jagatpatiḥ
ihānayasva kaṇiśaṃ mamāyaṃ cārpayiṣyati //
136.d:
ततो विष्णुर् गरुत्मन्तं प्राह शीघ्रं जगत्पतिः
इहानयस्व कणिशं ममायं चार्पयिष्यति ॥
136.m: Then the lord of the universe spoke quickly to Garuḍa: / “Bring an ear of grain here, and he will offer it to me;

136.s:
tato yogyān ayaṃ bhogān prāpsyate manasaḥ priyān
ākarṇya svāminādiṣṭaṃ tathā cakre sa pakṣirāṭ //
136.d:
ततो योग्यान् अयं भोगान् प्राप्स्यते मनसः प्रियान्
आकर्ण्य स्वामिनादिष्टं तथा चक्रे स पक्षिराट् ॥
136.m: then he will attain fitting enjoyments dear to his heart.” / Having heard the command of his master, the king of birds did so.

136.s:
viṣṇuhaste kaṇān prādāt sa maudgalyo yatavrataḥ
etasminn antare viṣṇur viśvakarmāṇam abravīt //
136.d:
विष्णुहस्ते कणान् प्रादात् स मौद्गल्यो यतव्रतः
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे विष्णुर् विश्वकर्माणम् अब्रवीत् ॥
136.m: Maudgalya, observing his vows, placed the grains in Viṣṇu's hand. / In the meantime, Viṣṇu spoke to Viśvakarman.

136.s:
viṣṇur uvāca
yāvac cāsya kule sapta puruṣās tāvad eva tu
bhavitāro mahābuddhe tāvat kāmā manīṣitāḥ
gāvo hiraṇyaṃ dhānyāni vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca //
136.d:
विष्णुर् उवाच
यावच् चास्य कुले सप्त पुरुषास् तावद् एव तु
भवितारो महाबुद्धे तावत् कामा मनीषिताः
गावो हिरण्यं धान्यानि वस्त्राण्य् आभरणानि च ॥
136.m: Viṣṇu said: / “As long as seven generations arise in his lineage, O greatly wise one, / for that long all desired objects— / cows, gold, grain, clothing, and ornaments—shall exist for him.”

136.s:
brahmovāca
yac ca kiṃcin manaḥprītyai loke bhavati bhūṣaṇam
tat sarvam āpa maudgalyo viṣṇugaṅgāprabhāvataḥ //
136.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यच् च किंचिन् मनःप्रीत्यै लोके भवति भूषणम्
तत् सर्वम् आप मौद्गल्यो विष्णुगङ्गाप्रभावतः ॥
136.m: Brahmā said: / And whatever serves as an ornament in the world to bring delight to the mind, / Maudgalya obtained all of that through the power of Viṣṇu and the Gaṅgā.

136.s:
gṛhaṃ gaccheti maudgalyo viṣṇunoktas tato yayau
āśrame svasya sarvarddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā ṛṣir abhāṣata //
136.d:
गृहं गच्छेति मौद्गल्यो विष्णुनोक्तस् ततो ययौ
आश्रमे स्वस्य सर्वर्द्धिं दृष्ट्वा ऋषिर् अभाषत ॥
136.m: Told by Viṣṇu: “Go home,” Maudgalya then went. / Seeing all manner of prosperity at his hermitage, the sage said:

136.s:
ṛṣir uvāca
aho dānaprabhāvo 'yam aho viṣṇor anusmṛtiḥ
aho gaṅgāprabhāvaś ca kair vicāryo mahān ayam //
136.d:
ऋषिर् उवाच
अहो दानप्रभावो ऽयम् अहो विष्णोर् अनुस्मृतिः
अहो गङ्गाप्रभावश् च कैर् विचार्यो महान् अयम् ॥
136.m: The sage said: / “Ah, how wonderful is this power of giving! Ah, how wonderful is the remembrance of Viṣṇu! / And ah, the power of the Gaṅgā! Who can fathom this great marvel?”

136.s:
brahmovāca
maudgalyo bhāryayā sārdhaṃ putraiḥ pautraiś ca bandhubhiḥ
pitṛbhyāṃ bubhuje bhogān bhuktiṃ muktim avāpa ca //
136.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मौद्गल्यो भार्यया सार्धं पुत्रैः पौत्रैश् च बन्धुभिः
पितृभ्यां बुभुजे भोगान् भुक्तिं मुक्तिम् अवाप च ॥
136.m:
Brahmā said:
Maudgalya, along with his wife, sons, grandsons, relatives,
and parents, enjoyed pleasures, and attained enjoyment and liberation.

136.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ maudgalyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tathā
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca bhuktimuktiphalapradam //
136.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं मौद्गल्यं वैष्णवं तथा
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदम् ॥
136.m:
From that time forward, that tīrtha has been Maudgalya and Vaiṣṇava;
bathing and giving gifts there bestow the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.

136.s:
tatra śrutiḥ smṛtir vāpi tīrthasya syāt kathaṃcana
tasya viṣṇur bhavet prītaḥ pāpair muktaḥ sukhī bhavet //
136.d:
तत्र श्रुतिः स्मृतिर् वापि तीर्थस्य स्यात् कथंचन
तस्य विष्णुर् भवेत् प्रीतः पापैर् मुक्तः सुखी भवेत् ॥
136.m:
If by any means there should be hearing or remembrance of that tīrtha,
Viṣṇu becomes pleased with him, and freed from sins, he becomes happy.

136.s:
ekādaśa sahasrāṇi tīrthānāṃ tīrayor dvayoḥ
sarvārthadāyināṃ tatra snānadānajapādibhiḥ //
136.d:
एकादश सहस्राणि तीर्थानां तीरयोर् द्वयोः
सर्वार्थदायिनां तत्र स्नानदानजपादिभिः ॥
136.m:
There are eleven thousand tīrthas on both banks
that grant all desires through bathing, giving gifts, silent recitation, and the like.

137.s:
brahmovāca
lakṣmītīrtham iti khyātaṃ sākṣāl lakṣmīvivardhanam
alakṣmīnāśanaṃ puṇyam ākhyānaṃ śṛṇu nārada //
137.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
लक्ष्मीतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं साक्षाल् लक्ष्मीविवर्धनम्
अलक्ष्मीनाशनं पुण्यम् आख्यानं शृणु नारद ॥
137.m: Brahmā said: / Hear, O Nārada, the holy tale known as Lakṣmītīrtha, / which directly increases prosperity and destroys misfortune.

137.s:
saṃvādaś ca purā tv āsīl lakṣmyāḥ putra daridrayā
parasparavirodhinyāv ubhe viśvaṃ samīyatuḥ //
137.d:
संवादश् च पुरा त्व् आसील् लक्ष्म्याः पुत्र दरिद्रया
परस्परविरोधिन्याव् उभे विश्वं समीयतुः ॥
137.m: Formerly, O son, there arose a dispute between Lakṣmī and Daridrā (Poverty). / Opposed to one another, both traversed the universe.

137.s:
tābhyām avyāpṛtaṃ vastu tan nāsti bhuvanatraye
mama jyaiṣṭhyaṃ mama jyaiṣṭhyam ity ūcatur ubhe mithaḥ
ahaṃ pūrvaṃ samudbhūtā ity āha śriyam ojasā //
137.d:
ताभ्याम् अव्यापृतं वस्तु तन् नास्ति भुवनत्रये
मम ज्यैष्ठ्यं मम ज्यैष्ठ्यम् इत्य् ऊचतुर् उभे मिथः
अहं पूर्वं समुद्भूता इत्य् आह श्रियम् ओजसा ॥
137.m: There is no entity in the three worlds unoccupied by the two of them. / Both said mutually, "Seniority belongs to me! Seniority belongs to me!" / [Daridrā] said vehemently to Śrī, "I was born first!"

137.s:
śrīlakṣmīr uvāca
kulaṃ śīlaṃ jīvitaṃ vā dehinām aham eva tu
mayā vinā dehabhājo jīvanto 'pi mṛtā iva //
137.d:
श्रीलक्ष्मीर् उवाच
कुलं शीलं जीवितं वा देहिनाम् अहम् एव तु
मया विना देहभाजो जीवन्तो ऽपि मृता इव ॥
137.m: Śrī Lakṣmī said: / I alone am lineage, good character, and the life of embodied beings. / Without me, embodied souls, though living, are as if dead.

137.s:
brahmovāca
daridrayā ca sā proktā sarvebhyo hy adhikā hy aham
muktir madāśritā nityaṃ daridraivaṃ vaco 'bravīt //
137.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दरिद्रया च सा प्रोक्ता सर्वेभ्यो ह्य् अधिका ह्य् अहम्
मुक्तिर् मदाश्रिता नित्यं दरिद्रैवं वचो ऽब्रवीत् ॥
137.m: Brahmā said: / And she was addressed by Daridrā: "I indeed am greater than all; / liberation is ever dependent on me." Thus Daridrā spoke these words:

137.s:
kāmaḥ krodhaś ca lobhaś ca mado mātsaryam eva ca
yatrāham asmi tatraite na tiṣṭhanti kadācana //
137.d:
कामः क्रोधश् च लोभश् च मदो मात्सर्यम् एव च
यत्राहम् अस्मि तत्रैते न तिष्ठन्ति कदाचन ॥
137.m: "Lust, anger, greed, pride, and malice— / wherever I am, these never abide.

137.s:
na bhayodbhūtir unmāda īrṣyā uddhatavṛttitā
yatrāham asmi tatraite na tiṣṭhanti kadācana //
137.d:
न भयोद्भूतिर् उन्माद ईर्ष्या उद्धतवृत्तिता
यत्राहम् अस्मि तत्रैते न तिष्ठन्ति कदाचन ॥
137.m: The arising of fear, madness, envy, and arrogant conduct— / wherever I am, these never abide."

137.s: daridrāyā vacaḥ śrutvā lakṣmīs tāṃ pratyabhāṣata //
137.d: दरिद्राया वचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मीस् तां प्रत्यभाषत ॥
137.m: Hearing the words of Daridrā, Lakṣmī answered her:

137.s:
lakṣmīr uvāca
alaṃkṛto mayā jantuḥ sarvo bhavati pūjitaḥ
nirdhanaḥ śivatulyo 'pi sarvair apy abhibhūyate //
137.d:
लक्ष्मीर् उवाच
अलंकृतो मया जन्तुः सर्वो भवति पूजितः
निर्धनः शिवतुल्यो ऽपि सर्वैर् अप्य् अभिभूयते ॥
137.m: Lakṣmī said: / Any creature adorned by me becomes revered by all. / A person without wealth, though equal to Śiva, is overcome by everyone.

137.s:
dehīti vacanadvārā dehasthāḥ pañca devatāḥ
sadyo nirgatya gacchanti dhīśrīhrīśāntikīrtayaḥ //
137.d:
देहीति वचनद्वारा देहस्थाः पञ्च देवताः
सद्यो निर्गत्य गच्छन्ति धीश्रीह्रीशान्तिकीर्तयः ॥
137.m: As soon as the word 'Give!' is uttered, the five deities residing in the body / immediately depart and leave: intellect, prosperity, modesty, peace, and renown.

137.s:
tāvad guṇā gurutvaṃ ca yāvan nārthayate param
arthī cet puruṣo jātaḥ kva guṇāḥ kva ca gauravam //
137.d:
तावद् गुणा गुरुत्वं च यावन् नार्थयते परम्
अर्थी चेत् पुरुषो जातः क्व गुणाः क्व च गौरवम् ॥
137.m: Good qualities and dignity last only so long as one does not beg from another. / If a man becomes a petitioner, where are virtues and where is dignity?

137.s:
tāvat sarvottamo jantus tāvat sarvaguṇālayaḥ
namasyaḥ sarvalokānāṃ yāvan nārthayate param //
137.d:
तावत् सर्वोत्तमो जन्तुस् तावत् सर्वगुणालयः
नमस्यः सर्वलोकानां यावन् नार्थयते परम् ॥
137.m: A creature is best among all and an abode of all virtues, / worthy of respect by all worlds, only so long as he does not beg from another.

137.s:
kaṣṭam etan mahāpāpaṃ nirdhanatvaṃ śarīriṇām
na mānayati no vakti na spṛśaty adhanaṃ janaḥ //
137.d:
कष्टम् एतन् महापापं निर्धनत्वं शरीरिणाम्
न मानयति नो वक्ति न स्पृशत्य् अधनं जनः ॥
137.m: This poverty is a misery, a great sin for embodied beings. / People do not respect, do not speak to, and do not touch a penniless man.

137.s: aham eva tataḥ śreṣṭhā daridre śṛṇu me vacaḥ //
137.d: अहम् एव ततः श्रेष्ठा दरिद्रे शृणु मे वचः ॥
137.m: Therefore I alone am superior. O Daridrā, hear my words!

137.s:
brahmovāca
tal lakṣmīvacanaṃ śrutvā daridrā vākyam abravīt //
137.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तल् लक्ष्मीवचनं श्रुत्वा दरिद्रा वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
137.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing those words of Lakṣmī, Daridrā spoke:

137.s:
daridrovāca
vaktuṃ na lakṣmīr jyeṣṭhāham iti vai lajjase muhuḥ
pāpeṣu ramase nityaṃ vihāya puruṣottamam //
137.d:
दरिद्रोवाच
वक्तुं न लक्ष्मीर् ज्येष्ठाहम् इति वै लज्जसे मुहुः
पापेषु रमसे नित्यं विहाय पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
137.m: Daridrā said: / Are you not ashamed to constantly say, "Lakṣmī, I am the elder"? / Abandoning Puruṣottama, you continually revel in sinners.

137.s:
viśvastavañcakā nityaṃ bhavatī ślāghase katham
sukhaṃ na tādṛk tvatprāptau paścāttāpo yathā guruḥ //
137.d:
विश्वस्तवञ्चका नित्यं भवती श्लाघसे कथम्
सुखं न तादृक् त्वत्प्राप्तौ पश्चात्तापो यथा गुरुः ॥
137.m: A perpetual betrayer of those who trust you, how can you boast of yourself? / There is not such pleasure in obtaining you as there is great remorse afterward.

137.s:
na tathā jāyate puṃsāṃ surayā dāruṇo madaḥ
tvatsaṃnidhānamātreṇa yathā vai viduṣām api //
137.d:
न तथा जायते पुंसां सुरया दारुणो मदः
त्वत्संनिधानमात्रेण यथा वै विदुषाम् अपि ॥
137.m: Wine does not produce such terrible intoxication in men / as does your mere presence, even for the wise.

137.s:
sadaiva ramase lakṣmīḥ prāyas tvaṃ pāpakāriṣu
ahaṃ vasāmi yogyeṣu dharmaśīleṣu sarvadā //
137.d:
सदैव रमसे लक्ष्मीः प्रायस् त्वं पापकारिषु
अहं वसामि योग्येषु धर्मशीलेषु सर्वदा ॥
137.m: O Lakṣmī, you almost always delight in evil-doers. / I always dwell among the worthy and those of righteous conduct,

137.s:
śivaviṣṇvanurakteṣu kṛtajñeṣu mahatsu ca
sadācāreṣu śānteṣu gurusevodyateṣu ca //
137.d:
शिवविष्ण्वनुरक्तेषु कृतज्ञेषु महत्सु च
सदाचारेषु शान्तेषु गुरुसेवोद्यतेषु च ॥
137.m: among those devoted to Śiva and Viṣṇu, the grateful, the noble, / those of virtuous conduct, the tranquil, and those intent on serving the guru,

137.s:
satsu vidvatsu śūreṣu kṛtabuddhiṣu sādhuṣu
nivasāmi sadā lakṣmīs tasmāj jyaiṣṭhyaṃ mayi sthitam //
137.d:
सत्सु विद्वत्सु शूरेषु कृतबुद्धिषु साधुषु
निवसामि सदा लक्ष्मीस् तस्माज् ज्यैष्ठ्यं मयि स्थितम् ॥
137.m: among the good, the learned, the heroic, the resolute, and the virtuous / do I ever dwell, O Lakṣmī; therefore seniority resides in me.

137.s:
brāhmaṇeṣu śuciṣmatsu vratacāriṣu bhikṣuṣu
nirbhayeṣu vasiṣyāmi lakṣmīs tvaṃ śṛṇu te sthitim //
137.d:
ब्राह्मणेषु शुचिष्मत्सु व्रतचारिषु भिक्षुषु
निर्भयेषु वसिष्यामि लक्ष्मीस् त्वं शृणु ते स्थितिम् ॥
137.m: I shall dwell among brāhmaṇas who are pure, observant of vows, mendicants, / and fearless. O Lakṣmī, hear your own dwelling place:

137.s:
rājavartiṣu pāpeṣu niṣṭhureṣu khaleṣu ca
piśuneṣu ca lubdheṣu vikṛteṣu śaṭheṣu ca //
137.d:
राजवर्तिषु पापेषु निष्ठुरेषु खलेषु च
पिशुनेषु च लुब्धेषु विकृतेषु शठेषु च ॥
137.m: Among those in royal service, the sinful, the cruel, the wicked, / the slanderous, the greedy, the perverse, the deceitful,

137.s:
anāryeṣu kṛtaghneṣu dharmaghātiṣu sarvadā
mitradrohiṣv aniṣṭeṣu bhagnacitteṣu vartase //
137.d:
अनार्येषु कृतघ्नेषु धर्मघातिषु सर्वदा
मित्रद्रोहिष्व् अनिष्टेषु भग्नचित्तेषु वर्तसे ॥
137.m: the ignoble, the ungrateful, the destroyers of dharma, / the betrayers of friends, the harmful, and the broken-hearted do you always dwell.

137.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ vivadamāne te jagmatur mām ubhe api
tayor vākyam upaśrutya mayokte te ubhe api //
137.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं विवदमाने ते जग्मतुर् माम् उभे अपि
तयोर् वाक्यम् उपश्रुत्य मयोक्ते ते उभे अपि ॥
137.m: Brahmā said: / As they disputed in this way, both came to me. / Having heard their words, both were told by me:

137.s:
mattaḥ pūrvatarā pṛthvī āpaḥ pūrvatarās tataḥ
strīṇāṃ vivādaṃ tā eva striyo jānanti netare //
137.d:
मत्तः पूर्वतरा पृथ्वी आपः पूर्वतरास् ततः
स्त्रीणां विवादं ता एव स्त्रियो जानन्ति नेतरे ॥
137.m: "The earth is older than me, and the waters are older than that; / women alone understand a dispute among women, not others.

137.s:
viśeṣataḥ punas tābhyaḥ kamaṇḍalubhavāś ca yāḥ
tatrāpi gautamī devī niścayaṃ kathayiṣyati //
137.d:
विशेषतः पुनस् ताभ्यः कमण्डलुभवाश् च याः
तत्रापि गौतमी देवी निश्चयं कथयिष्यति ॥
137.m: And especially from among them, those born from the water-pot. / Even among them, the goddess Gautamī will pronounce the decision.

137.s:
saiva sarvārtisaṃhartrī saiva saṃdehakartarī
te madvākyād bhuvaṃ gatvā bhūmyā ca sahite api //
137.d:
सैव सर्वार्तिसंहर्त्री सैव संदेहकर्तरी
ते मद्वाक्याद् भुवं गत्वा भूम्या च सहिते अपि ॥
137.m: She alone destroys all distress; she alone is the shearer of doubts." / At my words, they went to the earth, and accompanied by the earth

137.s:
adbhiś ca sahitāḥ sarvā gautamīṃ yayur āpagām
bhūmir āpas tayor vākyaṃ gautamyai kramaśaḥ sphuṭam //
137.d:
अद्भिश् च सहिताः सर्वा गौतमीं ययुर् आपगाम्
भूमिर् आपस् तयोर् वाक्यं गौतम्यै क्रमशः स्फुटम् ॥
137.m: and accompanied by the waters, they all went to the river Gautamī. / The earth and the waters clearly and sequentially

137.s:
sarvaṃ nivedayām āsur yathāvṛttaṃ praṇamya tām
daridrāyāś ca lakṣmyāś ca vākyaṃ madhyasthavat tadā //
137.d:
सर्वं निवेदयाम् आसुर् यथावृत्तं प्रणम्य ताम्
दरिद्रायाश् च लक्ष्म्याश् च वाक्यं मध्यस्थवत् तदा ॥
137.m: reported everything to Gautamī, bowing to her, exactly as it happened: / the words of Daridrā and of Lakṣmī, as impartial arbiters.

137.s:
śṛṇvatsu lokapāleṣu śṛṇvatyāṃ bhuvi nārada
śṛṇvatīṣv apsu sā gaṅgā daridrāṃ vākyam abravīt
saṃpraśasya tathā lakṣmīṃ gautamī vākyam abravīt //
137.d:
शृण्वत्सु लोकपालेषु शृण्वत्यां भुवि नारद
शृण्वतीष्व् अप्सु सा गङ्गा दरिद्रां वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
संप्रशस्य तथा लक्ष्मीं गौतमी वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
137.m: While the world guardians listened, while the earth listened, O Nārada, / while the waters listened, that Gaṅgā spoke to Daridrā; / having praised Lakṣmī, Gautamī uttered these words:

137.s:
gautamy uvāca
brahmaśrīś ca tapaḥśrīś ca yajñaśrīḥ kīrtisaṃjñitā
dhanaśrīś ca yaśaśrīś ca vidyā prajñā sarasvatī //
137.d:
गौतम्य् उवाच
ब्रह्मश्रीश् च तपःश्रीश् च यज्ञश्रीः कीर्तिसंज्ञिता
धनश्रीश् च यशश्रीश् च विद्या प्रज्ञा सरस्वती ॥
137.m: Gautamī said: / The splendor of sacred knowledge, the splendor of asceticism, the splendor of sacrifice known as renown, / the splendor of wealth, the splendor of fame, knowledge, wisdom, and Sarasvatī,

137.s:
bhuktiśrīś cātha muktiś ca smṛtir lajjā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā
siddhis tuṣṭis tathā puṣṭiḥ śāntir āpas tathā mahī //
137.d:
भुक्तिश्रीश् चाथ मुक्तिश् च स्मृतिर् लज्जा धृतिः क्षमा
सिद्धिस् तुष्टिस् तथा पुष्टिः शान्तिर् आपस् तथा मही ॥
137.m: and the splendor of enjoyment, liberation, memory, modesty, resolve, forbearance, / accomplishment, contentment, nourishment, peace, the waters, and the earth,

137.s:
ahaṃśaktir athauṣadhyaḥ śrutiḥ śuddhir vibhāvarī
dyaur jyotsnā āśiṣaḥ svastir vyāptir māyā uṣā śivā //
137.d:
अहंशक्तिर् अथौषध्यः श्रुतिः शुद्धिर् विभावरी
द्यौर् ज्योत्स्ना आशिषः स्वस्तिर् व्याप्तिर् माया उषा शिवा ॥
137.m: the power of selfhood, plants, sacred tradition, purity, night, / the sky, moonlight, blessings, well-being, pervasive power, illusory power, dawn, and the auspicious Śivā—

137.s:
yat kiṃcid vidyate loke lakṣmyā vyāptaṃ carācaram
brāhmaṇeṣv atha dhīreṣu kṣamāvatsv atha sādhuṣu //
137.d:
यत् किंचिद् विद्यते लोके लक्ष्म्या व्याप्तं चराचरम्
ब्राह्मणेष्व् अथ धीरेषु क्षमावत्स्व् अथ साधुषु ॥
137.m: whatever moving and unmoving exists in the world is pervaded by Lakṣmī. / Among brāhmaṇas, the steadfast, the forbearing, the virtuous,

137.s:
vidyāyukteṣu cānyeṣu bhuktimuktyanusāriṣu
yad yad ramyaṃ sundaraṃ vā tat tal lakṣmīvijṛmbhitam //
137.d:
विद्यायुक्तेषु चान्येषु भुक्तिमुक्त्यनुसारिषु
यद् यद् रम्यं सुन्दरं वा तत् तल् लक्ष्मीविजृम्भितम् ॥
137.m: those endowed with knowledge, and others pursuing enjoyment and liberation: / whatever is pleasant or beautiful, all that is a manifestation of Lakṣmī.

137.s:
kim atra bahunoktena sarvaṃ lakṣmīmayaṃ jagat
yasmin kasmiṃś ca yat kiṃcid utkṛṣṭaṃ paridṛśyate //
137.d:
किम् अत्र बहुनोक्तेन सर्वं लक्ष्मीमयं जगत्
यस्मिन् कस्मिंश् च यत् किंचिद् उत्कृष्टं परिदृश्यते ॥
137.m: What need is there of saying much on this matter? The whole world consists of Lakṣmī. / In whomsoever and in whatsoever something exalted is seen,

137.s:
lakṣmīmayaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ tayā hīnaṃ na kiṃcana
atremāṃ sundarīṃ devīṃ spardhayantī na lajjase //
137.d:
लक्ष्मीमयं तु तत् सर्वं तया हीनं न किंचन
अत्रेमां सुन्दरीं देवीं स्पर्धयन्ती न लज्जसे ॥
137.m: all that consists of Lakṣmī; nothing is devoid of her. / Are you not ashamed here to vie with this beautiful goddess?

137.s:
gaccha gaccheti tāṃ gaṅgā daridrāṃ vākyam abravīt
tataḥ prabhṛti gaṅgāmbho daridrāvairakāry abhūt //
137.d:
गच्छ गच्छेति तां गङ्गा दरिद्रां वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
ततः प्रभृति गङ्गाम्भो दरिद्रावैरकार्य् अभूत् ॥
137.m: "Begone! Begone!" Gaṅgā said to Daridrā. / From that time on, the water of the Gaṅgā became an enemy to poverty.

137.s:
tāvad daridrābhibhavo gaṅgā yāvan na sevyate
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham alakṣmīnāśanaṃ śubham //
137.d:
तावद् दरिद्राभिभवो गङ्गा यावन् न सेव्यते
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् अलक्ष्मीनाशनं शुभम् ॥
137.m: The humiliation by Daridrā lasts only as long as Gaṅgā is not resorted to. / From that time on, that sacred bath became auspicious, destroying misfortune.

137.s:
tatra snānena dānena lakṣmīvān puṇyavān bhavet
tīrthānāṃ ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi tasmiṃs tīrthe mahāmate
devarṣimunijuṣṭānāṃ sarvasiddhipradāyinām //
137.d:
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन लक्ष्मीवान् पुण्यवान् भवेत्
तीर्थानां षट् सहस्राणि तस्मिंस् तीर्थे महामते
देवर्षिमुनिजुष्टानां सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायिनाम् ॥
137.m: By bathing and giving gifts there, one becomes prosperous and virtuous. / There are six thousand sacred baths at that tīrtha, O noble-minded one, / resorted to by divine seers and sages, bestowing all accomplishments.

138.s:
brahmovāca
bhānutīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvasiddhikaraṃ nṛṇām
tatredaṃ vṛttam ākhyāsye mahāpātakanāśanam //
138.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
भानुतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं सर्वसिद्धिकरं नृणाम्
तत्रेदं वृत्तम् आख्यास्ये महापातकनाशनम् ॥
138.m: Brahmā said: / There is [a place] known as Bhānutīrtha, bestowing all accomplishments on men. / In that connection, I will relate this event that destroys great sins.

138.s:
śaryātir iti vikhyāto rājā paramadhārmikaḥ
tasya bhāryā sthaviṣṭheti rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi //
138.d:
शर्यातिर् इति विख्यातो राजा परमधार्मिकः
तस्य भार्या स्थविष्ठेति रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि ॥
138.m: There was a king well known as Śaryāti, supremely devoted to dharma; / his wife, Sthaviṣṭhā, was peerless in beauty on earth.

138.s:
madhucchandā iti khyāto vaiśvāmitro dvijottamaḥ
purodhās tasya nṛpater brahmarṣiḥ śamināṃ prabhuḥ //
138.d:
मधुच्छन्दा इति ख्यातो वैश्वामित्रो द्विजोत्तमः
पुरोधास् तस्य नृपतेर् ब्रह्मर्षिः शमिनां प्रभुः ॥
138.m: A best of twice-born men known as Madhucchandas, of the lineage of Viśvāmitra, / was the royal priest of that king, a brahmanical sage, a master among the self-controlled.

138.s:
diśo vijetuṃ sa jagāma rājā
purodhasā tena nṛpapravīraḥ
purodhasaṃ prāha mahānubhāvaṃ
jitvā diśaś cādhvani saṃniviṣṭaḥ
138.d:
दिशो विजेतुं स जगाम राजा
पुरोधसा तेन नृपप्रवीरः
पुरोधसं प्राह महानुभावं
जित्वा दिशश् चाध्वनि संनिविष्टः
138.m: That king, a hero among kings, set out to conquer the quarters / with that royal priest. / Having conquered the quarters and encamped upon the road, / he spoke to the high-minded royal priest:

138.s:
papracchedaṃ kena khedaṃ gato 'si
hetuṃ vadasveti mahānubhāva
tvam eva rājye mama sarvamānyaḥ
samastavidyāniravadyabodhaḥ
138.d:
पप्रच्छेदं केन खेदं गतो ऽसि
हेतुं वदस्वेति महानुभाव
त्वम् एव राज्ये मम सर्वमान्यः
समस्तविद्यानिरवद्यबोधः
138.m: He asked this: “Why have you fallen into sorrow? / State the cause, O highly distinguished one! / You alone are universally honoured in my kingdom, / your understanding of all branches of learning flawless.

138.s:
vidhūtapāpaḥ paritāpaśūnyaḥ
kim anyacetā iva lakṣyase tvam
jiteyam urvī vijitā narendrā
harṣasya hetau mahatīha jāte
138.d:
विधूतपापः परितापशून्यः
किम् अन्यचेता इव लक्ष्यसे त्वम्
जितेयम् उर्वी विजिता नरेन्द्रा
हर्षस्य हेतौ महतीह जाते
138.m: Your sins shaken off, free of anguish, / why do you appear as if your mind were elsewhere? / This earth has been conquered, kings subdued; / when a great reason for joy has arisen here,

138.s:
kiṃ tvaṃ kṛśo me vada satyam eva
dvijātivaryātimahānubhāva
saṃbodhya śaryātim uvāca vipraś
chandomadhuḥ premamayīṃ priyoktim
138.d:
किं त्वं कृशो मे वद सत्यम् एव
द्विजातिवर्यातिमहानुभाव
संबोध्य शर्यातिम् उवाच विप्रश्
छन्दोमधुः प्रेममयीं प्रियोक्तिम्
138.m: why are you emaciated? Tell me truly, / O best of the twice-born, of exceedingly great majesty!” / Addressing Śaryāti, the brahmin / Madhucchandas spoke loving, affectionate words:

138.s:
madhucchandā uvāca
śṛṇu bhūpāla madvākyaṃ bhāryayā yad udīritam
sthite yāme vayaṃ yāmo yāminī cārdhagāminī //
138.d:
मधुच्छन्दा उवाच
शृणु भूपाल मद्वाक्यं भार्यया यद् उदीरितम्
स्थिते यामे वयं यामो यामिनी चार्धगामिनी ॥
138.m: Madhucchandas said: / “Listen, O protector of the earth, to what was said by my wife: / ‘A watch remaining, we depart, and the night is half-gone.

138.s:
svāminī cāsya dehasya kāminī māṃ pratīkṣate
smṛtvā tat kāminīvākyaṃ śoṣaṃ yāti kalevaram
vikāre smarasaṃjāte jīvātur nalinānanā //
138.d:
स्वामिनी चास्य देहस्य कामिनी मां प्रतीक्षते
स्मृत्वा तत् कामिनीवाक्यं शोषं याति कलेवरम्
विकारे स्मरसंजाते जीवातुर् नलिनानना ॥
138.m: The mistress of this body, my loving wife awaits me.’ / Remembering that loving woman’s words, my body withers away. / When love's affliction arises, that lotus-faced woman is my elixir of life.”

138.s:
brahmovāca
vihasya cābravīd rājā purodhasam ariṃdamaḥ //
138.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
विहस्य चाब्रवीद् राजा पुरोधसम् अरिंदमः ॥
138.m: Brahmā said: / Smiling, the king, tamer of his foes, spoke to his royal priest:

138.s:
rājovāca
tvaṃ gurur mama mitraṃ ca kim ātmānaṃ viḍambase
kim anena mahāprājña mama vākyena mānada
kṣaṇavidhvaṃsini sukhe kā nāmāsthā mahātmanām //
138.d:
राजोवाच
त्वं गुरुर् मम मित्रं च किम् आत्मानं विडम्बसे
किम् अनेन महाप्राज्ञ मम वाक्येन मानद
क्षणविध्वंसिनि सुखे का नामास्था महात्मनाम् ॥
138.m: The king said: / “You are my guru and my friend; why do you mock yourself? / What is the use of this, O very wise one, with my words, O giver of honour? / What confidence indeed do the great-souled have in pleasure that vanishes in an instant?”

138.s:
brahmovāca
etad ākarṇya matimān madhucchandā vaco 'bravīt //
138.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतद् आकर्ण्य मतिमान् मधुच्छन्दा वचो ऽब्रवीत् ॥
138.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing this, the wise Madhucchandas spoke [these] words:

138.s:
madhucchandā uvāca
yatrānukūlyaṃ daṃpatyos trivargas tatra vardhate
na cedaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ rājan bhūṣaṇaṃ cātimanyatām //
138.d:
मधुच्छन्दा उवाच
यत्रानुकूल्यं दंपत्योस् त्रिवर्गस् तत्र वर्धते
न चेदं दूषणं राजन् भूषणं चातिमन्यताम् ॥
138.m: Madhucchandas said: / “Where there is harmony between husband and wife, there the threefold aim of life flourishes. / Nor is this a fault, O king; consider it an ornament!”

138.s:
brahmovāca
ājagāma svakaṃ deśaṃ mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ
parīkṣārthaṃ ca tatprema puryāṃ vārttām adīdiśat //
138.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
आजगाम स्वकं देशं महत्या सेनया वृतः
परीक्षार्थं च तत्प्रेम पुर्यां वार्त्ताम् अदीदिशत् ॥
138.m: Brahmā said: / Surrounded by a large army, he arrived at his own land; / and in order to test that love, he sent a report into the city:

138.s:
diśo vijetuṃ śaryātau yāte rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ
hatvā rasātalaṃ yāto rājānaṃ sapurodhasam //
138.d:
दिशो विजेतुं शर्यातौ याते राक्षसपुंगवः
हत्वा रसातलं यातो राजानं सपुरोधसम् ॥
138.m: “While Śaryāti went to conquer the quarters, a foremost Rākṣasa / killed the king along with his royal priest and departed to the netherworld.”

138.s:
rājño bhāryā niścayāya pravṛttā munisattama
vārttāṃ śrutvā dūtamukhān madhucchandaḥpriyā punaḥ //
138.d:
राज्ञो भार्या निश्चयाय प्रवृत्ता मुनिसत्तम
वार्त्तां श्रुत्वा दूतमुखान् मधुच्छन्दःप्रिया पुनः ॥
138.m: The king’s wives set out to ascertain [the truth], O best of sages; / but hearing the news from the messenger's mouth, Madhucchandas’s beloved,

138.s:
tadaivābhūd gataprāṇā tad vicitram ivābhavat
tasyā vṛttaṃ tu te dṛṣṭvā dūtā rājñe nyavedayan //
138.d:
तदैवाभूद् गतप्राणा तद् विचित्रम् इवाभवत्
तस्या वृत्तं तु ते दृष्ट्वा दूता राज्ञे न्यवेदयन् ॥
138.m: instantly lost her life. That was truly extraordinary. / Seeing what had happened to her, the messengers reported to the king

138.s:
yat kṛtaṃ rājapatnībhiḥ priyayā ca purodhasaḥ
vismito duḥkhito rājā punar dūtān abhāṣata //
138.d:
यत् कृतं राजपत्नीभिः प्रियया च पुरोधसः
विस्मितो दुःखितो राजा पुनर् दूतान् अभाषत ॥
138.m: what had been done by the king’s wives and by the priest’s beloved. / Astonished and distressed, the king spoke again to the messengers:

138.s:
rājovāca
śīghraṃ gacchantu he dūtā brāhmaṇyā yat kalevaram
rakṣantu vārttāṃ kuruta rājāgantā purodhasā //
138.d:
राजोवाच
शीघ्रं गच्छन्तु हे दूता ब्राह्मण्या यत् कलेवरम्
रक्षन्तु वार्त्तां कुरुत राजागन्ता पुरोधसा ॥
138.m: The king said: / “Go swiftly, O messengers! Guard the body / of the brahmin woman and announce: ‘The king is coming with his royal priest!’”

138.s:
brahmovāca
iti cintāture rājñi vāg uvācāśarīriṇī //
138.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इति चिन्तातुरे राज्ञि वाग् उवाचाशरीरिणी ॥
138.m: Brahmā said: / While the king was thus overwhelmed with anxiety, a bodiless voice spoke:

138.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
vidhāsyaty akhilaṃ gaṅgā rājaṃs tava samīhitam
sarvābhiṣaṅgaśamanī pāvanī bhuvi gautamī //
138.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
विधास्यत्य् अखिलं गङ्गा राजंस् तव समीहितम्
सर्वाभिषङ्गशमनी पावनी भुवि गौतमी ॥
138.m: The voice from the sky said: / “The Gaṅgā will accomplish all that you desire, O king— / the Gautamī, who allays all attachment and purifies the earth.”

138.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā sa śaryātir gautamītaṭam āśritaḥ
brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṃ dattvā tarpayitvā pitṝn dvijān //
138.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा स शर्यातिर् गौतमीतटम् आश्रितः
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं दत्त्वा तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् द्विजान् ॥
138.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing this, Śaryāti resorted to the bank of the Gautamī. / Giving wealth to brahmins and propitiating the ancestors and the twice-born,

138.s:
purohitaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ preṣayitvā dhanānvitam
anyatra tīrthe sārtheṣu dānaṃ dehi prayatnataḥ //
138.d:
पुरोहितं द्विजश्रेष्ठं प्रेषयित्वा धनान्वितम्
अन्यत्र तीर्थे सार्थेषु दानं देहि प्रयत्नतः ॥
138.m: he sent away the royal priest, the best of the twice-born, endowed with wealth: / “Distribute gifts with effort in another sacred place, among caravans!”

138.s:
etat sarvaṃ na jānāti rājñaḥ kṛtyaṃ purohitaḥ
gate tasmin gurau rājā vaiśvāmitre mahātmani //
138.d:
एतत् सर्वं न जानाति राज्ञः कृत्यं पुरोहितः
गते तस्मिन् गुरौ राजा वैश्वामित्रे महात्मनि ॥
138.m: The royal priest knew nothing of all this, the king’s intention. / When that guru, the great-souled descendant of Viśvāmitra, had departed,

138.s:
sarvaṃ balaṃ preṣayitvā gaṅgātīre 'gnim āviśat
ity uktvā sa tu rājendro gaṅgāṃ bhānuṃ surān api //
138.d:
सर्वं बलं प्रेषयित्वा गङ्गातीरे ऽग्निम् आविशत्
इत्य् उक्त्वा स तु राजेन्द्रो गङ्गां भानुं सुरान् अपि ॥
138.m: the king dismissed all his forces and entered the fire on the bank of the Gaṅgā. / Having thus addressed the Gaṅgā, the sun, and the gods:

138.s:
yadi dattaṃ yadi hutaṃ yadi trātā prajā mayā
tena satyena sā sādhvī mamāyuṣyeṇa jīvatu //
138.d:
यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं यदि त्राता प्रजा मया
तेन सत्येन सा साध्वी ममायुष्येण जीवतु ॥
138.m: “If I have given gifts, if I have offered oblations, if the subjects have been protected by me, / by that truth, may that virtuous woman live, at the cost of my life!”

138.s:
ity uktvāgnau praviṣṭe tu śaryātau nṛpasattame
tadaiva jīvitā bhāryā rājñas tasya purodhasaḥ //
138.d:
इत्य् उक्त्वाग्नौ प्रविष्टे तु शर्यातौ नृपसत्तमे
तदैव जीविता भार्या राज्ञस् तस्य पुरोधसः ॥
138.m: Having spoken thus, when Śaryāti, the best of kings, entered the fire, / at that very moment the wife of the king's royal priest was brought back to life.

138.s:
agnipraviṣṭaṃ rājānaṃ śrutvā vismayakāraṇam
pativratāṃ tathā bhāryāṃ mṛtāṃ jīvānvitāṃ punaḥ //
138.d:
अग्निप्रविष्टं राजानं श्रुत्वा विस्मयकारणम्
पतिव्रतां तथा भार्यां मृतां जीवान्वितां पुनः ॥
138.m: Hearing that the king had entered the fire—a cause for amazement— / and likewise that his devoted wife, having died, was again endowed with life,

138.s:
tadarthaṃ cāpi rājānaṃ tyaktātmānaṃ viśeṣataḥ
ātmanaś ca punaḥ kṛtyam asmaran nṛpater guruḥ //
138.d:
तदर्थं चापि राजानं त्यक्तात्मानं विशेषतः
आत्मनश् च पुनः कृत्यम् अस्मरन् नृपतेर् गुरुः ॥
138.m: and especially that the king had cast off his own life for her sake, / the king’s guru, considering his own duty:

138.s:
aham apy agnim āvekṣya uta yāsye priyāntikam
athaveha tapas tapsye tato niścayavān dvijaḥ //
138.d:
अहम् अप्य् अग्निम् आवेक्ष्य उत यास्ये प्रियान्तिकम्
अथवेह तपस् तप्स्ये ततो निश्चयवान् द्विजः ॥
138.m: “Shall I too enter the fire, or shall I go to my beloved? / Or shall I perform tapas here?” Then the twice-born made his decision:

138.s:
etad evātmanaḥ kṛtyaṃ manye sukṛtam eva ca
jīvayāmi ca rājānaṃ tato yāmi priyāṃ punaḥ //
138.d:
एतद् एवात्मनः कृत्यं मन्ये सुकृतम् एव च
जीवयामि च राजानं ततो यामि प्रियां पुनः ॥
138.m: “I consider this alone my duty and a righteous deed: / I shall bring the king to life, and then I will return to my beloved.

138.s:
etad eva śubhaṃ me syāt tatas tuṣṭāva bhāskaram
na hy anyaḥ kopi devo 'sti sarvābhīṣṭaprado raveḥ //
138.d:
एतद् एव शुभं मे स्यात् ततस् तुष्टाव भास्करम्
न ह्य् अन्यः कोपि देवो ऽस्ति सर्वाभीष्टप्रदो रवेः ॥
138.m: This alone will be auspicious for me.” Thereupon he praised the sun, / for there is no other god who grants all desires than the sun.

138.s:
madhucchandā uvāca
namo 'stu tasmai sūryāya muktaye 'mitatejase
chandomayāya devāya oṃkārārthāya te namaḥ //
138.d:
मधुच्छन्दा उवाच
नमो ऽस्तु तस्मै सूर्याय मुक्तये ऽमिततेजसे
छन्दोमयाय देवाय ओंकारार्थाय ते नमः ॥
138.m: Madhucchandas said: / “Homage to that Sūrya of immeasurable splendour, [source of] liberation; / to the god composed of Vedic metres, to the meaning of the syllable Oṃ, homage to you!

138.s:
virūpāya surūpāya triguṇāya trimūrtaye
sthityutpattivināśānāṃ hetave prabhaviṣṇave //
138.d:
विरूपाय सुरूपाय त्रिगुणाय त्रिमूर्तये
स्थित्युत्पत्तिविनाशानां हेतवे प्रभविष्णवे ॥
138.m: To the multiform, to the beautifully formed, to the three-stranded, to the three-formed, / to the cause of maintenance, creation, and destruction, the mighty lord!”

138.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prasannaḥ sūryo 'bhūd varayasvety abhāṣata //
138.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्रसन्नः सूर्यो ऽभूद् वरयस्वेत्य् अभाषत ॥
138.m: Brahmā said: / Then Sūrya was pleased and spoke: “Choose a boon!”

138.s:
madhucchandā uvāca
rājānaṃ dehi deveśa bhāryāṃ ca priyavādinīm
ātmanaś ca śubhān putrān rājñaś caiva śubhān varān //
138.d:
मधुच्छन्दा उवाच
राजानं देहि देवेश भार्यां च प्रियवादिनीम्
आत्मनश् च शुभान् पुत्रान् राज्ञश् चैव शुभान् वरान् ॥
138.m: Madhucchandas said: / “Grant me the king, O lord of gods, and my sweet-speaking wife, / auspicious sons for myself, and auspicious boons for the king!”

138.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prādāj jagannāthaḥ śaryātiṃ ratnabhūṣitam
tāṃ ca bhāryāṃ varān anyān sarvaṃ kṣemamayaṃ tathā //
138.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्रादाज् जगन्नाथः शर्यातिं रत्नभूषितम्
तां च भार्यां वरान् अन्यान् सर्वं क्षेममयं तथा ॥
138.m: Brahmā said: / Then the lord of the universe granted Śaryāti adorned with jewels, / and that wife, and other boons, and everything filled with well-being.

138.s:
tato yātaḥ priyāviṣṭaḥ prītena ca purodhasā
yayau sukhī svakaṃ deśaṃ tat tu tīrthaṃ śubhaṃ smṛtam //
138.d:
ततो यातः प्रियाविष्टः प्रीतेन च पुरोधसा
ययौ सुखी स्वकं देशं तत् तु तीर्थं शुभं स्मृतम् ॥
138.m: Then, reunited with his beloved, along with the pleased royal priest, / he happily went to his own realm. That sacred place is remembered as auspicious.

138.s:
tatra trīṇi sahasrāṇi tīrthāni guṇavanti ca
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ bhānutīrtham udāhṛtam //
138.d:
तत्र त्रीणि सहस्राणि तीर्थानि गुणवन्ति च
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं भानुतीर्थम् उदाहृतम् ॥
138.m: There are three thousand meritorious sacred places there. / From that time forward, that sacred place was called Bhānutīrtha,

138.s:
mṛtasaṃjīvanaṃ caiva śāryātaṃ ceti viśrutam
mādhucchandasamākhyātaṃ smaraṇāt pāpanun mune //
138.d:
मृतसंजीवनं चैव शार्यातं चेति विश्रुतम्
माधुच्छन्दसमाख्यातं स्मरणात् पापनुन् मुने ॥
138.m: and renowned as Mṛtasaṃjīvana and Śāryāta; / it is celebrated as Mādhucchandasa, destroying sin by its remembrance, O sage.

138.s:
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca sarvakratuphalapradam
mṛtasaṃjīvanaṃ tat syād āyurārogyavardhanam //
138.d:
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च सर्वक्रतुफलप्रदम्
मृतसंजीवनं तत् स्याद् आयुरारोग्यवर्धनम् ॥
138.m: Bathing and giving gifts at those places yields the fruit of all sacrifices; / it brings the dead to life and increases life and health.

139.s:
brahmovāca
khaḍgatīrtham iti khyātaṃ gautamyā uttare taṭe
tatra snānena dānena muktibhāgī bhaven naraḥ //
139.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
खड्गतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं गौतम्या उत्तरे तटे
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन मुक्तिभागी भवेन् नरः ॥
139.m: Brahmā said: / Khaḍgatīrtha is renowned on the northern bank of the Gautamī; / by bathing and giving gifts there, a person partakes of liberation.

139.s:
tatra vṛttaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada yatnataḥ
pailūṣa iti vikhyātaḥ kavaṣasya suto dvijaḥ //
139.d:
तत्र वृत्तं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद यत्नतः
पैलूष इति विख्यातः कवषस्य सुतो द्विजः ॥
139.m: I shall relate the event that occurred there; listen carefully, O Nārada: / A twice-born man renowned as Pailūṣa was the son of Kavaṣa.

139.s:
kuṭumbabhārāt parito hy arthārthī paridhāvati
na kimapy āsasādāsau tato vairāgyam āsthitaḥ //
139.d:
कुटुम्बभारात् परितो ह्य् अर्थार्थी परिधावति
न किमप्य् आससादासौ ततो वैराग्यम् आस्थितः ॥
139.m: Because of the burden of family, he ran all about seeking wealth, / but he obtained nothing at all; then he resorted to dispassion.

139.s:
atyantavimukhe daive vyarthībhūte tu pauruṣe
na vairāgyād anyad asti paṇḍitasyāvalambanam //
139.d:
अत्यन्तविमुखे दैवे व्यर्थीभूते तु पौरुषे
न वैराग्याद् अन्यद् अस्ति पण्डितस्यावलम्बनम् ॥
139.m: When fate is utterly adverse and human effort has proved vain, / there is no other recourse for a wise man than dispassion.

139.s:
iti saṃcintayām āsa tadāsau niḥśvasan muhuḥ
kramāgataṃ dhanaṃ nāsti poṣyāś ca bahavo mama //
139.d:
इति संचिन्तयाम् आस तदासौ निःश्वसन् मुहुः
क्रमागतं धनं नास्ति पोष्याश् च बहवो मम ॥
139.m:
He then reflected thus, sighing again and again:
"I have no inherited wealth, and I have many dependents to feed.

139.s:
mānī cātmā na kaṣṭārho hā dhig durdaivaceṣṭitam
sa kadācid vṛttiyuto vṛttibhiḥ parivartayan //
139.d:
मानी चात्मा न कष्टार्हो हा धिग् दुर्दैवचेष्टितम्
स कदाचिद् वृत्तियुतो वृत्तिभिः परिवर्तयन् ॥
139.m:
I have my pride and am unfit for hard labour. Alas, fie upon the working of bad fate!"
At one time, possessed of an occupation and shifting through various livelihoods,

139.s:
na lebhe tad dhanaṃ vṛtter virāgam agamat tadā
sevā niṣiddhā yā kācid gahanā duṣkaraṃ tapaḥ //
139.d:
न लेभे तद् धनं वृत्तेर् विरागम् अगमत् तदा
सेवा निषिद्धा या काचिद् गहना दुष्करं तपः ॥
139.m:
he could not obtain that wealth from his occupation, and then he became detached:
"Any service is forbidden and painful; ascetic penance is hard to perform.

139.s:
balād ākarṣatīyaṃ māṃ tṛṣṇā sarvatra duṣkṛte
tvayāpakṛtam ajñānāt tasmāt tṛṣṇe namo 'stu te //
139.d:
बलाद् आकर्षतीयं मां तृष्णा सर्वत्र दुष्कृते
त्वयापकृतम् अज्ञानात् तस्मात् तृष्णे नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
139.m:
This craving forcibly drags me everywhere into wrongdoing.
Wrong has been done by you through ignorance; therefore, O craving, homage to you!"

139.s:
evaṃ vicintya medhāvī tṛṣṇāchedāya kiṃ bhavet
ity ālocya sa pailūṣaḥ pitaraṃ vākyam abravīt //
139.d:
एवं विचिन्त्य मेधावी तृष्णाछेदाय किं भवेत्
इत्य् आलोच्य स पैलूषः पितरं वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
139.m:
Having reflected thus, the wise Pailūṣa, considering what might cut off craving,
spoke these words to his father:

139.s:
pailūṣa uvāca
jñānāsinā krodhalobhau saṃsṛtiṃ cātidustarām
chedmīmāṃ kena he tāta tam upāyaṃ vada prabho //
139.d:
पैलूष उवाच
ज्ञानासिना क्रोधलोभौ संसृतिं चातिदुस्तराम्
छेद्मीमां केन हे तात तम् उपायं वद प्रभो ॥
139.m:
Pailūṣa said:
With what can I cut off with the sword of knowledge these two, anger and greed, and this worldly cycle that is so hard to cross?
O father, O lord, tell me the means!

139.s:
kavaṣa uvāca
īśvarāj jñānam anvicched ity eṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ
tasmād ārādhayeśānaṃ tato jñānam avāpsyasi //
139.d:
कवष उवाच
ईश्वराज् ज्ञानम् अन्विच्छेद् इत्य् एषा वैदिकी श्रुतिः
तस्माद् आराधयेशानं ततो ज्ञानम् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
139.m:
Kavaṣa said:
"One should seek knowledge from the Lord"—such is the Vedic revelation.
Therefore, worship Īśāna; from that you will obtain knowledge.

139.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā sa pailūṣo jñānāyeśvaram ārcayat
tatas tuṣṭo maheśāno jñānaṃ prādād dvijātaye
prāptajñāno mahābuddhir gāthāḥ provāca muktidāḥ //
139.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा स पैलूषो ज्ञानायेश्वरम् आर्चयत्
ततस् तुष्टो महेशानो ज्ञानं प्रादाद् द्विजातये
प्राप्तज्ञानो महाबुद्धिर् गाथाः प्रोवाच मुक्तिदाः ॥
139.m:
Brahmā said:
Saying "So be it," Pailūṣa worshipped the Lord for knowledge.
Then, Maheśāna, pleased, gave knowledge to the twice-born.
Having obtained knowledge, of great intellect, he spoke verses that bestow liberation:

139.s:
pailūṣa uvāca
krodhas tu prathamaṃ śatrur niṣphalo dehanāśanaḥ
jñānakhaḍgena taṃ chittvā paramaṃ sukham āpnuyāt //
139.d:
पैलूष उवाच
क्रोधस् तु प्रथमं शत्रुर् निष्फलो देहनाशनः
ज्ञानखड्गेन तं छित्त्वा परमं सुखम् आप्नुयात् ॥
139.m:
Pailūṣa said:
Anger is the first enemy, fruitless and destroying the body.
Having cut it down with the sword of knowledge, one may attain supreme happiness.

139.s:
tṛṣṇā bahuvidhā māyā bandhanī pāpakāriṇī
chittvaitāṃ jñānakhaḍgena sukhaṃ tiṣṭhati mānavaḥ //
139.d:
तृष्णा बहुविधा माया बन्धनी पापकारिणी
छित्त्वैतां ज्ञानखड्गेन सुखं तिष्ठति मानवः ॥
139.m:
Craving is manifold illusory power, binding and causing sin.
Having cut it down with the sword of knowledge, a man abides in happiness.

139.s:
saṅgas tu paramo 'dharmo devādīnām iti śrutiḥ
asaṅgasyātmano hy asya saṅgo 'yaṃ paramo ripuḥ //
139.d:
सङ्गस् तु परमो ऽधर्मो देवादीनाम् इति श्रुतिः
असङ्गस्यात्मनो ह्य् अस्य सङ्गो ऽयं परमो रिपुः ॥
139.m:
Attachment is the supreme unrighteousness, even for gods and the rest—so says the scripture.
For this unattached self, this attachment is indeed the greatest enemy.

139.s:
chittvainaṃ jñānakhaḍgena śivaikatvam avāpnuyāt
saṃśayaḥ paramo nāśo dharmārthānāṃ vināśakṛt //
139.d:
छित्त्वैनं ज्ञानखड्गेन शिवैकत्वम् अवाप्नुयात्
संशयः परमो नाशो धर्मार्थानां विनाशकृत् ॥
139.m:
Having cut it down with the sword of knowledge, one attains oneness with Śiva.
Doubt is the greatest ruin, destroying dharma and worldly goods.

139.s:
chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ jantuḥ paramepsitam āpnuyāt
piśācīva viśaty āśā nirdahaty akhilaṃ sukham
pūrṇāhantāsinā chittvā jīvan muktim avāpnuyāt //
